  • Math me index aksar 1 se n; Python/PyTorch me 0 se n−1. range(1, 5) me 5 shaamil nahi.
  • Cross-entropy me double sum aata hai: Σsamples Σclasses — andar wala pehle (Ch 11).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Σ = kirana bill ka total. ∏ = sabka guna.

2.15 Mean, Variance, Standard deviation — average aur "kitna bikhra hua"

Kahani

Do classes ka average 50 marks hai. Class A me sabke 48 se 52 ke beech aaye. Class B me aadhe bachchon ke 0 aur aadhe ke 100. Average same, par dono classes bilkul alag hain! Average (mean) "beech" batata hai, aur variance / standard deviation batata hai ki numbers beech se kitna bikhre hue hain.

μ = 1n Σ xi    σ² = 1n Σ (xi − μ)²    s² = 1n − 1 Σ (xi − x̄)²    σ = √σ²
  • μ (mu) = mean = sabka jod ÷ ginti
  • (xi − μ) = har number ki mean se doori (deviation). Square isliye ki + aur − cancel na hon
  • σ² = population variance (1/n): jab poora data tumhare paas ho
  • s² = sample variance (1/(n−1), "Bessel's correction"): jab data badi population ka chhota sample ho. Mean bhi isi sample se nikala, to deviations thode chhote aate hain; n−1 se bhaag dekar wo kami poori karte hain (unbiased estimate)
  • σ = standard deviation = √variance — wapas original units me (marks², nahi marks)

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: data = [2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9]. Mean, dono variance, dono std nikalo.

  1. n = 8, Σ = 2+4+4+4+5+5+7+9 = 40, μ = 40/8 = 5
  2. Deviations: −3, −1, −1, −1, 0, 0, 2, 4
  3. Squares: 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16 → Σ = 32
  4. Population: σ² = 32/8 = 4, σ = √4 = 2
  5. Sample: s² = 32/7 ≈ 4.5714, s = √4.5714 ≈ 2.1381
  6. Bonus z-score (1.8 wala StandardScaler): 9 ka (9 − 5)/2 = 2 → "9 mean se 2 standard deviation upar hai".

Jawab: μ = 5; population σ² = 4, σ = 2; sample s² ≈ 4.5714, s ≈ 2.1381.

NumPy vs PyTorch · default ALAG hai (coding trap!)

import numpy as np
marks = [2., 4., 4., 4., 5., 5., 7., 9.]
a = np.array(marks)
t = torch.tensor(marks)

print(np.mean(a), np.var(a), np.std(a))       # numpy default: 1/n (population)
print(np.var(a, ddof=1), np.std(a, ddof=1))   # ddof=1 -> 1/(n-1)
print(t.mean(), t.var(), t.std())             # torch default: 1/(n-1) (sample)!
print(t.var(unbiased=False), t.std(unbiased=False))   # torch me 1/n (naya naam: correction=0)

Output

5.0 4.0 2.0
4.571428571428571 2.138089935299395
tensor(5.) tensor(4.5714) tensor(2.1381)
tensor(4.) tensor(2.)

Exam Radar

  • Population variance ÷ n; sample variance ÷ (n − 1).
  • np.var/np.std default = population (ddof=0); torch.var/torch.std default = sample (unbiased, n−1). StandardScaler population std use karta hai.
  • BatchNorm (Ch 20) training me batch ka mean aur biased (1/n) variance use karke normalize karta hai.
  • Weight init (Ch 21) poora variance ka khel hai: Xavier Var(W) = 2/(nin + nout), He Var(W) = 2/nin.

Galti mat karna

  • Variance ko std samajh lena. Std = √variance. Variance 4 → std 2.
  • Deviations ka seedha jod (bina square) — wo hamesha 0 aata hai! (−3−1−1−1+0+0+2+4 = 0)

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Mean = beech. Std = beech se aam taur pe kitni doori. Sample me n−1, numpy n, torch n−1.

2.16 Normal (Gaussian) aur Uniform distribution — weights kahan se aate hain

Kahani

College ke saare students ki height naapo. Zyada tar log average (lagbhag 5'6") ke aas paas, kuch thode chhote, kuch thode lambe, aur bahut kam log bahut chhote ya bahut lambe. Graph banao to ghante (bell) jaisi shape banti hai — ye normal distribution.

Ab Ludo ka paasa phenko: 1 se 6, sab ki chance barabar. Graph ekdum flat — ye uniform distribution.

Neural network banate waqt shuru me weights random rakhte hain — ya to bell curve se nikaal ke, ya flat range se. Isiliye ye dono jaanna zaroori hai (Chapter 21).

Normal 𝒩(μ, σ²):   p(x) = 1σ√2π e−(x − μ)² / (2σ²)     Uniform U(a, b):   p(x) = 1b − a
  • μ = beech (peak yahan), σ = chaudai (σ bada → bell chaudi aur neechi). 𝒩(0, 1) = standard normal
  • e−(x−μ)²/(2σ²) = beech se door jaate hi tezi se girta hai (2.7 wala e−x); aage wala 1/(σ√2π) bas area ko 1 banata hai
  • 𝒩(0,1) ka peak: 1/√(2π) ≈ 0.3989
  • 68–95–99.7 rule: μ ± 1σ me ≈ 68.27%, ± 2σ me ≈ 95.45%, ± 3σ me ≈ 99.73% data
  • Uniform U(a, b): a se b tak har value barabar; mean = (a+b)/2, variance = (b−a)²/12

Chalo numbers se samjhein

  1. U(−1, 1): height 1/(1 − (−1)) = 1/2 = 0.5; mean (−1 + 1)/2 = 0; variance (1 − (−1))²/12 = 4/12 ≈ 0.3333
  2. Xavier uniform (Ch 21) preview: U(−a, a) with a = √(6/(n_in + n_out)). nin = 3, nout = 2: a = √(6/5) ≈ 1.0954, variance a²/3 = 1.2/3 = 0.4 = 2/(3+2) ✓
  3. Heights ~ 𝒩(165 cm, 10²): 68% log 155 se 175 cm ke beech, 95% log 145 se 185 cm ke beech.

PyTorch · randn = normal, rand = uniform [0, 1)

torch.manual_seed(0)                      # har baar same random numbers
z = torch.randn(100000)                   # N(0, 1) se 1 lakh numbers
print(z.mean(), z.std())                  # ~0 aur ~1
print(((z > -1) & (z < 1)).float().mean(), ((z > -2) & (z < 2)).float().mean())  # ~68%, ~95%

u = torch.rand(100000) * 2 - 1            # [0,1) ko [-1,1) me khinch ke khiskaya: a + (b-a)*rand
print(u.min(), u.max(), u.mean(), u.var())   # var ~ 1/3

h = 5 + 2 * torch.randn(100000)           # mu + sigma * randn  ->  N(5, 2^2)
print(h.mean(), h.std())

Output

tensor(-0.0024) tensor(1.0012)
tensor(0.6811) tensor(0.9547)
tensor(-1.0000) tensor(1.0000) tensor(0.0027) tensor(0.3342)
tensor(4.9919) tensor(2.0003)

Exam Radar

  • torch.randn → standard normal 𝒩(0, 1). torch.rand → uniform [0, 1). torch.randint(low, high, size) → integers, high exclusive.
  • 𝒩(μ, σ²) banane ke liye: μ + σ·randn. U(a, b): a + (b−a)·rand.
  • 68–95–99.7 rule. Uniform variance = (b−a)²/12.
  • Init functions: nn.init.normal_, nn.init.uniform_, xavier_uniform_, kaiming_normal_ (He) — Ch 21.

Galti mat karna

  • rand aur randn me confusion: "n" = normal. rand ke numbers kabhi negative nahi; randn ke ho sakte hain.
  • 𝒩(0, 0.01) me 0.01 variance hai (std 0.1). Kai jagah σ likhte hain, kai jagah σ² — dhyaan se padho.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Normal = heights ki ghanti (randn). Uniform = Ludo ka paasa (rand).

2.17 Probability ki basics — toss, baarish, aur Bernoulli coin

Kahani

Cricket match ka toss: heads ki chance 1/2. Do matches me dono baar heads? 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4 — kyunki ek toss doosre ko affect nahi karta. Ab baarish: kisi bhi din baarish ki chance kam hai, par agar aasmaan me kaale baadal hain to chance kaafi badh jaati hai. "Agar … diya hua hai to" — ye conditional probability hai. Classifier bhi yahi bolta hai: "agar is patient ke ye 30 features hain, to malignant hone ki probability 0.83".

0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1    Σ P(sab outcomes) = 1    P(not A) = 1 − P(A)    P(A and B) = P(A)·P(B) [independent]    P(A | B) = P(A and B)P(B)
  • P = probability: 0 = kabhi nahi, 1 = pakka
  • Saare possible outcomes ki probabilities ka jod hamesha 1 (softmax output isi liye jod ke 1 hota hai)
  • Independent events (ek doosre pe asar nahi) → probabilities guna. Yahi data likelihood ka product hai (Ch 11)
  • P(A | B) = "B ho chuka hai, to A ki probability" — B ki duniya me A ka hissa. ML me P(y | x) = input diya hua hai, label ki probability

Chalo numbers se samjhein

  1. Do paase, dono pe 6: 1/6 × 1/6 = 1/36 ≈ 0.0278
  2. 100 din: 30 din baadal, unme se 20 din baarish. P(baarish | baadal) = 20/30 ≈ 0.6667. Formula se: P(baarish and baadal) = 0.20, P(baadal) = 0.30 → 0.20/0.30 ≈ 0.6667 ✓
  3. Softmax output [0.1, 0.7, 0.2]: 0.1 + 0.7 + 0.2 = 1 ✓ — valid probability distribution.

Bernoulli — ek sikka, do nateeje

Jis experiment ke sirf do nateeje hon (1 ya 0: heads/tails, malignant/benign, pass/fail) use Bernoulli trial kehte hain. P(y = 1) = p, to P(y = 0) = 1 − p. Dono ko ek hi formula me likhne ka jugaad:

P(y) = py (1 − p)1 − y,    y ∈ {0, 1}
  • y = 1 rakho: p1(1−p)0 = p ✓. y = 0 rakho: p0(1−p)1 = 1 − p ✓ (kyunki kuch bhi0 = 1)
  • Log lo: ln P(y) = y ln p + (1−y) ln(1−p). Iske aage minus lagao → Binary Cross-Entropy ka ek term! (Lab 5 ka BCE formula yahi hai)

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: model har sample ko p = 0.8 deta hai. Asli labels [1, 1, 0]. Likelihood, log-likelihood, aur average negative log-likelihood?

  1. Har sample: P(1) = 0.8, P(1) = 0.8, P(0) = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2
  2. Independent → guna: 0.8 × 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.128 (likelihood)
  3. Log: 2 ln 0.8 + ln 0.2 = 2(−0.2231) + (−1.6094) = −2.0557 = ln 0.128 ✓
  4. Average NLL: 2.0557 / 3 ≈ 0.6852

Jawab: likelihood 0.128, log-likelihood −2.0557, average NLL ≈ 0.6852 — aur nn.BCELoss bhi exactly yahi deta hai.

PyTorch · BCE = average negative log-likelihood (Ch 11 preview)

bce = nn.BCELoss()                              # Lab 5 wala loss
p = torch.tensor([0.8, 0.8, 0.8])               # model ki P(y=1)
y = torch.tensor([1., 1., 0.])                  # asli labels
print(bce(p, y))                                # mean of -[y ln p + (1-y) ln(1-p)]

Output

tensor(0.6852)

Exam Radar

  • Probabilities 0 se 1; saare outcomes ka jod 1; independent → guna; P(A|B) = P(A∩B)/P(B).
  • Binary classifier ka output = P(y = 1 | x). Bernoulli: py(1−p)1−y.
  • Maximize likelihood ⇔ minimize negative log-likelihood ⇔ minimize cross-entropy (Ch 11).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Toss guna hote hain, log unhe jodta hai, minus lagao to loss ban jaata hai.

2.18 max vs argmax — "sabse zyada kitna" vs "sabse zyada kaun"

Kahani

Result board pe do sawaal: "Highest marks kitne aaye?" → 98. Ye max (value). "Topper kaun hai?" → roll number 7. Ye argmax (position / kaun). Ek value deta hai, doosra uska pata (index).

maxi xi = sabse badi value     argmaxi xi = wo index i jahan sabse badi value hai
  • "arg" = argument = input/position. argmax = "kis input pe max milta hai"
  • Python/PyTorch me index 0 se shuru hota hai
  • Classification ka final answer = probabilities (ya raw scores) ka argmax

Chalo numbers se samjhein

  1. p = [0.1, 0.7, 0.2] → max = 0.7, argmax = 1 (0-based: position 0 pe 0.1, position 1 pe 0.7)
  2. Raw scores (logits) [1.0, 3.0, 2.0] → softmax [0.0900, 0.6652, 0.2447]. argmax dono ka 1 — softmax order nahi badalta (monotonic), isliye prediction ke liye softmax lagana zaroori nahi.
  3. Tie: [3, 7, 7, 1] → argmax = 1 (pehli wali 7).

PyTorch · max aur argmax (dim wala khel Ch 3.18 me)

pp = torch.tensor([0.1, 0.7, 0.2])
print(torch.max(pp), torch.argmax(pp))          # value vs index

logits = torch.tensor([1.0, 3.0, 2.0])
print(torch.softmax(logits, dim=0), torch.argmax(logits), torch.argmax(torch.softmax(logits, dim=0)))
print(torch.argmax(torch.tensor([3, 7, 7, 1])))  # tie: pehla index

Output

tensor(0.7000) tensor(1)
tensor([0.0900, 0.6652, 0.2447]) tensor(1) tensor(1)
tensor(1)

Exam Radar

  • max → value, argmax → index. Multi-class prediction = argmax(dim=1) over class scores (Ch 3.18).
  • argmax(softmax(z)) = argmax(z).
  • argmax differentiable nahi (chhota badlav → index ya to same ya jump) — isliye training softmax + cross-entropy se hoti hai, argmax sirf prediction/accuracy ke liye.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

max = "kitne marks?", argmax = "topper kaun?".

Python + PyTorch ki grammar — code padhna aur likhna seekho

Variables · List · Dict · Loops · if · Functions · Classes & super().__init__() · import · f-string · with · lambda · NumPy · Tensors (Lab 0) · dtype · Broadcasting · @ vs * · dim · view/reshape · Indexing · cat/stack · NumPy↔Torch · Device · requires_grad

Exam ka 30% coding hai, aur saare labs PyTorch me hain. Lekin PyTorch Python ke upar bana hai — jaise Hindi me chitthi likhne se pehle matra aur vyakaran aana chahiye. Is chapter ke pehle hisse (3.1–3.12) me Python ka utna hi vyakaran jitna DL code me dikhta hai, aur doosre hisse (3.13–3.24) me tensors — bilkul Lab 0 ki tarah. Har code chala ke asli output chipkaya hai.

3.1 Variables, types aur operators — Python ki ABCD

Kahani

Maa ki rasoi me dabbe hain, har dabbe pe parchi lagi hai: "cheeni", "chai patti", "namak". Dabbe ke andar cheez = value, parchi = variable ka naam. Python me lr = 0.1 likhne ka matlab: ek dabba banao, us pe parchi "lr" lagao, andar 0.1 rakh do. Dabba kis type ka hai (number, text, haan/na), Python khud samajh leta hai.

TypeKya haiExampleDL me kahan
intpoora numberepochs = 25epochs, batch_size, neurons
floatdashamlav wala numberlr = 0.1learning rate, loss value
strtext"cuda"device naam, column naam
boolTrue / Falseshuffle=Trueflags
None"kuch nahi"best_model = Noneabhi value nahi

Python · types aur operators

age = 20                 # int: poora number
lr = 0.1                 # float: dashamlav wala number
name = "Riya"            # str: text (quotes me)
is_training = True       # bool: True / False (capital T/F)
best_model = None        # None: "abhi kuch nahi hai"
print(type(age), type(lr), type(name), type(is_training), type(best_model))

print(7 / 2, 7 // 2, 7 % 2, 2 ** 3)   # divide, floor-divide, remainder, POWER
print(2 ^ 3)                          # ^ = XOR, power nahi!

Output

<class 'int'> <class 'float'> <class 'str'> <class 'bool'> <class 'NoneType'>
3.5 3 1 8
1

Operators dhyaan se: / hamesha float deta hai (7/2 = 3.5). // = floor division (neeche round: 7//2 = 3). % = remainder (7%2 = 1). ** = power (2**3 = 8). Aur ^ power NAHI hai — ye bitwise XOR hai: 2 = 010, 3 = 011, XOR = 001 = 1. Lab 0 me t1*(2^3) likha tha aur output bilkul t1 jaisa aaya — kyunki 2^3 = 1, to t1×1 = t1!

Python ka sabse bada niyam: indentation (4 spaces) hi block hai. for, if, def, class ke baad colon : aur andar wali lines 4 space aage. Brackets nahi, spaces. # ke baad sab comment.

Exam Radar

  • 2 ** 3 = 8 (power), 2 ^ 3 = 1 (XOR). Lab 0 trap.
  • 7 / 2 = 3.5, 7 // 2 = 3, 7 % 2 = 1.
  • True/False/None capital letter se. Galat indentation → IndentationError.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Variable = parchi wala dabba. Power = do sitare **, ek topi ^ nahi.

3.2 List — numbers ki line, ginti 0 se

Kahani

Building ka ground floor "0" hota hai, pehli manzil "1". Python me list ki ginti bhi 0 se: pehla element index 0 pe. Aur peeche se ginna ho to −1 = aakhri, −2 = second last — jaise lift me "top floor" button.

List [ ] me kuch bhi rakh sakte ho, aur baad me badal sakte ho (mutable). Slicing list[start:stop:step]: start shaamil, stop shaamil NAHI. Khaali chhodo to: start = shuru, stop = end, step = 1.

Python · indexing, slicing, append, len

losses = [0.67, 0.54, 0.46, 0.40]   # Lab 5 jaise epoch-wise losses
print(losses[0], losses[-1])        # pehla, aakhri (negative = peeche se)
print(losses[1:3])                  # index 1 se shuru, 3 se PEHLE ruk jao
print(losses[:2], losses[2:], losses[::2])   # shuru se 2 tak, 2 se end tak, har doosra
losses.append(0.36)                 # end me naya element
print(len(losses), losses)
losses[0] = 0.70                    # list badal sakti hai (mutable)
print(losses)

Output

0.67 0.4
[0.54, 0.46]
[0.67, 0.54] [0.46, 0.4] [0.67, 0.46]
5 [0.67, 0.54, 0.46, 0.4, 0.36]
[0.7, 0.54, 0.46, 0.4, 0.36]

Lab 5 me exactly yahi tha: train_losses = [] (khaali list), fir har epoch train_losses.append(loss.item()), aur end me plt.plot(range(1, epochs + 1), train_losses). Network ka architecture bhi list me rakh sakte ho: layers = [30, 16, 8, 1].

Exam Radar

  • x[1:3] → index 1 aur 2 (3 nahi). x[-1] → aakhri. len(x) → kitne elements.
  • Yahi slicing rules tensors pe bhi (3.20).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Ground floor = 0. Slice ka stop = darwaza, andar nahi aata.

3.3 Dictionary — naam se dhoondho, position se nahi

Kahani

Phone ki contact list: tum "Mummy" dhoondhte ho, number mil jaata hai. "Contact number 37" koi nahi dhoondhta. Dictionary = key → value ki jodiyan. Key se value nikalo.

Python · dict

params = {"lr": 0.1, "epochs": 25, "optimizer": "SGD"}   # key: value
print(params["lr"])                     # key se value nikalo
params["batch_size"] = 32               # naya key-value jodo
print(params.get("dropout", 0.0))       # key nahi hai? default 0.0 do (error nahi)
for key, value in params.items():       # saare jode ek ek karke
    print(key, "->", value)
print(list(params.keys()))

Output

0.1
0.0
lr -> 0.1
epochs -> 25
optimizer -> SGD
batch_size -> 32
['lr', 'epochs', 'optimizer', 'batch_size']

DL me dict har jagah: hyperparameter config, Optuna ka study.best_params (Ch 22) ek dict hai jaise {'lr': 0.003, 'n_layers': 2}, aur model.state_dict() = layer ke naam → weights tensor ka dict (model save karne ke liye).

Exam Radar

  • Missing key pe d["x"] → KeyError; d.get("x", default) safe hai.
  • .items() → (key, value) jodiyan, loop me sabse common.

3.4 Loops — for, range, enumerate, zip, break

Kahani

Class me teacher attendance leti hain: roll number 1, 2, 3 … ek ek karke, har ek ke saath same kaam ("present?"). Ye for loop hai. Training loop bhi yahi hai: epoch 1, 2, 3 … har baar same kaam (forward, loss, backward, step).

Python · for, range, enumerate, zip, break

for epoch in range(3):                  # 0, 1, 2  (3 shaamil nahi)
    print("epoch", epoch + 1)
print(list(range(1, 6)), list(range(0, 10, 3)))   # (start, stop) aur (start, stop, step)

items = ["chai", "samosa", "biscuit"]
for i, item in enumerate(items):        # index + value dono ek saath
    print(i, item)

prices = [10, 15, 5]
for item, price in zip(items, prices):  # do lists ko jodi me chalao
    print(item, price)

for epoch in range(100):                # break = loop beech me tod do
    if epoch == 2:                      # (early stopping me yahi hota hai, Ch 19)
        print("ruk gaye at", epoch)
        break

2 biscuit
chai 10
samosa 15
biscuit 5
ruk gaye at 2
  • range(n) → 0 se n−1. range(a, b) → a se b−1. range(a, b, s) → s ke kadam.
  • enumerate(x) → (index, value). Training me: for i, (xb, yb) in enumerate(loader): — batch number bhi chahiye to.
  • zip(a, b) → dono lists ke elements jodi me. Raju ka MSE (1.3) isi se nikla.
  • break → loop turant band (early stopping). continue → is round ka baaki chhodo, agla round.
  • Lab 5 ka dil: for epoch in range(epochs):. Mini-batch me nested loop: for epoch in range(epochs): ke andar for xb, yb in loader: (Ch 14).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

range(3) = 0, 1, 2. Teen baar, par 3 kabhi nahi.

3.5 if / elif / else — traffic signal wala faisla

Kahani

Signal laal → ruko. Warna agar peela → dheere. Warna → chalo. Upar se neeche check hota hai, jo pehli condition sach mili, wahi block chalta hai, baaki skip.

Python · if / elif / else

acc = 0.85
if acc >= 0.9:
    print("Excellent")
elif acc >= 0.7:                        # pehli condition fail hui to ye check
    print("Theek hai")
else:                                   # koi bhi sach nahi to ye
    print("Aur train karo")

gpu_available = False
device = "cuda" if gpu_available else "cpu"   # ek line wala if-else
print(device)
print(3 == 3.0, 3 != 4, (acc > 0.5) and (acc < 0.9), not True)

Output

Theek hai
cpu
True True True False

Ek line wala if-else (conditional expression) — A if condition else B — exactly wahi pattern hai jo har lab me device chunne ke liye aata hai: torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'). Comparisons: == (barabar? — ek = assignment hai!), !=, <, >=; jodne ke liye and, or, not. None check: if best_model is None:.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Laal → peela → hara: pehli sach condition jeet-ti hai.

3.6 Functions — def, return, default arguments

Kahani

Maa ki recipe card: "Input: chawal, paani. Process: 20 min pakao. Output: bhaat." Ek baar card likh do, roz use karo. Function bhi wahi: naam do (def), inputs lo (parameters), kaam karo, jawab wapas do (return).

Python · def, default args, multiple return

def predict(x, w, b=0.0):               # b ka DEFAULT 0.0 hai
    return w * x + b                    # return = function ka jawab

print(predict(10, -2, 100))             # positional: order se
print(predict(10, -2))                  # b nahi diya -> default 0.0
print(predict(x=10, w=-2, b=100))       # keyword: naam se (order matter nahi)

def stats(values):
    m = sum(values) / len(values)
    return m, max(values)               # do cheezein = ek tuple

mean_v, max_v = stats([2, 4, 9])        # unpacking: dono alag variables me
print(mean_v, max_v)

Output

80
-20.0
80
5.0 9
  • Default argument (b=0.0): na do to default. PyTorch me har jagah: nn.Linear(in, out, bias=True), DataLoader(..., shuffle=False) default.
  • Keyword argument: naam se pass karo (lr=0.1) — order ki tension khatam. Positional pehle, keyword baad me.
  • Multiple return: Lab 1 me return output, hidden_values aur call pe probs, hidden_values = hidden_layer_xor_forward(X).
  • return na likha to function None deta hai. Optuna ka objective(trial) (Ch 22) ek number (accuracy/loss) return karta hai.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

def = recipe card. return = plate me khana.

3.7 Classes — class, __init__, self, methods, inheritance, super().__init__()

Kahani

Raju ki chai stall itni chali ki usne franchise shuru ki. Usne ek naksha (blueprint) banaya: har stall me ek owner hoga, ek rate hoga, aur "cups bike" ka register hoga; har stall chai bech sakta hai. Is naksha = class. Naksha se bane asli stalls (Raju ka, Shyam ka) = objects (instances). Har stall ka data apna — Raju ke 5 cup bike to Shyam ke register pe asar nahi.

Jab naya stall khulta hai, ek "opening ceremony" hoti hai jisme owner ka naam, rate set hota hai aur khaali register rakha jaata hai — ye __init__ hai. Stall ke andar har kaam me "mera register, mera rate" bolna padta hai — wo "mera" = self.

Fir Meena ne Masala-chai franchise li. Usko basic stall ki saari cheezein chahiye (owner, rate, register, bechna), plus masala. Wo naksha dobara nahi likhti — basic naksha inherit karti hai. Aur opening ceremony me pehle basic franchise ka standard setup karwati hai (counter, register) — ye super().__init__() hai — fir apni masala wali cheez jodti hai. Agar standard setup bhool gayi, to register hi nahi bana, aur pehli bikri pe hi gadbad!

Definition

class = naksha; object / instance = naksha se bani asli cheez. attribute = object ka data (self.price). method = class ke andar ka function, jiska pehla parameter hamesha self (wo object khud). __init__ = constructor, object bante hi apne aap chalta hai. Inheritance = class Child(Parent): → parent ki saari attributes/methods child ko milti hain; child unhe override (naya version) kar sakta hai. super() = parent class tak pahunchne ka raasta; super().__init__(...) = parent ka constructor chalao.

Python · class, __init__, self, method

class ChaiStall:                                  # blueprint (naksha)
    def __init__(self, owner, price=10):          # constructor: object bante hi chalta hai
        self.owner = owner                        # attribute: is object ki apni cheez
        self.price = price
        self.cups_sold = 0

    def sell(self, n):                            # method: object ka kaam
        self.cups_sold += n                       # apni hi attribute badli
        return n * self.price

raju = ChaiStall("Raju")                          # object (instance) #1
shyam = ChaiStall("Shyam", price=12)              # object #2, alag data
print(raju.sell(5), shyam.sell(5))                # same method, alag jawab
print(raju.cups_sold, raju.owner, shyam.price)

Output

50 60
5 Raju 12

Dhyaan do: raju.sell(5) likhte hain, par method ki definition def sell(self, n) hai. Python khud raju ko self ki jagah bhej deta hai: raju.sell(5) = ChaiStall.sell(raju, 5).

Python · inheritance, super().__init__(), override — aur bhoolne ka nateeja

class MasalaChaiStall(ChaiStall):                 # ChaiStall se INHERIT
    def __init__(self, owner, price=15, masala="elaichi"):
        super().__init__(owner, price)            # pehle parent ka __init__ chalao!
        self.masala = masala                      # fir apni nayi attribute

    def sell(self, n):                            # method OVERRIDE (naya version)
        bill = super().sell(n)                    # parent wala sell bhi use karo
        return bill + 2 * n                       # +2 rupaye masala per cup

m = MasalaChaiStall("Meena")
print(m.sell(4), m.cups_sold, m.masala, m.owner)

class Broken(ChaiStall):
    def __init__(self, owner):
        self.masala = "adrak"                     # super().__init__() BHOOL GAYE

b = Broken("Bunty")
print(b.masala)
try:
    print(b.cups_sold)                            # parent ka setup chala hi nahi
except AttributeError as e:
    print("AttributeError:", e)

Output

68 4 elaichi Meena
adrak
AttributeError: 'Broken' object has no attribute 'cups_sold'

Broken ne apna __init__ likha par parent ka nahi chalaya, to self.cups_sold = 0 wali line kabhi chali hi nahi — register bana hi nahi. Child me __init__ likho to parent ka __init__ khud bulana padta hai.

Ab asli maal: har PyTorch model ek class hai

Lab 5 ka MySimpleNN dekho — ab har line samajh aayegi. class MySimpleNN(nn.Module) = nn.Module (PyTorch ka "basic franchise") se inherit. super().__init__() = nn.Module ka setup chalao — ye andar parameters aur sub-modules ka "register" banata hai. Uske baad self.linear = nn.Linear(...) likhne pe nn.Module chupke se is layer ko register me likh leta hai, aur isi register se model.parameters() saare weights dhoondh ke optimizer ko deta hai. Lab 5 ke words: "MUST be called first — registers the module machinery".

Aur model(x) kaise forward chala deta hai? Python me agar class me __call__ method ho, to object ko function ki tarah bula sakte ho. nn.Module ka __call__ pehle hooks waghera chalata hai, fir tumhara forward. Chhota sa demo:

Python · __call__ ka jaadu (nn.Module isi tarah forward chalata hai)

class MiniModule:
    def __call__(self, x):              # object ko function ki tarah call karo to ye chalta hai
        print("(pehle hooks/checks)")
        return self.forward(x)          # ...fir forward

class Doubler(MiniModule):
    def forward(self, x):
        return 2 * x

d = Doubler()
print(d(21))                            # d(21) -> d.__call__(21) -> d.forward(21)

Output

(pehle hooks/checks)
42

PyTorch · Lab 5 ka MySimpleNN — aur super() bhoolne ka asli error

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class MySimpleNN(nn.Module):                      # Lab 5: nn.Module se inherit
    def __init__(self, num_features):
        super().__init__()                        # nn.Module ki machinery ON (parameter tracking)
        self.linear = nn.Linear(num_features, 1)  # sub-module: weights apne aap register
        self.sigmoid = nn.Sigmoid()

    def forward(self, features):                  # computation yahan likho
        out = self.linear(features)               # (N, 30) -> (N, 1)
        out = self.sigmoid(out)                   # probability (0, 1)
        return out

model = MySimpleNN(30)
print(model)
x = torch.randn(4, 30)                            # 4 patients
print(model(x).shape)                             # model(x), model.forward(x) nahi
print(sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())) # 30 weights + 1 bias

class Oops(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        self.linear = nn.Linear(2, 1)             # super().__init__() bhool gaye
try:
    Oops()
except AttributeError as e:
    print("AttributeError:", e)

Output

MySimpleNN(
  (linear): Linear(in_features=30, out_features=1, bias=True)
  (sigmoid): Sigmoid()
)
torch.Size([4, 1])
31
AttributeError: cannot assign module before Module.__init__() call

Exam Radar

  • Har model: class Net(nn.Module) → __init__ me pehli line super().__init__() → layers self.xxx = ... me → forward(self, x) me computation → return.
  • Bhool gaye to: AttributeError: cannot assign module before Module.__init__() call.
  • Call model(x), model.forward(x) nahi (hooks skip ho jaate). Method ka naam exactly forward.
  • print(model) layers dikhata hai; model.parameters() sirf self. pe rakhi layers ke weights deta hai.

Galti mat karna

  • Method me self bhool jaana: def forward(x): → call pe TypeError: forward() takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given.
  • Layer forward ke andar banana (nn.Linear(30, 1)(x)) — har call pe naye random weights, kuch seekha hi nahi jaayega, aur optimizer ko dikhenge bhi nahi. Layers hamesha __init__ me.
  • __init__ ki spelling: do underscore aage, do peeche. __int__ likha to constructor chalega hi nahi.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Class = franchise ka naksha, object = asli stall, self = "mera", super().__init__() = "pehle head-office ka setup, fir mera masala".

3.8 import, from … import, as — toolbox kholna

Kahani

Papa ka toolbox: poora box utha lao (import torch) aur har baar bolo "box se pench-kas". Ya sirf pench-kas nikaal lo (from … import …). Aur lamba naam? Nickname rakh do — jaise "Rajesh" ko "Raju" (as).

Python · course ke standard imports

import torch                                   # poora package, naam se use: torch.zeros
import torch.nn as nn                          # lamba naam -> chhota nickname "nn"
import torch.optim as optim
import torch.nn.functional as F
import numpy as np
from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader   # package se sirf ye do cheezein
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

print(nn.Linear is torch.nn.Linear)            # same cheez, bas chhota naam
print(F.relu(torch.tensor([-1.0, 2.0])))       # F = functional version

Output

True
tensor([0., 2.])

Ye wahi imports hain jo poore notebook ke code me chalenge. nn = layers aur losses (classes: nn.ReLU()), F = wahi cheezein function ki tarah (F.relu(x)), optim = optimizers (SGD, Adam), DataLoader = batches (Ch 14).

3.9 f-strings — print me values ghusana

String ke aage f lagao, aur { } ke andar koi bhi variable/expression likho — wo value ban ke chhap jaayega. Format bhi: {x:.4f} = 4 decimal, {n:02d} = 2 digit (aage zero), {a:.2%} = percent.

Python · Lab 5 ka print, aur formatting

epoch, loss = 3, 0.4555133879184723
print(f'Epoch: {epoch + 1}, Loss: {loss}')                # Lab 5 style: {} me koi bhi expression
print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1:02d} | loss {loss:.4f} | acc {0.9825:.2%}")   # format: 2 digit, 4 decimal, percent
print("Epoch", epoch + 1, "Loss", round(loss, 4))         # bina f-string wala tareeka

Output

Epoch: 4, Loss: 0.4555133879184723
Epoch 04 | loss 0.4555 | acc 98.25%
Epoch 4 Loss 0.4555

3.10 with block — "kaam khatam, safai apne aap" (aage torch.no_grad())

Kahani

Library se kitaab li. Niyam: block me padho, block khatam hote hi kitaab apne aap wapas — chahe beech me phone aa jaaye (error). with yahi guarantee deta hai: block me ghuste waqt setup, nikalte waqt cleanup. Isko context manager kehte hain.

Python + PyTorch · with open, with torch.no_grad()

with open("notes.txt", "w") as fh:      # file kholi, naam fh
    fh.write("DL ka exam kal hai!\n")
print(fh.closed)                        # block khatam -> file apne aap band (error aaye tab bhi)

x = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)
with torch.no_grad():                   # is block ke andar gradient tracking BAND
    y = x * 3
print(y.requires_grad)                  # False: koi graph nahi bana
z = x * 3                               # block ke bahar: tracking wapas ON
print(z.requires_grad)

Output

True
False
True

Lab 5 evaluation: with torch.no_grad(): ke andar model chalaya, kyunki test pe gradient nahi chahiye — graph banana memory aur time ki barbaadi hai. Block ke bahar tracking apne aap wapas ON. (Ye model.eval() se alag cheez hai — wo dropout/BatchNorm ka mode badalta hai, Ch 20. Evaluation me dono lagte hain.)

Exam Radar

  • with torch.no_grad(): → andar ke operations ka graph nahi banta, requires_grad=False results. Evaluation/inference ke liye.
  • Lab 5 pitfall: evaluation me no_grad bhoolna → bekaar memory/compute.

3.11 lambda aur list comprehension — ek-line ke jugaad

lambda = chhota, bina naam ka function: lambda v: v ** 2 = "v do, v² lo". Jahan ek chhota function argument me dena ho (sorting key, LambdaLR scheduler Ch 15, transforms.Lambda). List comprehension = loop + list ek line me: [f(v) for v in items if condition]. Agar square brackets hata do aur seedha sum(...) me daal do, to wo generator expression hai — list banaye bina ek ek value deta hai. Parameter ginne ka famous one-liner yahi hai.

Python · lambda, comprehension, parameter count

square = lambda v: v ** 2                         # chhota, bina naam ka function
print(square(5))

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print([v ** 2 for v in nums])                     # list comprehension: har v ka square
print([v for v in nums if v % 2 == 0])            # filter ke saath: sirf even

model = nn.Linear(30, 1)
print(sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())) # generator expression: 30 + 1
print(sorted(["relu", "elu", "tanh"], key=lambda s: len(s)))   # lambda as "key"

Output

25
[1, 4, 9, 16, 25]
[2, 4]
31
['elu', 'relu', 'tanh']

Sirf trainable parameters ginne hon to: sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad).

3.12 NumPy minimum — PyTorch ka bada bhai

Kahani

NumPy pehle aaya, PyTorch baad me — aur PyTorch ne NumPy ki bhasha lagbhag copy ki. pandas, sklearn (Lab 5 ka StandardScaler, train_test_split) sab NumPy arrays dete hain. To data ka safar hota hai: CSV → pandas → NumPy → PyTorch tensor.

NumPy · array, shape, dtype, dot, broadcasting, astype

import numpy as np
a = np.array([1.5, 2.0, 3.0])
print(a.shape, a.dtype)                  # float64 = numpy ka default float!
b = np.array([1, 2, 3])
print(b.dtype)                           # int64
M = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
print(M.shape, M.ndim)
print(np.dot([1, 2], [3, 4]), M @ np.ones(3))      # dot product, matrix @ vector
print(M + 10)                            # broadcasting: scalar har element me
print(M + np.array([100, 200, 300]))     # (2,3) + (3,): har row me same vector
print(a.astype(np.float32).dtype)        # Lab 5 wali trick: float32 me badlo

Output

(3,) float64
int64
(2, 3) 2
11 [ 6. 15.]
[[11 12 13]
 [14 15 16]]
[[101 202 303]

float32

Exam Radar

  • NumPy ka default float = float64, PyTorch ka = float32. Isi farak se Lab 5 ka "Double vs Float" error aata hai (3.15).
  • np.array, .shape, .ndim, .dtype, np.dot, @, .astype(np.float32) — tensors me inke bhai: torch.tensor, .shape, .dim(), .dtype, torch.dot, @, .to(torch.float32).

3.13 Tensor kya hai — NumPy array + do superpowers

Kahani

Tensor ko NumPy array ka "superhero" version samjho. Shakal same (numbers ka dabba, shape, dtype), par do shaktiyaan extra: (1) GPU pe daud sakta hai (Lab 0: 29 guna tez), aur (2) apna itihaas yaad rakh sakta hai — kis operation se bana — taaki derivative apne aap nikal sake (autograd, 3.24). Deep learning me data, weights, gradients, loss — sab tensor hain.

Chapter 2.1 wali dimensions yaad karo, ab DL ke asli examples ke saath. Images ke liye PyTorch ka order fix hai: (N, C, H, W) = (batch me kitni photos, channels, height, width). "Channels first". Grayscale (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST) me C = 1, colour (CIFAR-10, ImageNet) me C = 3 (Red, Green, Blue).

PyTorch · 0-D se 4-D tak

loss = torch.tensor(0.6703)               # 0-D: ek number
bias = torch.zeros(16)                    # 1-D: 16 neurons ke bias
X_batch = torch.randn(455, 30)            # 2-D: (samples, features) - Lab 5
img = torch.rand(3, 32, 32)               # 3-D: (C, H, W) - ek colour photo (CIFAR-10)
mnist_batch = torch.rand(64, 1, 28, 28)   # 4-D: (N, C, H, W) - 64 grayscale digits
for t in [loss, bias, X_batch, img, mnist_batch]:
    print(t.dim(), tuple(t.shape))

Output

0 ()
1 (16,)
2 (455, 30)
3 (3, 32, 32)
4 (64, 1, 28, 28)

Exam Radar

  • PyTorch image format: (N, C, H, W). Ek photo (C, H, W) = 3-D; model ko dene se pehle batch dim jodo → (1, C, H, W) (3.19).
  • MNIST/Fashion-MNIST: 1 × 28 × 28; CIFAR-10: 3 × 32 × 32. Tabular (Lab 5): (N, features).
  • t.dim() = t.ndim = number of dimensions.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Tensor = NumPy + GPU + yaaddasht. Photos ka order: N-C-H-W = Number (kitni photos), Channels, Height, Width.

3.14 Tensor banana — Lab 0 ki poori list

FunctionKya banata haiYaad rakhne wali baat
torch.tensor(data)list/array se tensordtype data se: ints → int64, decimals → float32. Data copy hota hai

Isiliye labs me SEED = 42, torch.manual_seed(SEED) likhte hain — taaki har baar same weights se shuru ho aur results compare ho sakein.
