torch.autograd.grad(output, input) ek tuple return karta hai (isliye [0]); ye .grad me jama nahi karta, seedha gradient de deta hai. Lab ki shart thi: derivative formula khud mat likho, autograd se nikalo. Tests: sigmoid(0) → (0.5, 0.25), tanh(0) → (0.0, 1.0).

Tanh ke fayde

  • Zero-centered (−1, 1): outputs + aur − dono → zig-zag kam, sigmoid se behtar gradient flow
  • Center par steeper: max derivative 1 (sigmoid 0.25)
  • Smooth, differentiable

Nuksaan

  • Still vanishing gradient: bade |z| par saturate (sigmoid se bhi tez)
  • exp() ka cost

Kahan use hota hai: RNN aur LSTM ke hidden states (cell output), purane shallow networks. Modern deep feed-forward/CNN hidden layers me ReLU family ne jagah le li.

Exam Radar

  • tanh range (−1, 1), tanh(0) = 0, zero-centered.
  • tanh′(z) = 1 − tanh2(z), max 1 at z = 0.
  • tanh(z) = 2σ(2z) − 1; tanh′(z) = 4σ′(2z).
  • Sigmoid′ aur tanh′ cross at z ≈ 1.663; usse aage tanh′ chhota.
  • Tanh vanishing gradient fix NAHI karta (S-shape problem). Lecture slide: "same problem as Sigmoid but less severe" (center pe slope 4 guna). Worksheet 03 ka table: "saturates faster than sigmoid, so vanishing gradient is worse". Dono apni jagah sach: |z| < 1.663 pe tanh better, tails me tanh worse. MCQ me context dekho.
  • Code: torch.tanh(x), nn.Tanh().

Galti mat karna

  • Tanh zero-centered hai, isse vanishing gradient solve nahi hota — do alag problems hain. Zero-centering zig-zag theek karta hai, saturation ko nahi.
  • tanh(z) = 2σ(2z) − 1 me "2z" bhoolna common hai; 2σ(z) − 1 galat hai (check: 2σ(1) − 1 = 0.4621 = tanh(0.5), tanh(1) nahi).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Tanh = sigmoid ka "−1 se +1" wala bada bhai: zero pe khada, chot 1 tak, par S-shape ki bimari (saturation) wahi.

9.6 ReLU — modern default

Kahani

Ghar ki paani ki tanki ke pipe me ek one-way valve laga hai. Pressure ulta (negative) ho to valve band — paani zero. Pressure seedha (positive) ho to jitna pressure, utna paani — seedha proportional. Na koi limit, na koi "atakna". Ye valve hai ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit). "Rectify" ka matlab hi hai ulta current rokna — jaise electronics me rectifier.

ReLU(z) = max(0, z) = z  agar z > 0,    0  agar z ≤ 0
ReLU′(z) = 1  agar z > 0,    0  agar z < 0,    z = 0 par undefined (PyTorch 0 leta hai)
  • Range [0, ∞) — 0 included (bracket), upar koi limit nahi (unbounded). ReLU(0) = 0.
  • z > 0 par function z hai, jiska slope 1. z < 0 par function 0 (constant), slope 0.
  • z = 0 par corner (kink): left slope 0, right slope 1 — dono alag, isliye derivative exist nahi karta. Libraries convention se 0 le leti hain.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — wahi saturated sawaal, ab ReLU ke saath (worksheet 03, Part 4.3)

Sawaal: x = 1, w = 6, b = 0, y = 0, α = 1 (sigmoid ke saath step sirf 0.00246 tha).

  1. z = 6,  ŷ = max(0, 6) = 6
  2. Error: 6 − 0 = 6
  3. Derivative: f′(6) = 1
  4. Gradient: 6 × 1 × 1 = 6
  5. Update: wnew = 6 − 1 × 6 = 0
  6. Check: z = 0, ŷ = 0, error = 0

Jawab: ek hi step me error exactly zero! Step ratio ReLU/sigmoid = 6/0.00246041 ≈ 2439.

Honest note (worksheet ka): do cheezein badli. Error ≈1 se 6 hua (kyunki ReLU unbounded hai) — ≈6 guna. Derivative 0.0025 se 1 hua — ≈405 guna (1/σ′(6) = 405.43). Asli hero derivative hai.

ReLU ke fayde

  • No vanishing gradient for z > 0: derivative exactly 1, gradients bina chhote hue peeche jaate hain → bahut deep networks train ho paate hain. AlexNet paper (2012) ne dikhaya ki ek 4-layer CNN ReLU ke saath CIFAR-10 pe 25% training error tak tanh wale same network se 6 guna tez pahuncha — isi liye AlexNet ne ReLU chuna (Chapter 24).
  • Cheap: sirf ek comparison, max(0, z). Koi exp() nahi. Derivative bhi bas "positive hai ya nahi".
  • Sparsity: z ≤ 0 wale neurons exactly 0 output dete hain. Random init par lagbhag aadhe neurons kisi bhi input par "off" rehte hain → sparse representation, kam computation, thoda regularization jaisa effect.

ReLU ke nuksaan

  • Dying ReLU (neeche detail me).
  • Not zero-centered: outputs ≥ 0, to sigmoid wala zig-zag argument yahan bhi lagta hai.
  • Unbounded: output ki koi upper limit nahi. ReLU(6) = 6 koi "decision" nahi hai, isliye classification ki final layer me ReLU nahi chalega (worksheet 4.2). Final layer me sigmoid/softmax. (Regression me agar target kabhi negative nahi ho sakta, jaise price, to output pe ReLU chal sakta hai.)
  • z = 0 par non-differentiable — practically koi dikkat nahi, convention 0.

PyTorch · ReLU paanch tareeke + autograd

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

z = torch.tensor([-3.0, -0.5, 0.0, 0.5, 3.0], requires_grad=True)

r1 = torch.relu(z)              # functional (torch namespace)
r2 = F.relu(z)                  # functional (F namespace) - same cheez
r3 = nn.ReLU()(z)               # layer
r4 = torch.clamp(z, min=0)      # scratch: 0 se neeche wale ko 0 kar do
r5 = torch.maximum(z, torch.zeros_like(z))   # scratch: max(0, z)
print("relu   :", r1.detach())
print("same?  :", all(torch.equal(r1, r) for r in [r2, r3, r4, r5]))

r1.sum().backward()
print("grad   :", z.grad)       # z=0 par PyTorch 0 deta hai

Output

relu   : tensor([0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.5000, 3.0000])
same?  : True
grad   : tensor([0., 0., 0., 1., 1.])
  • torch.relu(x) aur F.relu(x) same. nn.ReLU() layer hai; iska ek optional argument inplace=False (default) hai — True karne pe input tensor ko hi overwrite karta hai (memory bachata hai).
  • torch.clamp(z, min=0) = 0 se neeche sab 0. Scratch implementation ke liye sabse simple.
  • Gradient row: z = −3, −0.5 → 0; z = 0 → 0; positive → 1. PyTorch ka convention confirm.

Dying ReLU problem

Kahani

Valve wali kahani yaad hai? Ek din bahut zor ka jhatka laga (bahut bada update) aur valve "band" position me jam gaya. Ab chahe kitna bhi pressure aaye, valve nahi khulta. Aur valve kholne wala mechanic tabhi aata hai jab thoda sa paani beh raha ho (gradient) — paani zero, mechanic kabhi nahi aayega. Neuron hamesha ke liye dead.

Kya hota hai: agar kisi ReLU neuron ka z = w·x + b har training input ke liye negative ho jaaye, to wo har input pe 0 output deta hai. Uska derivative bhi har jagah 0. Chain rule me ye 0 multiply hota hai, to us neuron ke weights aur bias ka gradient exactly 0 — weights kabhi update nahi honge, neuron permanently dead. (Slide: "If a neuron outputs 0 for all training inputs, its gradient is also 0 → weight never updates → neuron is 'dead' permanently.")

Kyun hota hai (causes):

  • Bada learning rate / bada gradient update: ek jhatke me weights aur bias itne khisak jaate hain ki z sab inputs ke liye negative ho jaata hai (Lab 3 ka explanation).
  • Bada negative bias: b bahut negative ho to w·x use cross hi nahi kar paata. Teacher ke "activations" simulator ka scenario B: w = (0.5, 0.5), b = −3, data points (2, 2) ke aas-paas → z ≈ 0.5·4 − 3 = −1 < 0, aur (−2, −2) wale → −5. Sab negative: ReLU dead, weights bit-by-bit same rehte hain. Uske 2-3-1 network ka "one dead relu" preset ek hidden bias ko seedha −8 pe set karta hai.
  • Data drift: training pe neuron zinda tha, par real duniya ka data shift ho gaya (sensor recalibrate) aur ab saare inputs pe z < 0 (Lab 3 Part B).

Chalo numbers se samjhein — worksheet 03, Part 5

Sawaal: x = 1, w = −3, b = 0, y = 1, α = 1.

  1. z = −3,  ŷ = max(0, −3) = 0
  2. Error: 0 − 1 = −1 (galat hai!)
  3. Derivative: f′(−3) = 0
  4. Gradient: (−1)(0)(1) = 0,  Update: wnew = −3 − 0 = −3
  5. Agla update: phir z = −3, phir gradient 0... hamesha.
  6. α = 1,000,000 kar do: 106 × 0 = 0 — phir bhi zero.

Worksheet: "This perceptron is not slow, it is dead. The gradient is exactly zero rather than merely small, and no learning rate can rescue a product containing zero."

PyTorch · worksheet ke dono sides autograd se

import torch

def one_update(x_val, w_val, b_val, y_val, alpha, act):
    x = torch.tensor(float(x_val))
    w = torch.tensor(float(w_val), requires_grad=True)
    b = torch.tensor(float(b_val), requires_grad=True)
    y = torch.tensor(float(y_val))
    y_hat = act(w * x + b)
    loss = 0.5 * (y_hat - y) ** 2
    loss.backward()
    with torch.no_grad():
        new_w = w - alpha * w.grad
    return y_hat.item(), w.grad.item(), new_w.item()

# Positive side: worksheet Part 4.3 (x=1, w=6, b=0, y=0, alpha=1)
print("ReLU, w=6 :", one_update(1, 6, 0, 0, 1.0, torch.relu))
# Negative side: worksheet Part 5 (x=1, w=-3, b=0, y=1, alpha=1)
print("ReLU, w=-3:", one_update(1, -3, 0, 1, 1.0, torch.relu))
# Learning rate 10 lakh bhi kuch nahi karega
print("ReLU, w=-3, alpha=1e6:", one_update(1, -3, 0, 1, 1e6, torch.relu))

Output

ReLU, w=6 : (6.0, 6.0, 0.0)
ReLU, w=-3: (0.0, 0.0, -3.0)
ReLU, w=-3, alpha=1e6: (0.0, 0.0, -3.0)

Tuple = (ŷ, ∂L/∂w, new w). Positive side: ek step me w 6 → 0. Negative side: gradient 0, w −3 pe atka, chahe α 10 lakh ho.

PyTorch · Lab 3 · "Spot the dead neuron" (solution)

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

W_hidden = torch.tensor([[ 0.2, -0.5,  0.1,  0.8],
                         [ 0.4,  0.3, -0.7,  0.2],
                         [-0.1,  0.6,  0.5, -0.3]])   # (3 inputs, 4 neurons)
b_hidden = torch.tensor([0.1, -0.2, 0.3, 0.0])

# Part A: 100 samples, values -2 se 2 (har sample me 3 same features)
x1 = torch.linspace(-2, 2, 100).unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, 3)   # (100,) -> (100,1) -> (100,3)
z_hidden = x1 @ W_hidden + b_hidden                         # (100,3) @ (3,4) -> (100,4)
a_hidden = F.relu(z_hidden)
print("Part A: range -2 to 2")
for i in range(a_hidden.shape[1]):                          # har column = ek neuron
    is_dead = torch.all(a_hidden[:, i] == 0).item()         # poore column me sirf 0?
    print(f"Neuron {i} completely dead? {is_dead}")

# Part B: data drift - saari values 5 se neeche shift
x2 = x1 - 5.0                                               # ab range -7 to -3
a_hidden2 = F.relu(x2 @ W_hidden + b_hidden)
print("\nPart B: range -7 to -3")
for i in range(a_hidden2.shape[1]):
    is_dead = torch.all(a_hidden2[:, i] == 0).item()
    print(f"Neuron {i} completely dead? {is_dead}")
print("column sums of W_hidden:", W_hidden.sum(dim=0))

Output

Part A: range -2 to 2
Neuron 0 completely dead? False
Neuron 1 completely dead? False
Neuron 2 completely dead? False
Neuron 3 completely dead? False

Part B: range -7 to -3
Neuron 0 completely dead? True
Neuron 1 completely dead? True
Neuron 2 completely dead? False
Neuron 3 completely dead? True
column sums of W_hidden: tensor([ 0.5000,  0.4000, -0.1000,  0.7000])
  • torch.linspace(-2, 2, 100) = −2 se 2 tak 100 barabar doori wale numbers, shape (100,). .unsqueeze(1) → (100, 1). .repeat(1, 3) → (100, 3): har sample me teeno features same value t.
  • Rows = samples, columns = neurons. a_hidden[:, i] = neuron i ka poora column. torch.all(... == 0) = kya saare 100 samples pe output 0 hai? Haan → completely dead (is data ke liye).
  • Part B kyun: har sample (t, t, t) hai, to neuron j ka z = t × (column j ka sum) + bj. Column sums = (0.5, 0.4, −0.1, 0.7). t ∈ [−7, −3] par: neuron 0: 0.5t + 0.1 ∈ [−3.4, −1.4] → dead; neuron 1: 0.4t − 0.2 ∈ [−3.0, −1.4] → dead; neuron 3: 0.7t ∈ [−4.9, −2.1] → dead; neuron 2: −0.1t + 0.3 ∈ [0.6, 1.0] → zinda (negative weight sum × negative input = positive). Lab ka question isi ka hai: mostly positive weights + strongly negative inputs = negative z = dead.
Lab 3 trap: wahan "At z=0: ReLU'=1.00" print hua. Kyunki torch.linspace(-6, 6, 1201) ka centre element float32 me exactly 0 nahi, 1.34 × 10−7 hai (positive)! Exact 0 par PyTorch ReLU′ = 0 deta hai.

Fixes for dying ReLU: Leaky ReLU / PReLU / ELU (negative side pe non-zero slope), chhota learning rate, achha initialization (He init, Chapter 21), Batch Norm (Chapter 20).

Exam Radar

  • ReLU(z) = max(0, z), range [0, ∞), ReLU(0) = 0.
  • Derivative: 1 (z > 0), 0 (z < 0), undefined at 0 → PyTorch uses 0. Max derivative 1.
  • Pros: no vanishing gradient for z > 0, cheap, sparse. Default for hidden layers (CNNs, MLPs).
  • Cons: dying ReLU (cause: large LR / large negative bias; output 0 for all inputs → gradient 0 forever), not zero-centered, unbounded (final classification layer me nahi).
  • Code: torch.relu, F.relu, nn.ReLU(inplace=False), torch.clamp(z, min=0).

Galti mat karna

  • "ReLU me vanishing gradient bilkul nahi" — sirf z > 0 side pe. Negative side pe gradient vanish nahi, seedha zero hai (aur wahi dying ReLU hai).
  • Dead neuron "slow" nahi, "dead" hai: learning rate badhane se zinda nahi hoga.
  • ReLU linear nahi hai! Do linear tukde, beech me mod → non-linear.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

ReLU = one-way valve: ulta pressure → 0, seedha → jitna aaya utna. Valve jam = dead neuron.

9.7 Leaky ReLU (aur PReLU) — neuron ko zinda rakho

Kahani

Valve band hai, lekin plumber ne usme jaan-boojh ke ek chhota sa leak chhod diya. Ulta pressure aaye to bhi thoda-sa paani (1%) rista rehta hai. Is ristey paani se mechanic ko pata chalta rehta hai ki pipe zinda hai, aur wo valve ko theek kar sakta hai. Yahi Leaky ReLU hai.

Pehle ek galat idea (worksheet 03, Part 6): "ReLU positive side pe isliye kaam karta hai kyunki wahan f(z) = z, slope 1. To negative side pe bhi f(z) = z kar do!" Ye identity function ban jaata hai: derivative hamesha 1, koi neuron nahi marega... par ŷ = z = wx + b — activation ne kuch kiya hi nahi. Network phir ek seedhi line (9.1 ka linear trap). Hume chahiye: negative side pe non-zero slope, lekin positive side se alag slope, taaki z = 0 par mod bana rahe.

LeakyReLU(z) = max(αz, z) = z  agar z > 0,    αz  agar z ≤ 0    (α = 0.01)
LeakyReLU′(z) = 1  agar z > 0,    α  agar z < 0
  • α = chhota constant, typically 0.01 (PyTorch me naam negative_slope, default 0.01). Hyperparameter — haath se choose.
  • Range (−∞, ∞): negative side pe bhi chhote negative outputs (−3 → −0.03).
  • max(αz, z) wala form sirf 0 < α < 1 ke liye sahi hai (positive z pe z > αz, negative pe αz > z).

Chalo numbers se samjhein — wahi dead sawaal (worksheet 03, Part 7.2)

Sawaal: x = 1, w = −3, b = 0, y = 1, αlr = 1, slope 0.01.

  1. z = −3 (negative branch),  ŷ = 0.01 × (−3) = −0.03
  2. Error: −0.03 − 1 = −1.03
  3. Derivative: f′(−3) = 0.01
  4. Gradient: (−1.03)(0.01)(1) = −0.0103
  5. Update: wnew = −3 − (1)(−0.0103) = −2.9897

Jawab: w −3 → −2.9897. Neuron zinda hai (ReLU me step 0 tha), lekin "crawling" — bahut dheere.

Leaky ReLU ki do kamzoriyan (worksheet): (1) negative side ka output bahut chhota (−0.03), kyunki 0.01 ek chhota fixed constant hai jo haath se chuna; (2) z = 0 par derivative 0.01 se 1 pe jump karta hai — derivative continuous nahi.

PReLU — α ko bhi seekh lo

Parametric ReLU (PReLU): formula same, max(αz, z), lekin α ek learnable parameter hai jo backprop se train hota hai (He et al., 2015). Fayda: sahi slope data khud chunta hai. Nuksaan: extra parameters train karne padte hain (aur overfitting ka thoda risk). PyTorch: nn.PReLU(num_parameters=1, init=0.25) — default ek hi α poori layer ke liye, shuru me 0.25; num_parameters=C do to har channel ka alag α.

PyTorch · Leaky ReLU + PReLU

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

z = torch.tensor([-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 2.0], requires_grad=True)

l1 = F.leaky_relu(z, negative_slope=0.01)       # functional; default slope bhi 0.01 hai
l2 = nn.LeakyReLU(0.01)(z)                      # layer; pehla argument = negative_slope
l3 = torch.where(z > 0, z, 0.01 * z)            # scratch: z>0 to z, warna 0.01*z
print("leaky :", l1.detach())
print("same? :", torch.allclose(l1, l2), torch.allclose(l1, l3))
l1.sum().backward()
print("grad  :", z.grad)

prelu = nn.PReLU()                              # alpha ek learnable parameter hai
print("PReLU alpha (init):", prelu.weight.data, "| trainable params:",
      sum(p.numel() for p in prelu.parameters()))
print("PReLU output:", prelu(torch.tensor([-3.0, 2.0])).detach())

Output

leaky : tensor([-0.0300, -0.0100,  0.0000,  2.0000])
same? : True True
grad  : tensor([0.0100, 0.0100, 0.0100, 1.0000])
PReLU alpha (init): tensor([0.2500]) | trainable params: 1
PReLU output: tensor([-0.7500,  2.0000])
  • F.leaky_relu(x, negative_slope=0.01) functional; nn.LeakyReLU(negative_slope=0.01) layer — pehla positional argument hi slope hai, isliye nn.LeakyReLU(0.01).
  • torch.where(cond, a, b): jahan cond True wahan a, warna b — piecewise functions likhne ka standard tareeka.
  • Gradient: negative aur z = 0 dono pe 0.01 (PyTorch z = 0 ko negative branch me rakhta hai), positive pe 1.
  • PReLU ka α ek nn.Parameter hai (prelu.weight), isliye parameters() me count hota hai: 1. Output: −3 × 0.25 = −0.75.

Exam Radar

  • Leaky ReLU = max(αz, z), α = 0.01; PyTorch negative_slope=0.01 default.
  • Derivative: 1 (z > 0), α (z < 0) → fixes dying ReLU. Range (−∞, ∞).
  • Cons: α hand-tuned hyperparameter; tiny negative outputs; derivative jump at 0.
  • PReLU: α learned; nn.PReLU() default init 0.25, 1 parameter. Con: extra parameters.
  • Use: GANs ke hidden layers (dead units training bigaadte hain), jab ReLU units mar rahe hon.

Galti mat karna

  • Identity function (slope 1 dono taraf) = "Leaky ReLU with α = 1" = linear = bekaar. Slopes alag hone chahiye.
  • Leaky ReLU ka α (slope) aur learning rate α alag cheezein hain.
  • PReLU ka α learn hota hai, Leaky ka fixed — MCQ ka favourite difference.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Leaky = valve me 1% leak. PReLU = leak kitna ho, wo pipe khud seekhe.

9.8 ELU — smooth negative side

Kahani

Kitchen ki "soft-close" drawer dekhi hai? Dhakka do to wo seedha thak se nahi lagti — dheere-dheere smoothly ruk jaati hai ek fixed point pe. ELU ka negative side bhi aisa hi hai: seedhi leak wali line nahi, balki ek smooth curve jo dheere-dheere ek floor (−α) tak jaake ruk jaati hai.

ELU(z) = z  agar z > 0,    α(ez − 1)  agar z ≤ 0    (α = 1.0 default)
ELU′(z) = 1  agar z > 0,    αez = ELU(z) + α  agar z < 0
  • ELU = Exponential Linear Unit (Clevert et al., 2015). α = scale, PyTorch alpha=1.0 default.
  • Range (−α, ∞); α = 1 ke saath (−1, ∞). ELU(0) = α(e0 − 1) = 0.
  • z → −∞: ez → 0, to ELU → α(0 − 1) = −α. Ye floor hai: negative side bounded → saturates to −α.
  • Derivative derivation: d/dz[α(ez − 1)] = α·ez − 0 = αez (ez ka derivative ez, constant −1 ka 0). Aur αez = α(ez − 1) + α = ELU(z) + α — derivative output se hi nikal aata hai.

Smooth kyun? z = 0 par left side ka derivative αe0 = α, right side ka 1. Agar α = 1, dono barabar — koi jump nahi, function "continuously differentiable" (kink-free) ban jaata hai. ReLU (0 → 1 jump) aur Leaky (0.01 → 1 jump) dono ke paas kink hai, ELU (α = 1) ke paas nahi. Lab 3: "Because the gradients match from both directions, the transition is seamless... This smoothness can help gradient descent converge faster by avoiding oscillations around the origin."

Chalo numbers se samjhein — worksheet 03, Part 8.2

Sawaal: x = 1, w = −3, b = 0, y = 1, learning rate 1, ELU α = 1. (Useful: e−3 = 0.049787)

  1. z = −3 (negative branch)
  2. ŷ = e−3 − 1 = 0.049787 − 1 = −0.950213
  3. Error: −0.950213 − 1 = −1.950213
  4. Derivative: f′(−3) = e−3 = 0.049787 (check: ELU + α = −0.950213 + 1 = 0.049787 ✓)
  5. Gradient: (−1.950213)(0.049787)(1) = −0.097095
  6. Update: wnew = −3 + 0.097095 = −2.902905

Jawab: w = −2.902905. ELU ka step / Leaky ka step = 0.097095/0.0103 ≈ 9.4 guna. Kyun? Negative output −0.95 (lagbhag −1, sirf −0.03 nahi) aur derivative 0.0498 (fixed 0.01 nahi).

Activation (x = 1, w = −3, y = 1)ŷf′(−3)∂L/∂ww: −3 →Verdict
ReLU000−3Dead
Identity−31−41Alive, par network ek seedhi line
Leaky ReLU−0.030.01−0.0103−2.9897Alive, crawling
ELU−0.9502130.049787−0.097095−2.902905Alive, moving properly

PyTorch · worksheet ka verdict table autograd se (float64)

import torch

def one_update(x_val, w_val, b_val, y_val, alpha, act):
    x = torch.tensor(float(x_val), dtype=torch.float64)
    w = torch.tensor(float(w_val), dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
    b = torch.tensor(float(b_val), dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True)
    y = torch.tensor(float(y_val), dtype=torch.float64)
    y_hat = act(w * x + b)
    loss = 0.5 * (y_hat - y) ** 2
    loss.backward()
    with torch.no_grad():
        new_w = w - alpha * w.grad
    return round(y_hat.item(), 6), round(w.grad.item(), 6), round(new_w.item(), 6)

import torch.nn.functional as F
# Worksheet Part 5/7/8: x=1, w=-3, b=0, y=1, alpha=1
print("ReLU      :", one_update(1, -3, 0, 1, 1.0, F.relu))
print("Identity  :", one_update(1, -3, 0, 1, 1.0, lambda t: t))
print("LeakyReLU :", one_update(1, -3, 0, 1, 1.0, lambda t: F.leaky_relu(t, 0.01)))
print("ELU       :", one_update(1, -3, 0, 1, 1.0, lambda t: F.elu(t, alpha=1.0)))

Output

ReLU      : (0.0, 0.0, -3.0)
Identity  : (-3.0, -4.0, 1.0)
LeakyReLU : (-0.03, -0.0103, -2.9897)
ELU       : (-0.950213, -0.097095, -2.902905)

PyTorch · ELU teen tareeke + derivative = ELU + α

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

z = torch.tensor([-5.0, -1.0, 0.0, 2.0], requires_grad=True)
alpha = 1.0

e1 = F.elu(z, alpha=alpha)                               # functional
e2 = nn.ELU(alpha=alpha)(z)                              # layer
e3 = torch.where(z > 0, z, alpha * (torch.exp(z) - 1))   # scratch
print("elu   :", e1.detach())
print("same? :", torch.allclose(e1, e2), torch.allclose(e1, e3))

e1.sum().backward()
print("grad          :", z.grad)
print("ELU(z) + alpha:", (e1 + alpha).detach(), "(sirf z <= 0 wale entries match karne chahiye)")

Output

elu   : tensor([-0.9933, -0.6321,  0.0000,  2.0000])
same? : True True
grad          : tensor([0.0067, 0.3679, 1.0000, 1.0000])
ELU(z) + alpha: tensor([0.0067, 0.3679, 1.0000, 3.0000]) (sirf z <= 0 wale entries match karne chahiye)

Negative entries (−5, −1) aur z = 0 pe grad = ELU + α (0.0067, 0.3679, 1.0). Positive z = 2 pe grad 1 hai, ELU + α = 3 nahi — formula sirf negative side ka hai. F.elu(x, alpha=1.0) functional, nn.ELU(alpha=1.0) layer; dono me alpha default 1.0.

ELU ke fayde

  • Never dies: negative side pe gradient αez > 0
  • Smooth at 0 (α = 1): no kink, behtar gradient flow
  • Negative outputs → mean activation zero ke paas → Batch Norm jaisa fayda, faster convergence
  • Bounded below (−α) → negative side noise ke liye robust; aur ek seedhi line nahi, to non-linear

Nuksaan

  • exp() lagta hai (z < 0 pe) → ReLU se slow
  • Bahut negative z pe derivative phir chhota (e−10 ≈ 0.000045) — negative side saturate hota hai
  • α ek aur hyperparameter

Use: hidden layers jahan bahut saare ReLU units mar rahe hon, ya jahan faster convergence chahiye.

Exam Radar

  • ELU = z (z > 0), α(ez − 1) (z ≤ 0); α = 1.0 default; range (−α, ∞).
  • Derivative z < 0: αez = ELU(z) + α; z = 0 pe α (=1 → smooth).
  • Saturates to −α for very negative z; mean activations closer to zero; costlier (exp).
  • ELU(−1) = −0.6321, ELU(−3) = −0.9502, ELU(−5) = −0.9933.
  • Lecture slide family summary: ReLU (fast, sparse, dies), Leaky (no dying, α tune), ELU (smooth, near-zero mean, exp cost), PReLU (α learned, extra params).

Galti mat karna

  • ELU ka range (−1, ∞) sirf α = 1 ke liye; general (−α, ∞).
  • ELU "saturate nahi hota" — galat; positive side pe nahi, negative side pe −α pe saturate hota hai. Ye feature hai (noise robustness), bug nahi.
  • ELU ka derivative z < 0 pe ez − 1 nahi, αez hai (−1 constant ka derivative 0).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

ELU = soft-close drawer: positive pe ReLU, negative pe smooth landing at −α.

9.9 Softmax — scores ko probabilities me badlo

Kahani

Teen dost — Cat, Dog, Bird — ek hi biryani ki handi share kar rahe hain. Har ek ka "bhookh score" hai: 2.0, 1.0, 0.1. Rule: handi poori baantni hai (total = 1 handi), koi khaali haath nahi jaayega (sabko kuch na kuch), aur jo zyada bhookha uska hissa kaafi zyada — sirf thoda nahi. Softmax yahi baantwara karta hai: Cat ko 65.9%, Dog ko 24.2%, Bird ko 9.9%.

Ab tak ke activations ek number lete the, ek number dete the (element-wise). Softmax alag hai: ye poora vector leta hai (har class ka ek raw score, jise logit bolte hain) aur ek probability distribution deta hai. Sigmoid ek yes/no sawaal ka jawab deta hai. Teen class (cat/dog/bird) ke liye ek sigmoid kaafi nahi, aur teen alag sigmoids bhi nahi — wo independently answer karenge aur sum 1 nahi hoga (sigmoid([2, 1, 0.1]) = [0.8808, 0.7311, 0.5250], sum 2.1368!). Hume ek function chahiye jo teeno scores ko saath me dekhe.

softmax(z)i = si = eziΣj=1K ezj
  • z = (z1, ..., zK) = final layer ke K raw scores (logits), koi bhi real numbers
  • ezi = exponential: har value positive bana deta hai, aur bade score ko bahut zyada bada (amplify)
  • Σj ezj = saare exponentials ka total; isse divide karne pe sum exactly 1
  • Har si ∈ (0, 1), aur Σi si = 1 → valid probability distribution

Chalo numbers se samjhein — worksheet 03 Part 10.3 / Lab 3

Sawaal: logits z = [2.0, 1.0, 0.1] (cat, dog, bird). Softmax nikalo.

  1. Exponentiate: e2.0 = 7.389056,  e1.0 = 2.718282,  e0.1 = 1.105171
  2. Add: Σ = 7.389056 + 2.718282 + 1.105171 = 11.212509
  3. Divide: p1 = 7.389056/11.212509 = 0.659001
  4. p2 = 2.718282/11.212509 = 0.242433
  5. p3 = 1.105171/11.212509 = 0.098566
  6. Check: 0.659001 + 0.242433 + 0.098566 = 1.000000 ✓

Jawab: ≈ [0.659, 0.242, 0.099]. Sabse bada = cat, 65.9% confidence.

Lecture slide wala example: logits [2.0, 1.0, −1.0] → e: 7.39, 2.72, 0.37; Σ = 10.48 → 70.5%, 25.9%, 3.5%. Dhyaan do: scores me fark 2 vs 1 tha (sirf 2 guna), probabilities me 70.5 vs 25.9 (≈ e1 = 2.72 guna) — exponential differences ko amplify karta hai.

PyTorch · Lab 3 · softmax chaar tareeke

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

logits = torch.tensor([2.0, 1.0, 0.1])            # cat, dog, bird ke raw scores

p1 = torch.softmax(logits, dim=0)                 # functional (torch namespace)
p2 = F.softmax(logits, dim=0)                     # functional (F namespace)
p3 = nn.Softmax(dim=0)(logits)                    # layer
p4 = torch.exp(logits) / torch.exp(logits).sum()  # scratch
print("probs :", p1)
print("sum   :", p1.sum().item())
print("same? :", torch.allclose(p1, p2), torch.allclose(p1, p3), torch.allclose(p1, p4))
print("argmax logits:", logits.argmax().item(), "| argmax probs:", p1.argmax().item())

Output

probs : tensor([0.6590, 0.2424, 0.0986])
sum   : 1.0000001192092896
same? : True True True
argmax logits: 0 | argmax probs: 0

Sum 1.0000001192... aaya, exactly 1 nahi — ye float32 ki rounding hai (Lab 3 me bhi yahi print hua). torch.softmax(x, dim=...), F.softmax(x, dim=...), nn.Softmax(dim=...) — teeno me dim batana zaroori hai: kis dimension ke across sum 1 karna hai.

Key properties

  • Probability distribution: har output (0, 1) me, total 1 → class probabilities ki tarah padho.
  • Order preserved: ez increasing hai, aur sabko same Σ se divide kiya → bada logit = badi probability. Isliye argmax(softmax(z)) = argmax(z). Sirf predicted class chahiye (accuracy) to softmax lagane ki zaroorat hi nahi — logits ka argmax kaafi hai.
  • Amplifies differences: sabse bade logit ko disproportionately badi probability; chhote squeeze ho ke 0 ki taraf.
  • Output layer only: hidden layers me kabhi nahi (wahan ReLU). Worksheet: "Meaningful only across a whole layer, never for one unit alone."
  • Pair with cross-entropy: softmax + categorical cross-entropy = standard multi-class setup (Chapter 11).

Shift invariance: sab scores me same number jodo, kuch nahi badalta

Proof

softmax(z + c)i = ezi + cΣj ezj + c = ec · eziec · Σj ezj = eziΣj ezj = softmax(z)i

ec upar-neeche dono me hai, cancel. Check: [102, 101, 100.1] ka softmax bhi [0.659001, 0.242433, 0.098566]. Softmax sirf scores ke differences ko dekhta hai, absolute level ko nahi.

Numerical stability: subtract-max trick

Chalo numbers se samjhein — overflow

Sawaal: logits [1000, 1001, 1002].

  1. Naive: e1000 computer me inf (float32 sirf e88.7 tak, float64 e709.8 tak sambhal sakta hai). inf/inf = nan → output [nan, nan, nan]. Training barbaad.
  2. Trick: max (1002) subtract karo (shift invariance se answer nahi badlega): [1000, 1001, 1002] − 1002 = [−2, −1, 0]
  3. e−2 = 0.135335, e−1 = 0.367879, e0 = 1; Σ = 1.503215
  4. 0.135335/1.503215 = 0.090031,  0.367879/1.503215 = 0.244728,  1/1.503215 = 0.665241

Jawab: [0.0900, 0.2447, 0.6652]. Max subtract karne ke baad sabse bada exponent e0 = 1 — overflow impossible, aur denominator ≥ 1, to divide-by-zero bhi nahi.

PyTorch · overflow vs stable softmax

import torch

big = torch.tensor([1000.0, 1001.0, 1002.0])

naive = torch.exp(big) / torch.exp(big).sum()     # e^1000 = inf  ->  inf/inf = nan
print("naive :", naive)

shifted = big - big.max()                         # [-2, -1, 0]: max ab 0 hai
stable = torch.exp(shifted) / torch.exp(shifted).sum()
print("stable:", stable)
print("torch :", torch.softmax(big, dim=0))       # PyTorch andar se yahi trick karta hai

# Shift invariance: har score me same constant jodo, probs same
z = torch.tensor([2.0, 1.0, 0.1])
print(torch.softmax(z, dim=0), torch.softmax(z + 100, dim=0))

Output

naive : tensor([nan, nan, nan])
stable: tensor([0.0900, 0.2447, 0.6652])
torch : tensor([0.0900, 0.2447, 0.6652])
tensor([0.6590, 0.2424, 0.0986]) tensor([0.6590, 0.2424, 0.0986])

Teacher ke Lab 2 visualizer ke JavaScript me bhi softmax aise hi likha hai: Math.exp(s - maxS). Built-in torch.softmax ye trick khud karta hai; scratch implementation me tumhe karna padega.

Temperature (slide me hai)

softmax(z/T): T = temperature. Low T (< 1) → differences bade → distribution sharp (lagbhag one-hot). High T (> 1) → differences chhote → soft/uniform. T = 1 normal softmax. LLMs ka "temperature" setting yahi hai.

Softmax vs Sigmoid, aur 2-class softmax = sigmoid

ProblemOutput activationOutput unitsExample
Binary (2 class, ek sawaal)Sigmoid1Spam ya nahi
Multi-class, single-label (exactly ek class sahi)SoftmaxK (har class ka ek)Digit 0–9 → 10 units
Multi-label (kai classes ek saath sahi ho sakti)Sigmoid har unit pe (independent)KPhoto me cat bhi, dog bhi

Proof: 2-class softmax = sigmoid of the difference

s1 = ez1ez1 + ez2   (upar-neeche ez1 se divide)
= 11 + ez2 − z1 = 11 + e−(z1 − z2) = σ(z1 − z2)

Worksheet ka version: scores z aur 0 lo → softmax = ez/(ez + 1) = 1/(1 + e−z) = σ(z). "Sigmoid is simply softmax for two classes." Numbers: logits [2.0, 0.5] → softmax [0.8176, 0.1824], aur σ(2.0 − 0.5) = σ(1.5) = 0.8176 ✓.

Derivative (Jacobian) — bas pehchaan lo

∂si∂zj = si(δij − sj)
  • δij = Kronecker delta: 1 agar i = j, warna 0
  • Diagonal (i = j): si(1 − si) — bilkul sigmoid jaisa!
  • Off-diagonal (i ≠ j): −sisj — ek class ka score badhao to baaki ki probabilities ghatti hain (sum 1 jo rehna hai)
  • Output ek vector hai, input ek vector — isliye derivative ek matrix (Jacobian). Har row ka sum 0 (kyunki Σs = 1 constant).

PyTorch · 2-class = sigmoid, temperature, Jacobian check

import torch

# 2-class softmax = sigmoid(z1 - z2)
z = torch.tensor([2.0, 0.5])
print("softmax :", torch.softmax(z, dim=0))
print("sigmoid :", torch.sigmoid(z[0] - z[1]), torch.sigmoid(z[1] - z[0]))

# Temperature: softmax(z / T)
logits = torch.tensor([2.0, 1.0, 0.1])
for T in [0.5, 1.0, 2.0]:
    print(f"T={T}:", torch.softmax(logits / T, dim=0))

# Jacobian: d s_i / d z_j = s_i * (delta_ij - s_j)
s = torch.softmax(logits, dim=0)
J_auto = torch.autograd.functional.jacobian(lambda t: torch.softmax(t, dim=0), logits)
J_formula = torch.diag(s) - torch.outer(s, s)
print("Jacobian:\n", J_auto)
print("formula match?", torch.allclose(J_auto, J_formula, atol=1e-6))

Output

softmax : tensor([0.8176, 0.1824])
sigmoid : tensor(0.8176) tensor(0.1824)
T=0.5: tensor([0.8638, 0.1169, 0.0193])
T=1.0: tensor([0.6590, 0.2424, 0.0986])
T=2.0: tensor([0.5017, 0.3043, 0.1940])
Jacobian:
 tensor([[ 0.2247, -0.1598, -0.0650],
        [-0.1598,  0.1837, -0.0239],
        [-0.0650, -0.0239,  0.0889]])
formula match? True

Jacobian diagonal: 0.659(1 − 0.659) = 0.2247 ✓. torch.autograd.functional.jacobian(f, x) poora derivative matrix de deta hai; torch.outer(s, s) = s ka har element s ke har element se multiply (3×3 matrix).

The dim trap (Lab 3 pro-tip)

Ek akela vector (shape (3,)) ho to dim=0. Lekin real training me batch hota hai: shape (N, K) — rows = samples, columns = classes. Har sample ki probabilities ka sum 1 chahiye → sum columns ke across, yaani dim=1.

PyTorch · nn.Softmax(dim=1) vs galat dim=0

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Batch: 2 samples (rows), 3 classes (columns)  -> shape (2, 3)
logits = torch.tensor([[2.0, 1.0, 0.1],
                       [1.0, 3.0, 0.5]])

right = nn.Softmax(dim=1)(logits)     # har ROW (sample) ke andar softmax
wrong = nn.Softmax(dim=0)(logits)     # har COLUMN ke andar - galat!
print("dim=1:\n", right, "\nrow sums:", right.sum(dim=1))
print("dim=0:\n", wrong, "\nrow sums:", wrong.sum(dim=1))

Output

dim=1:
 tensor([[0.6590, 0.2424, 0.0986],
        [0.1112, 0.8214, 0.0674]]) 
row sums: tensor([1.0000, 1.0000])
dim=0:
 tensor([[0.7311, 0.1192, 0.4013],
        [0.2689, 0.8808, 0.5987]]) 
row sums: tensor([1.2516, 1.7484])

dim=0 ne har column (ek class, saare samples) ko normalize kar diya — rows ka sum 1.25 aur 1.75, bakwaas. Koi error bhi nahi aayi! Silent bug. dim=-1 (last dimension) bhi (N, K) ke liye dim=1 jaisa hi kaam karta hai.

nn.CrossEntropyLoss ko raw logits do (link Chapter 11)

PyTorch ka nn.CrossEntropyLoss andar khud log-softmax lagata hai (stable tareeke se), phir correct class ki −log probability leta hai. Isliye model ki last layer pe softmax mat lagao jab ye loss use karo — warna softmax do baar lagega.

PyTorch · double softmax ki galti

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

torch.manual_seed(0)
logits = torch.tensor([[2.0, 1.0, 0.1],
                       [1.0, 3.0, 0.5]])     # model ka raw output, (N=2, K=3)
target = torch.tensor([0, 2])               # class indices: sample0 -> cat, sample1 -> bird

ce = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()                  # andar khud log-softmax lagata hai
print("sahi  (raw logits)      :", ce(logits, target).item())
print("galat (softmax pehle)   :", ce(torch.softmax(logits, dim=1), target).item())
manual = -(torch.log(torch.softmax(logits, dim=1))[[0, 1], target]).mean()
print("manual -mean(log p_true):", manual.item())

Output

sahi  (raw logits)      : 1.5568820238113403
galat (softmax pehle)   : 1.1150377988815308
manual -mean(log p_true): 1.5568821430206299

Sahi value 1.5569 = mean(−ln 0.659001, −ln 0.067425) = mean(0.4170, 2.6967). Softmax pehle laga diya to loss 1.1150 — galat number, aur gradients bhi kamzor (probabilities pe dobara softmax sab ko flat kar deta hai). Target [0, 2] class indices hain (dtype long), one-hot nahi.

Exam Radar

  • si = ezi/Σjezj; outputs (0, 1), sum = 1; [2.0, 1.0, 0.1] → [0.659, 0.242, 0.099].
  • Shift invariant: softmax(z + c) = softmax(z) → subtract max for stability ([1000, 1001, 1002] naive → nan; stable → [0.090, 0.245, 0.665]).
  • argmax unchanged by softmax (order preserved).
  • 2-class softmax = σ(z1 − z2). Binary → sigmoid (1 unit); multi-class single-label → softmax (K units); multi-label → K sigmoids.
  • Jacobian ∂si/∂zj = si(δij − sj).
  • Temperature: low T sharp, high T soft. Output layer only, never hidden.
  • Code: torch.softmax(x, dim=1), F.softmax(x, dim=1), nn.Softmax(dim=1) for (N, K) batches. nn.CrossEntropyLoss wants raw logits + class indices.

Galti mat karna

  • Softmax ko "element-wise" mat bolna — har output saare inputs pe depend karta hai.
  • Batch (N, K) pe dim=0 lagana: error nahi aayega, answer galat aayega.
  • nn.CrossEntropyLoss se pehle softmax lagana = double softmax.
  • Multi-label problem pe softmax: galat, kyunki softmax classes ko aapas me compete karwata hai (ek badhe to doosri ghate).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Biryani ki ek handi: ez se bhookh badhao, total se baanto, sab ka hissa jod ke 1. Sab ki bhookh me same number jodo — baantwara same.

9.11 Kaunsa activation kahan? — practical guide

Kahani

Ek restaurant ki kitchen socho: andar ke saare cooks (hidden layers) ek hi tez, sasti technique use karte hain — ReLU. Lekin counter pe plate (output layer) kaise serve hogi, ye customer ke order pe depend karta hai: number chahiye (bill amount) to seedha number, haan/na chahiye to sigmoid, menu me se ek dish chunni hai to softmax.

Jagah / TaskActivationOutput unitsLoss (PyTorch)
Hidden layers (default)ReLUany—
Hidden, units mar rahe honLeaky ReLU / ELU / PReLUany—
Hidden in RNN/LSTM, old netstanh (states), sigmoid (gates)——
Regression (number)None (linear); ReLU agar negative ho hi nahi sakta1 (per target)nn.MSELoss / nn.L1Loss
Binary classificationSigmoid1nn.BCELoss (after sigmoid) ya nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss (raw logit)
Multi-class (single label)SoftmaxKnn.CrossEntropyLoss — raw logits do, softmax nahi
Multi-labelSigmoid per classKnn.BCEWithLogitsLoss

Worksheet ke final questions: (1) 10 digits (0–9) classify karne hain → final layer me 10 units, softmax. (2) Chest X-ray normal ya pneumonia → 1 unit, sigmoid, binary cross-entropy. Worksheet ki line: "The activation function decides what the network can output. The loss function decides how we score it. They must be chosen as a pair."

PyTorch · ek nn.Module, teen tarah ke output

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_features, n_out, task):
        super().__init__()
        self.task = task
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(in_features, 16), nn.ReLU(),    # hidden layer 1: ReLU
            nn.Linear(16, 8), nn.ReLU(),              # hidden layer 2: ReLU
        )
        self.head = nn.Linear(8, n_out)               # output layer: raw scores (logits)

    def forward(self, x):
        out = self.head(self.body(x))
        if self.task == "regression":
            return out                                # koi activation nahi
        if self.task == "binary":
            return torch.sigmoid(out)                 # (N, 1), har value (0, 1) me
        if self.task == "multiclass":
            return torch.softmax(out, dim=1)          # (N, K), har row ka sum 1

torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randn(4, 5)                                 # 4 samples, 5 features
print("regression:", Net(5, 1, "regression")(x).shape)
print("binary    :", Net(5, 1, "binary")(x).squeeze().detach())
probs = Net(5, 3, "multiclass")(x)
print("multiclass row sums:", probs.sum(dim=1).detach())

Output

regression: torch.Size([4, 1])
binary    : tensor([0.5126, 0.4880, 0.5301, 0.4966])
multiclass row sums: tensor([1., 1., 1., 1.])
  • Hidden layers nn.Sequential me nn.Linear + nn.ReLU() pairs. Activation layers ke koi parameters nahi hote, sirf Linear ke.
  • Binary output (N, 1) me har value (0, 1); multiclass (N, K) me dim=1 softmax, har row ka sum 1.
  • Practice tip: training ke time aksar forward raw logits return karta hai aur nn.CrossEntropyLoss / nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss andar stable tareeke se softmax/sigmoid sambhal lete hain. Probabilities sirf prediction/report ke time chahiye. (Binary values ~0.5 isliye kyunki model untrained hai.)

Exam Radar

  • Hidden default: ReLU. Dying problem → Leaky ReLU / ELU.
  • Output: regression → none/linear; binary → sigmoid (1 unit); multi-class → softmax (K units); multi-label → sigmoid (K units).
  • ReLU final classification layer me nahi (unbounded); softmax hidden layer me nahi.
  • nn.CrossEntropyLoss = log-softmax + NLL → raw logits do.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Andar ReLU, bahar order ke hisaab se: number → kuch nahi, haan/na → sigmoid, ek-me-se-ek → softmax.

Chapter 10

Universal Approximation Theorem, Depth vs Width

Network capacity · UAT (Cybenko 1989, Hornik 1991) · bumps & ReLU pieces · linear regions · folding · depth vs width trade-off

10.1 Network capacity, width aur depth — pehle shabd samjho

Kahani

Golu ke paas LEGO blocks hain. Kitni tarah ki cheezein bana sakta hai — ye do baaton pe depend karta hai: (1) har manzil (floor) me kitne blocks rakh sakta hai — chaudai, aur (2) kitni manzilein upar-upar jod sakta hai — oonchai. Zyada blocks = zyada tarah ki shapes. Neural network me bhi yahi: "kitni tarah ke functions bana sakta hai" = capacity; har layer me neurons = width; kitni layers = depth.

Definitions

Capacity (expressiveness / expressive power): network kitne alag-alag, kitne complicated functions represent kar sakta hai. Zyada capacity = zyada flexible (lekin overfitting ka risk bhi, Chapter 18).

Width (UDL me D): ek hidden layer me kitne neurons (hidden units).

Depth (UDL me K): kitni hidden layers. Ek hidden layer = shallow network (Chapter 7); do ya zyada = deep network.

Lecture slide: "Neural network architectures are primarily characterized by: Depth → number of layers, Width → number of neurons per layer. Both influence model capacity, expressiveness, and computational cost — but in different ways." Is chapter ka sawaal: ek hidden layer kitna kar sakta hai, aur depth kyun chahiye?

10.2 Universal Approximation Theorem (UAT)

Kahani

Ek darzi (tailor) kehta hai: "Mujhe kaafi saare chhote kapde ke tukde do, main tumhare body ke kisi bhi shape ka kurta itna fit bana dunga ki fark ek millimetre se kam ho." Wo ye nahi kehta ki kitne tukde lagenge (shayad lakhon), na ye ki wo kitni der me banayega. Bas itna guarantee: ban sakta hai. UAT bhi aisa hi darzi hai.

UAT — simple shabdon me

Ek feed-forward network jisme sirf ek hidden layer ho, us layer me kaafi (finite) neurons hon, aur ek non-linear activation ho — wo kisi bhi continuous function ko, ek closed aur bounded region pe, jitna chaho utni accuracy se approximate kar sakta hai.

Har continuous f aur har ε > 0 ke liye aise N, vi, wi, bi exist karte hain ki
F(x) = Σi=1N vi φ(wi·x + bi)    aur    |F(x) − f(x)| < ε   har x ∈ K ke liye
  • F(x) = shallow network: N hidden units, unit i ke weights wi, bias bi, output weight vi (chaaho to output bias bhi jodo)
  • φ = non-linear activation (Cybenko: sigmoid; general: koi bhi non-polynomial, jaise ReLU, tanh)
  • K = compact set ⊂ ℝn = closed + bounded region, jaise [0, 1] ya [−π, π] ya ek box. Poori infinite real line nahi.
  • ε (epsilon) = allowed galti; jitna chhota chaho (0.1, 0.001, ...) — bas N badhta jaayega
  • "Universal" = kisi bhi continuous function ke liye; "Approximation" = exact nahi, ε ke andar

History (MCQ favourite):

  • Cybenko (1989) — "Approximation by superpositions of a sigmoidal function": proof sigmoid activation ke liye.
  • Hornik (1991) (aur Hornik, Stinchcombe & White, 1989) — dikhaya ki ye kisi khaas activation ka kamaal nahi; multilayer feed-forward architecture khud universal approximator hai (general activations).
  • Leshno et al. (1993): koi bhi non-polynomial activation chalega — isme ReLU bhi aata hai.
  • Teacher ke Lecture 1 worksheet ki timeline: 1986 backprop ne revival kiya, aur "the Universal Approximation Theorem (1989) then gave that revival a theoretical foundation."

Lecture slide ka exact statement: "A feed-forward network with a single hidden layer containing a finite number of neurons can approximate continuous functions on compact subsets of ℝn." Aur turant "The Catch: To approximate complex functions, that single layer might need an exponentially large number of neurons (infinite width)."

Exam Radar

  • UAT: one hidden layer, finite (but enough) neurons, non-linear activation → any continuous function on a compact (closed, bounded) set, any accuracy ε.
  • Cybenko 1989 = sigmoid; Hornik 1991 = general (architecture is what matters).
  • Linear activation ke saath UAT fail (network linear hi rahega) — non-linearity zaroori.
  • Catch: neurons ki sankhya exponentially badi ho sakti hai.

Galti mat karna

  • "UAT kehta hai ek hidden layer kaafi hai, to deep networks bekaar" — galat. UAT existence batata hai, efficiency nahi (10.5, 10.7).
  • "Any function" nahi — continuous function, compact domain pe.
  • "Exact" nahi — approximate (ε ke andar).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

UAT = darzi ki guarantee: "ban jayega" — kitne tukde, kitna time, aur doosre insaan pe fit hoga ya nahi — ye guarantee nahi.

10.3 Intuition 1: sigmoid se "bump", bumps se koi bhi curve

Kahani

Diwali pe ghar ki deewar pe LED lights ka "skyline" banana hai. Har light ek chhota sa khamba (bar) hai — jitni chaho utni oonchai. Bahut saare patle-patle khambe paas-paas lagao, har ek ki oonchai curve ke hisaab se rakho — door se dekhne pe poora curve dikhta hai. Sigmoid neurons se aise hi "khambe" (bumps) bante hain.

Step 1 — steep sigmoid = lagbhag step. σ(k(x − a)) me k bada lo (weight bada) to S-curve bahut steep ho jaata hai: x < a pe ≈ 0, x > a pe ≈ 1. Bias se jump ki jagah (a) chunte hain: σ(kx − ka), yaani weight k, bias −ka.

Step 2 — do steps ka difference = bump. Ek step a pe upar, doosra b pe: bump(x) = σ(k(x − a)) − σ(k(x − b)). [a, b] ke andar ≈ 1, bahar ≈ 0. Ek bump = 2 hidden neurons (output weights +h aur −h, jahan h = bump ki oonchai).

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: a = 1, b = 2, k = 10. bump(x) nikalo.

  1. x = 1.5 (andar): σ(10 × 0.5) − σ(10 × (−0.5)) = σ(5) − σ(−5) = 0.993307 − 0.006693 = 0.986614
  2. x = 1 (kinare pe): σ(0) − σ(−10) = 0.5 − 0.000045 = 0.499955
  3. x = 0 (bahar): σ(−10) − σ(−20) ≈ 0.000045 − 0.000000 = 0.000045
  4. x = 3 (bahar): σ(20) − σ(10) = 1.000000 − 0.999955 = 0.000045

Jawab: andar ≈ 0.99, bahar ≈ 0 — ek saaf bump. k aur bada karo to aur bhi rectangle jaisa.

Step 3 — bahut saare bumps = koi bhi curve. Domain ko N chhote tukdon me baanto, har tukde pe ek bump, oonchai = us tukde ke beech me f ki value. Ye ek "seedhi" (staircase) banata hai jo f ke paas hai. Tukde patle karo (N badhao) → staircase f ke aur paas. Yahi UAT ka dil hai.

Bumps NHidden units (2N)Max error (ideal steps), sin on [0, π]
480.3827
8160.1951
16320.0980
32640.0491

Pattern: units double → error lagbhag aadha. Koi bhi ε chahiye? Bas N itna bada lo. (Numbers numpy se verify kiye — har tukde pe beech wali value, sabse buri galti tukde ke kinare pe.)

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

2 sigmoid = 1 bump (khamba). Bahut saare khambe = koi bhi skyline.

10.4 Intuition 2: ReLU ke tukdon se koi bhi curve

Chapter 7 yaad karo: shallow ReLU network ka output ek piecewise-linear function hai — seedhe tukde, aur har hidden unit ek joint (mod) deta hai jahan uska z = 0 hota hai, yaani x = −b/w. Joint ke baad us unit ka slope add ho jaata hai. To curve ko chhote seedhe tukdon se jodo — jaise chakri (polygon) se circle banate hain. Jitne zyada units, utne zyada tukde, utna better fit.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — haath se ek network banao jo [0, 2] pe y = x2 kare

Idea: points x = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 pe x2 = 0, 0.25, 1, 2.25, 4. Inhe seedhi lines se jodo (4 tukde).

  1. Har tukde ka slope: (0.25 − 0)/0.5 = 0.5,  (1 − 0.25)/0.5 = 1.5,  (2.25 − 1)/0.5 = 2.5,  (4 − 2.25)/0.5 = 3.5
  2. Pehla unit ReLU(x) shuru ka slope deta hai: v1 = 0.5
  3. Har joint pe slope kitna badhta hai, wahi us unit ka output weight: v2 = 1.5 − 0.5 = 1,  v3 = 2.5 − 1.5 = 1,  v4 = 3.5 − 2.5 = 1
  4. Network: ŷ = 0.5·ReLU(x) + 1·ReLU(x − 0.5) + 1·ReLU(x − 1) + 1·ReLU(x − 1.5) (hidden weights sab 1, biases 0, −0.5, −1, −1.5)
  5. Check x = 0.75: 0.5(0.75) + 1(0.25) + 0 + 0 = 0.375 + 0.25 = 0.625; sach: 0.752 = 0.5625; error 0.0625
  6. Check x = 2: 0.5(2) + 1(1.5) + 1(1) + 1(0.5) = 1 + 1.5 + 1 + 0.5 = 4 ✓ (exact)

Jawab: 4 ReLU units se max error 0.0625 (tukdon ke beech me). Ye error = h2/4 hai jahan h = tukde ki lambai (0.5). 2 units (h = 1) → 0.25; 8 units (h = 0.25) → 0.015625; 16 units → 0.0039. Units double → error ÷ 4.

PyTorch · haath se set kiya hua shallow ReLU net (weights khud daale)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Hand-made shallow ReLU network jo [0, 2] par x^2 ko 4 seedhe tukdon se approximate kare
class HingeNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.hidden = nn.Linear(1, 4)        # 4 ReLU units, har unit ka ek "joint"
        self.out = nn.Linear(4, 1)
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.hidden.weight.fill_(1.0)                                # sab weights 1
            self.hidden.bias.copy_(torch.tensor([0.0, -0.5, -1.0, -1.5]))  # joints: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5
            self.out.weight.copy_(torch.tensor([[0.5, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]]))    # slope kitna badhe
            self.out.bias.fill_(0.0)

    def forward(self, x):                    # x: (N, 1)
        return self.out(torch.relu(self.hidden(x)))   # (N,1) -> (N,4) -> (N,1)

net = HingeNet()
x = torch.tensor([[0.0], [0.25], [0.5], [0.75], [1.0], [1.5], [1.75], [2.0]])
with torch.no_grad():
    y_hat = net(x)
for xi, yi in zip(x.squeeze().tolist(), y_hat.squeeze().tolist()):
    print(f"x = {xi:4.2f}   net = {yi:6.4f}   x^2 = {xi**2:6.4f}   error = {yi - xi**2:6.4f}")

Output

x = 0.00   net = 0.0000   x^2 = 0.0000   error = 0.0000
x = 0.25   net = 0.1250   x^2 = 0.0625   error = 0.0625
x = 0.50   net = 0.2500   x^2 = 0.2500   error = 0.0000
x = 0.75   net = 0.6250   x^2 = 0.5625   error = 0.0625
x = 1.00   net = 1.0000   x^2 = 1.0000   error = 0.0000
x = 1.50   net = 2.2500   x^2 = 2.2500   error = 0.0000
x = 1.75   net = 3.1250   x^2 = 3.0625   error = 0.0625
x = 2.00   net = 4.0000   x^2 = 4.0000   error = 0.0000

nn.Linear(1, 4) ki weight shape (4, 1) hai (out_features, in_features); .fill_(1.0) sab ko 1 karta hai (underscore = in-place). Joints (0.5, 1, 1.5, aur 0) pe error exactly 0, tukdon ke beech 0.0625.

Training se: zyada hidden units → better fit

Ab weights haath se nahi, gradient descent se. sin(x) on [−π, π], 200 points, shallow ReLU net, Adam (lr = 0.01), 3000 full-batch epochs, sirf hidden units badle:

PyTorch · shallow net, alag widths, sin(x) fit

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

x = torch.linspace(-math.pi, math.pi, 200).unsqueeze(1)   # (200, 1) inputs
y = torch.sin(x)                                           # (200, 1) targets

def fit(hidden_units, epochs=3000):
    torch.manual_seed(0)                                   # har run same tareeke se shuru
    model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, hidden_units),      # 1 hidden layer (shallow)
                          nn.ReLU(),
                          nn.Linear(hidden_units, 1))
    opt = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
    loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
    for epoch in range(epochs):                            # full-batch training
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss = loss_fn(model(x), y)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    return loss.item(), sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())

for h in [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 64]:
    mse, n_params = fit(h)
    print(f"hidden units = {h:3d} | params = {n_params:4d} | final MSE = {mse:.6f}")

Output (real run, CPU)

hidden units =   1 | params =    4 | final MSE = 0.162880
hidden units =   2 | params =    7 | final MSE = 0.162880
hidden units =   4 | params =   13 | final MSE = 0.148979
hidden units =   8 | params =   25 | final MSE = 0.003322
hidden units =  16 | params =   49 | final MSE = 0.000121
hidden units =  64 | params =  193 | final MSE = 0.000189

Trend saaf: 1–2 units → MSE 0.163 (bas ek tedhi line), 8 units → 0.0033, 16 units → 0.00012. Do baatein dhyaan se: (1) H = 4 ka 0.149 — 4 units me kaafi achha fit possible tha, phir bhi training atak gayi (agle section me wajah). (2) H = 64 (0.000189) aur H = 16 (0.000121) dono practically perfect; chhota fark Adam ke aakhri steps ke noise ka hai — capacity kaafi ho jaane ke baad aur units se fit aur better hona zaroori nahi.

Exam Radar

  • Shallow ReLU net = piecewise-linear function; unit i ka joint x = −bi/wi.
  • More units → more pieces → better approximation (UAT ka constructive picture).
  • Sigmoid view: 2 units = 1 bump; ReLU view: 1 unit = 1 joint.

10.5 UAT kya promise NAHI karta

Kahani

Darzi wali guarantee yaad hai? "Kurta fit ban sakta hai." Par: (1) shayad 10 lakh tukde lagein, (2) darzi ko shayad pata hi na chale ki tukde kaise jodne hain, (3) tumhare naap pe bana kurta tumhare bhai pe fit hoga ya nahi — koi guarantee nahi, (4) aur ye bhi nahi bataya ki silai ka koi aur tareeka (layers me banana) kam tukdon me kaam kar deta.

  1. Kitne neurons? Nahi batata. Zaroori neurons astronomically (exponentially) zyada ho sakte hain — khaaskar jab input dimensions zyada hon. Slide: "might need an exponentially large number of neurons (infinite width)."
  2. Training weights dhoondh payegi? Nahi. UAT sirf kehta hai sahi weights exist karte hain (existence proof). Gradient descent unhe dhoondh le — iski koi guarantee nahi (local minima, dead units, bad init).
  3. Generalization? Nahi. Training points pe perfect fit ka matlab naye data pe achha hona nahi — overfitting ho sakta hai (Chapter 18). UAT sirf "fit kar sakta hai" bolta hai, "sahi seekhega" nahi.
  4. Depth? Kuch nahi kehta. Ye nahi kehta ki ek layer best hai; deep networks wahi kaam bahut kam parameters me kar sakte hain (10.7).
  5. Domain ke bahar? Sirf compact (bounded) region pe guarantee. Range ke bahar (extrapolation) koi promise nahi — ReLU net to door jaake seedhi line ban jaata hai.

PyTorch · "weights exist" ≠ "training dhoondh legi" (H = 4)

import math
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim

x = torch.linspace(-math.pi, math.pi, 200).unsqueeze(1)
y = torch.sin(x)

def fit_and_inspect(hidden_units, seed, epochs=3000):
    torch.manual_seed(seed)                               # alag seed = alag random init
    model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, hidden_units), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(hidden_units, 1))
    opt = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
    for _ in range(epochs):
        opt.zero_grad()
        loss = nn.functional.mse_loss(model(x), y)
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
    with torch.no_grad():
        a = torch.relu(model[0](x))                       # (200, H) hidden activations
        dead = (a.sum(dim=0) == 0).sum().item()           # jo unit har x pe 0 de raha hai
    return loss.item(), dead

for seed in [0, 1]:
    mse, dead = fit_and_inspect(4, seed)
    print(f"H = 4, seed = {seed}: final MSE = {mse:.6f}, dead units = {dead}")

Output

H = 4, seed = 0: final MSE = 0.148979, dead units = 1
H = 4, seed = 1: final MSE = 0.005328, dead units = 1

Same architecture (4 units), sirf random init alag: seed 0 → MSE 0.149 (atak gaya), seed 1 → 0.0053 (28 guna better). Dono me ek unit dead ReLU nikla (har x pe output 0 — 9.6). UAT ne kaha tha 4 units kaafi achha kar sakte hain; training ne har baar wo nahi dhoondha. Yahi point #2 hai.

Galti mat karna

  • UAT ≠ learnability theorem. UAT ≠ generalization theorem.
  • "Finite neurons" ka matlab "kam neurons" nahi — finite par bahut bade ho sakte hain.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

UAT: "ho sakta hai" (CAN). Training: "hoga ya nahi" (WILL). Generalization: "naye data pe chalega ya nahi". Teen alag sawaal.

10.6 Linear regions — shallow network kitne tukde bana sakta hai?

ReLU network input space ko linear regions me baant deta hai: har region ke andar function ek seedhi line (ya flat plane) hai, aur regions ki boundaries pe mod. Jitne zyada regions, utna complicated function — regions ki ginti capacity ka ek achha naap hai.

1-D input, ek hidden layer, D ReLU units → at most D + 1 linear regions
Parameters (1 input, 1 output): D weights + D biases + D output weights + 1 output bias = 3D + 1
  • Har unit ka ek joint (x = −b/w). D joints ek line ko zyada se zyada D + 1 tukdon me kaatte hain (jaise ek rassi pe 3 gaanth = 4 tukde).
  • "At most" isliye: do units ka joint same jagah ho, ya joint domain ke bahar ho, to kam regions.
  • Di-dimensional input pe har unit ek hyperplane boundary banata hai; regions at most Σj=0Di C(D, j). Example: 2-D input, 3 units → C(3,0) + C(3,1) + C(3,2) = 1 + 3 + 3 = 7 (teen lines ek kaagaz ko 7 hisson me kaat sakti hain). 2-D, 10 units → 1 + 10 + 45 = 56.

Exam Radar

  • Shallow ReLU net, 1-D input, D units → ≤ D + 1 regions, 3D + 1 parameters. Regions width ke saath sirf linearly badhte hain.

10.7 Depth ka jaadu — composition aur "folding"

Kahani

Ek A4 kaagaz lo. Beech se modo (fold) — 2 parat. Phir modo — 4 parat. Phir — 8. Ab us mude hue kaagaz pe kainchi se ek seedha cut lagao (saari parton ke aar-paar) aur kaagaz khol do. Kitne cut dikhenge? 8! Ek baar ki mehnat, 8 jagah copy. 10 baar modo to ek cut → 1024 cuts. Deep network yahi karta hai: pehli layers input space ko fold karti hain, aur agli layer jo bhi function banati hai wo har fold pe copy ho jaata hai.

Lecture slide (UDL Chapter 4 se): "A way to think about composing networks is that the first network 'folds' the input space x back onto itself. Thus multiple inputs generate the same output. Then the second network applies a function, which is replicated at all points that were folded on top of one another. This allows us to create complex distributions using a combination of layers."

Chalo numbers se samjhein — "tent" fold, sirf 2 ReLU units

Fold function: T(x) = 2·ReLU(x) − 4·ReLU(x − 0.5) on [0, 1].

  1. x = 0.2: 2(0.2) − 4(0) = 0.4
  2. x = 0.8: 2(0.8) − 4(0.3) = 1.6 − 1.2 = 0.4 — same! Fold ho gaya.
  3. x = 0.5: 2(0.5) − 0 = 1; x = 1: 2 − 4(0.5) = 0. T poore [0, 1] ko do baar [0, 1] pe map karta hai (upar jaao, neeche aao) → 2 pieces.
  4. T(T(x)): har half pe poora T dobara → 4 pieces. Teen baar → 8. k layers (har ek me 2 units) → 2k pieces, sirf 2k units.
  5. Shallow network ko 2k pieces ke liye D + 1 ≥ 2k → D ≥ 2k − 1 units chahiye.
  6. k = 10: deep = 20 units → 1024 pieces; shallow ≥ 1023 units. k = 20: deep = 40 units → 1,048,576 pieces; shallow ≥ 1,048,575 units!

Depth ke saath regions exponentially (2k) badhte hain; width ke saath sirf linearly (D + 1).

PyTorch · deep "tent" network, pieces ginti

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class TentLayer(nn.Module):
    """2 ReLU units: T(x) = 2*relu(x) - 4*relu(x - 0.5)  -> [0,1] ko 'fold' karta hai"""
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.hidden = nn.Linear(1, 2)
        self.combine = nn.Linear(2, 1)
        with torch.no_grad():
            self.hidden.weight.copy_(torch.tensor([[1.0], [1.0]]))
            self.hidden.bias.copy_(torch.tensor([0.0, -0.5]))
            self.combine.weight.copy_(torch.tensor([[2.0, -4.0]]))
            self.combine.bias.fill_(0.0)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.combine(torch.relu(self.hidden(x)))

def count_pieces(model):
    x = torch.linspace(0, 1, 2**16 + 1).unsqueeze(1)
    with torch.no_grad():
        y = model(x).squeeze()
    slopes = (y[1:] - y[:-1]) / (x[1:, 0] - x[:-1, 0])
    changes = (slopes[1:] - slopes[:-1]).abs() > 1e-3     # slope kahan badla
    return changes.sum().item() + 1

for depth in [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]:
    deep = nn.Sequential(*[TentLayer() for _ in range(depth)])   # depth baar fold
    units = 2 * depth
    print(f"depth {depth}: ReLU units = {units:2d}, linear pieces = {count_pieces(deep):2d}, "
          f"shallow net needs >= {2**depth - 1} units")

Output

depth 1: ReLU units =  2, linear pieces =  2, shallow net needs >= 1 units
depth 2: ReLU units =  4, linear pieces =  4, shallow net needs >= 3 units
depth 3: ReLU units =  6, linear pieces =  8, shallow net needs >= 7 units
depth 4: ReLU units =  8, linear pieces = 16, shallow net needs >= 15 units
depth 5: ReLU units = 10, linear pieces = 32, shallow net needs >= 31 units
depth 6: ReLU units = 12, linear pieces = 64, shallow net needs >= 63 units

nn.Sequential(*[TentLayer() for _ in range(depth)]) — list ke saare layers ko unpack (*) karke ek ke baad ek jodta hai. Pieces gin ne ke liye 65,537 points pe slope nikala aur dekha slope kitni baar badla. Depth 3 se aage deep network kam units me zyada pieces de raha hai, aur gap exponentially badhta hai.

UDL ka general result (slide "Number of regions vs parameters")

Deep net: 1 input, 1 output, K hidden layers × D units (D > 2) → up to (D + 1)K linear regions
Parameters = 3D + 1 + (K − 1)D(D + 1)
  • 3D + 1: pehli layer (D weights + D biases) + output layer (D weights + 1 bias) — shallow wala hi count
  • (K − 1)D(D + 1): K hidden layers ke beech K − 1 connections; har ek me D × D weights + D biases = D(D + 1)
  • Slide pe agar "(K − 1)D(D − 1)" jaisa dikhe to khud gin ke check karo: D×D weights + D biases = D(D + 1). Example se confirm: K = 5, D = 10 → 471 (UDL Fig 4.7 ka highlighted point), (D − 1) wala formula 391 deta — mismatch.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — same budget, shallow vs deep

  1. Deep, K = 5, D = 10: params = 3(10) + 1 + (5 − 1)(10)(11) = 31 + 440 = 471
  2. Regions: (10 + 1)5 = 115 = 161,051
  3. Shallow with ~471 params: 3D + 1 ≈ 471 → D = 156 (3 × 156 + 1 = 469 params)
  4. Shallow regions: D + 1 = 157

Lagbhag same parameters: shallow 157 regions, deep 161,051 regions — ~1000 guna zyada. (UDL Fig 4.7 ka doosra case: 10 inputs, K = 5, D = 50 → 10,801 parameters aur 1040 se zyada regions.)

"Up to" — ye maximum hai. Trained network me asli regions isse kaafi kam hote hain; lekin potential depth ke saath exponential hai.

10.8 Depth efficiency — kuch functions ke liye shallow ko exponential units chahiye

Depth efficiency: aise functions exist karte hain jinhe deep network thode units/parameters se bana leta hai, lekin shallow network ko unhi ke liye exponentially zyada units chahiye. Tent example isi ka proof tha (2k units vs 2k − 1). Slide: "Depth allows for compositional efficiency. A deep network can represent a function with O(N) parameters that a shallow network would need O(2N) parameters to represent." (Research: Montúfar et al. 2014 — regions; Telgarsky 2016, Eldan & Shamir 2016 — depth separation.)

Face analogy (slide): "It is easier to describe a face as (Eyes + Nose + Mouth) than to describe every pixel coordinate individually." Real-world data compositional hota hai — chhote parts milke bade parts, bade parts milke object. Deep network har layer me ek level upar ka feature banata hai, aur neeche ke features ko reuse karta hai. Shallow network ko har combination alag se yaad rakhna padta hai.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Width = zyada log ek hi floor pe kaam karein (jodna). Depth = assembly line (fold pe fold, guna-guna). Jodna linear, guna exponential.

10.9 Depth vs Width — trade-off

Go Deeper (modern trend)

Pros

  • Zyada expressive per parameter (regions exponential in depth)
  • Hierarchical features: edges → shapes → objects; features reuse
  • Aksar better generalization (UDL: deep networks practice me behtar generalize karte dikhte hain)

Cons

  • Vanishing / exploding gradients: backprop me layer-dar-layer factors multiply (Chapter 13)
  • Harder optimization: loss landscape ulta-pulta, shattered gradients (Chapter 25)
  • Sequential compute: layer 2 tab tak shuru nahi jab tak layer 1 khatam nahi → zyada latency, depth ke across parallel nahi

Ilaaj (baad ke chapters): ReLU (9.6), Batch Norm (Ch 20), achha init — Xavier/He (Ch 21), residual connections — ResNet (Ch 25).

Go Wider

Pros

  • Easier to optimize (slide: "smoother landscape")
  • Parallel / GPU friendly: poori layer ek matrix multiply
  • Zyada capacity per layer, fine-grained details (slide: "Width = Memory/Capacity")
  • Kam data / simple problems pe achha (slide)

Cons

  • Params ~ width²: hidden-to-hidden layer ka D × D; width double → ~4× params
  • Memory zyada
  • Overfitting risk (slide)
  • Compositional functions ke liye inefficient — exponentially units chahiye ho sakte hain

Slide summary: "Go Deeper: Better parameter efficiency. Captures hierarchical structure. Harder to train (Gradient issues). Go Wider: Easier to optimize (smoother landscape). Easier to parallelize (GPU friendly). Risk of overfitting." Slide 35: "Width = Memory/Capacity", slide 36: "Depth = Abstraction".

10.10 Comparison table + parameter counting

AspectDeep (zyada layers)Wide (zyada units/layer)
Regions (1-D ReLU)up to (D + 1)K — exponential in KD + 1 — linear in D
Parameter efficiencyHighLow (params ~ D2)
FeaturesHierarchical, reusable (abstraction)Flat, ek hi level (memory)
OptimizationMushkil (vanishing/exploding)Aasaan (smoother)
Parallelism / latencySequential, zyada latencyParallel, GPU friendly
OverfittingGeneralization aksar betterRisk zyada
Best forImages, speech, text — compositional dataSimple / small tabular problems
Fixes neededReLU, BN, He init, ResNet skipsRegularization (L2, dropout)

Chalo numbers se samjhein — MNIST jaisa input (784 pixels → 10 classes)

Yaad rakho: nn.Linear(in, out) ke params = in × out (weights) + out (biases).

  1. Wide-shallow 784 → 512 → 10: 784 × 512 + 512 = 401,920; 512 × 10 + 10 = 5,130; total 407,050
  2. Deep-narrow 784 → 256 → 256 → 256 → 256 → 10: pehli 784 × 256 + 256 = 200,960
  3. Teen hidden-to-hidden: 3 × (256 × 256 + 256) = 3 × 65,792 = 197,376
  4. Output: 256 × 10 + 10 = 2,570; total 200,960 + 197,376 + 2,570 = 400,906
  5. Width² effect: Linear(256, 256) = 65,792 vs Linear(512, 512) = 512 × 512 + 512 = 262,656 → ≈ 3.99 guna

Jawab: dono ~4 lakh params ke (407,050 vs 400,906), lekin deep wala 4 levels ke features bana sakta hai. Width double karne se hidden-to-hidden params ~4 guna.

Toy 1-D version: 1 → 64 → 1 = 193 params, ≤ 65 regions; 1 → 8 → 8 → 8 → 1 = 169 params (3·8 + 1 + 2·8·9), ≤ 93 = 729 regions. Kam params, ~11 guna zyada regions.

PyTorch · dono networks banao, params gino

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

def count_params(model):
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())   # numel = tensor me kitne numbers

wide_shallow = nn.Sequential(                 # 1 hidden layer, 512 units
    nn.Linear(784, 512), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(512, 10))

deep_narrow = nn.Sequential(                  # 4 hidden layers, 256 units each
    nn.Linear(784, 256), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(256, 256), nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(256, 10))

print("wide-shallow params:", count_params(wide_shallow))
print("deep-narrow  params:", count_params(deep_narrow))

x = torch.randn(32, 784)                      # 32 images, 28*28 = 784 pixels each
print(wide_shallow(x).shape, deep_narrow(x).shape)   # dono (32, 10)

# Width double karo -> hidden-to-hidden params ~4 guna
print("Linear(256,256):", count_params(nn.Linear(256, 256)))
print("Linear(512,512):", count_params(nn.Linear(512, 512)))

Output

wide-shallow params: 407050
deep-narrow  params: 400906
torch.Size([32, 10]) torch.Size([32, 10])
Linear(256,256): 65792
Linear(512,512): 262656
  • model.parameters() saare learnable tensors (weights + biases) deta hai; p.numel() = us tensor me kitne numbers. Sum = total params. Exam me "count params" sawaal isi formula se: in × out + out per Linear layer. ReLU layers ke 0 params.
  • Dono models ka output (32, 10) — architecture alag, interface same.

Architecture design (slide "Designing the architecture" / "Let's play"): teacher ne playground.tensorflow.org dikhaya tha — wahan hidden layers aur neurons badal ke, activation (ReLU/tanh/sigmoid/linear) badal ke dekho ki spiral data pe decision boundary kaise banti hai. Linear activation ke saath kitni bhi layers lagao, boundary seedhi hi rahegi (9.1); ReLU + depth se spiral bhi kat jaata hai.

Exam Radar

  • Width = neurons per layer (D), depth = number of hidden layers (K). Shallow = 1 hidden layer.
  • Shallow 1-D ReLU: ≤ D + 1 regions, 3D + 1 params. Deep: up to (D + 1)K regions, 3D + 1 + (K − 1)D(D + 1) params. K = 5, D = 10 → 471 params, 161,051 regions.
  • Depth = composition = "folding" → regions exponential in depth; width → linear.
  • Depth efficiency: shallow may need O(2N) where deep needs O(N).
  • Deep: + param efficiency, hierarchy, generalization; − vanishing/exploding gradients, hard optimization, latency. Wide: + easy optimization, parallel; − params ~ width², memory, overfitting.
  • Fixes for deep: ReLU, BatchNorm, Xavier/He init, ResNet skip connections.

Galti mat karna

  • Depth = hidden layers ki ginti; input layer ko count mat karo (koi computation nahi karti).
  • "(D + 1)K" maximum hai, guarantee nahi.
  • "Deep hamesha better" — nahi; bina ReLU/BN/init/skip ke bahut deep plain network train hi nahi hota (ResNet ka motivation).
  • Param count me bias bhoolna: Linear(784, 512) = 401,408 + 512 = 401,920, sirf 401,408 nahi.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Width = yaaddasht (memory), Depth = samajh (abstraction). Kaagaz ko k baar fold karo, ek cut lagao, 2k cuts pao.

Chapter 11

Loss Functions — galti ka hisaab-kitaab

Loss vs Cost · Loss landscape · Maximum Likelihood · NLL · MSE · MAE · Huber · Binary & Categorical Cross-Entropy · Hinge · PyTorch loss classes

11.1 Loss function kya hai — teacher ki laal pen

Kahani

Yaad karo school ka maths test. Tumne answer likha, aur Sharma ma'am ne laal pen uthaya. Ma'am sirf "sahi" ya "galat" nahi likhti thi — wo dekhti thi ki kitna galat hai. Asli answer 50 tha aur tumne 49 likha? Bas aadha mark kata. Tumne 500 likh diya? Poore marks gaye, upar se daant bhi padi.

Ab socho ek robot student hai — hamara neural network. Wo bhi har sawaal ka answer guess karta hai. Usko sudharne ke liye ek "laal pen" chahiye jo har guess ko dekh kar ek number de: "itna galat hai tu". Wahi number hai loss, aur jo rule ye number nikaalta hai wo hai loss function. Robot ka poora kaam ek line ka hai: aise weights dhoondho ki ye laal-pen wala number chhota se chhota ho jaaye.

Network ko ek input x milta hai, wo apne weights θ (theta — saare weights aur biases ka ek naam) use karke ek prediction ŷ ("y-hat", matlab "y ka guess") nikaalta hai. Asli answer y hai (isko target ya true label bhi kehte hain). Loss function in dono ko compare karke ek akela number deta hai. Bada number = badi galti. Chhota number = achha guess. Zero = bilkul perfect.

Definition (teacher ki slide se)

A Loss Function L(y, ŷ) is a differentiable scalar that measures the discrepancy between the network's prediction ŷ and the true label y. Training = minimising L by adjusting weights via gradient descent.

Hindi me: loss function ek aisa formula hai jo "prediction aur asli answer me kitna farak hai" ko ek number (scalar) me badal deta hai, aur jiska derivative nikal sakte hain (differentiable), taaki gradient descent us number ko neeche la sake.

Is picture ko dhyaan se dekho, poora deep learning isi loop me hai: x → network → ŷ → loss → gradient → weights update → phir se. Loss function is loop ka compass hai. Agar compass galat direction bataye (galat loss chuna), to network bahut mehnat karke bhi galat cheez seekhega.

Loss vs Cost — ek bachcha vs poori class

Ma'am ek bachche ki copy check karti hai — wo us bachche ka loss hai. Phir wo poori class ka average nikaalti hai — wo cost hai. Bas itna hi farak hai.

ℓi = L(yi, ŷi)      J(θ) = 1n Σi=1n ℓi
  • ℓi = loss — sirf i-th example (ek bachche) ki galti
  • J(θ) = cost (cost function / objective) — saare n examples ki galti ka average; ye weights θ ka function hai, kyunki weights badlo to saare ŷ badlenge
  • n = examples ki ginti (poora dataset ya ek mini-batch)
  • Σ = "sabko jodo" (sum), 1n = "phir n se divide karo" (average)

Average kyun, sum kyun nahi? Kyunki sum lene par 1000 examples wale batch ka number 100 examples wale batch se apne-aap 10 guna bada ho jaata — galti badhi nahi, bas ginti badhi. Average lene se number batch size se independent ho jaata hai, aur learning rate har batch size par same tarah kaam karta hai.

PyTorch · loss (per example) vs cost (average)

import torch

y_true = torch.tensor([3.0, -0.5, 2.0, 7.0])   # asli answers (4 examples)
y_pred = torch.tensor([2.5,  0.0, 2.0, 8.0])   # model ke guesses

per_example = (y_true - y_pred) ** 2   # har example ka apna LOSS
cost = per_example.mean()              # poore batch ka COST = average
print(per_example)
print(cost)

Output

tensor([0.2500, 0.2500, 0.0000, 1.0000])
tensor(0.3750)
Real life me log "loss" aur "cost" ko aksar ek hi matlab me bol dete hain. PyTorch ka nn.MSELoss() bhi default me average (cost) hi deta hai, phir bhi naam "Loss" hai.

Achhe loss function ki khoobiyan

  • Hamesha ≥ 0 — galti negative nahi ho sakti. (Ma'am marks kaat sakti hai, extra marks galti ke liye nahi deti.)
  • Perfect prediction par 0 — ŷ = y ho to loss = 0.
  • Badi galti → bada loss — loss galti ke saath badhna chahiye (monotonic).
  • Differentiable (smooth) — iska derivative nikalna chahiye, kyunki gradient descent ko slope chahiye: wnew = wold − α · ∂L/∂w. (Ye wahi update rule hai jo L2 worksheet me tumne L = ½(ŷ − y)² ke saath haath se chalaya tha.)
  • Ek scalar number — PyTorch me loss.backward() sirf ek single number par chalta hai.
  • Task ke hisaab se sahi — regression (number predict karna) aur classification (category predict karna) ke liye alag loss. Isi chapter ka asli sawaal yahi hai: kaunsa loss kab, aur kyun.

Accuracy ko hi loss kyun nahi bana dete?

Accuracy (kitne sahi) to sabse seedha number hai, usi ko maximize kar do? Problem: accuracy step function jaisi hai. Weight ko thoda sa hilao — prediction 0.61 se 0.62 ho gayi — par class wahi rahi, to accuracy bilkul nahi badli. Matlab accuracy ka slope (gradient) almost har jagah zero hai. L2 worksheet ka Part 3 yaad karo: threshold (step) function ka derivative 0 tha, isliye wnew = wold raha — kuch seekha hi nahi. Accuracy ko loss banaoge to wahi hoga. Isliye hum smooth loss (jaise cross-entropy) se train karte hain, aur accuracy ko sirf metric (report card) ki tarah dekhte hain.

Exam Radar

  • Loss = ek example ki galti; Cost J(θ) = poore dataset/batch ka average. Goal hamesha minimize.
  • Loss function output = scalar, differentiable, ≥ 0, perfect par 0.
  • Training = loss minimize karna gradient descent se; gradient ∇L backprop se aata hai (Chapter 12–13).
  • Course convention: error = prediction − target = ŷ − y (L3 backprop notes: "Always prediction minus target").
  • Accuracy = metric, loss nahi — kyunki uska gradient almost everywhere zero hai.

Galti mat karna

  • PyTorch me argument order: loss_fn(prediction, target). MSE me order se farak nahi padta (square symmetric hai), par BCE / CrossEntropy me order ulta kiya to galat ya error.
  • reduction='none' wala loss ek vector hai; us par seedha .backward() karoge to RuntimeError: grad can be implicitly created only for scalar outputs. Pehle .mean() ya .sum() karo.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Loss = laal pen ka number. Network ka ek hi sapna: laal pen ka number zero ho jaaye.

11.2 Loss landscape — pahad, ghaati aur saddle

Kahani

Socho tum raat ko Himachal ke pahadon me phans gaye ho, ghup andhera, torch bhi nahi. Tumhe neeche ghaati me gaon tak pahunchna hai. Kya karoge? Pair se zameen ka dhalaan (slope) mehsoos karoge aur jidhar dhalaan neeche jaata hai, udhar ek kadam rakhoge. Baar baar. Yahi gradient descent hai. Aur ye pahadi ilaaka? Wo hai loss landscape.

Har possible weights θ ke liye ek loss value hoti hai. Agar weights ko zameen ke coordinates maano aur loss ko uunchaai (altitude), to ek pahadi map ban jaata hai — slide 4 ke shabdon me: "The altitude is the Error. Our goal is to reach the lowest point (Global Minimum)." Is map ko J(θ) bhi likhte hain.

  • Global minimum — poore map ka sabse neecha point. Yahan loss sabse kam hai. Asli manzil.
  • Local minimum — ek chhota gaddha jo aas-paas sabse neecha hai, par poore map me nahi. Gradient descent yahan atak sakta hai, kyunki har taraf chadhaai dikhti hai.
  • Convex landscape — ek kateri (bowl) jaisa: sirf ek hi minimum, koi jhoota gaddha nahi. Kahin se bhi shuru karo, neeche utarte raho, global minimum milega. Example: linear regression + MSE. Kyun? ŷ = wx + b ho to (y − wx − b)² weights ka ek quadratic (parabola/bowl) hai.
  • Non-convex landscape — ubad-khabad, kai gaddhe, plateaus (samtal maidan). Hidden layers wale neural networks ka landscape aisa hi hota hai, chahe loss koi bhi ho.
  • Saddle point — ghode ki kaathi (saddle) jaisa: ek disha (θ1) se dekho to ghaati, doosri disha (θ2) se dekho to pahad ki choti. Wahan slope (gradient) = 0 hai, par wo minimum nahi hai. Gradient descent wahan bahut dheere chalta hai. Bade networks (lakhon dimensions) me asli dushman local minima se zyada saddle points aur plateaus hote hain.

Yahi wajah hai ki aage chal kar hum plain gradient descent se aage badh kar Momentum aur Adam padhenge — jo plateaus aur saddles se nikalne me madad karte hain (slide 35: "Shows why Adam/momentum needed").

Exam Radar

  • Loss landscape = J(θ) parameters ke against; altitude = error; goal = global minimum.
  • Convex → har local minimum hi global minimum hai (koi jhoota gaddha nahi; strictly convex ho to minimum unique bhi), GD hamesha pahunchta hai (sahi learning rate ke saath). Linear regression + MSE convex hai.
  • Neural network ka loss landscape non-convex → local minima, saddle points, plateaus.
  • Saddle point: gradient = 0 par minimum nahi (ek direction me upar, doosri me neeche).
  • Convexity loss + model dono par depend karti hai: sigmoid + BCE (logistic regression) weights me convex hai, par sigmoid + MSE non-convex — classification me CE pasand karne ki ek aur wajah (11.16 dekho).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Andhere pahad me sirf dhalaan mehsoos karke neeche utarna — yahi training. Bowl me raasta pakka, ubad-khabad pahad me atakne ka darr.

11.3 Maximum Likelihood — Bunty ke sikke ki kahani

Kahani

Gully cricket me toss hamesha Bunty ke sikke se hota hai. Aaj sabne gin liya: 10 toss me 7 baar heads, 3 baar tails. Pappu chillaya, "Sikka tedha hai!" Ab sawaal ye hai: is sikke par heads aane ka asli chance p kitna maanein? 0.5 (seedha sikka)? 0.3? 0.9?

Tumhara dimaag turant bolega "0.7, aur kya!" Bilkul sahi. Par ye 0.7 kahaan se aaya? Isi "dimaag ke jugaad" ka proper naam hai Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) — aur yahi poore chapter ki neev hai, kyunki MSE aur cross-entropy dono isi se paida hote hain.

Probability vs Likelihood — ek hi formula, ulta sawaal

Probability

p pata hai (maano 0.5), data abhi aaya nahi. Sawaal: "Is sikke se 7 heads aane ka chance kitna?" — parameter fixed, data variable.

Likelihood

Data aa chuka hai (7 H, 3 T), p pata nahi. Sawaal: "Ye data dekh ke, kaunsa p sabse zyada believable hai?" — data fixed, parameter variable.

i.i.d. — isliye probabilities multiply hoti hain

Har toss independent hai (pichhla toss agle ko affect nahi karta) aur sab toss identically distributed hain (sab ek hi sikke se, same p). Is jodi ko kehte hain i.i.d. (independent and identically distributed). Independent events ka "sab saath me hona" = unki probabilities ka guna (product). Ek heads ka chance p, ek tails ka (1 − p). To hamare 10 tosses ka chance:

L(p) = ∏i=110 P(tossi | p) = p · p · (1 − p) · … = p7 (1 − p)3
  • L(p) = likelihood: "agar heads ka chance p hota, to bilkul yahi data dekhne ka chance kitna"
  • ∏ = "sabko multiply karo" (Σ ka guna wala bhai)
  • p7 = 7 heads, har ek ka chance p; (1 − p)3 = 3 tails, har ek ka chance 1 − p
  • (Agar order ki parwaah na ho to aage ek constant 10C7 = 120 lagta hai. Constant se peak ki jagah nahi badalti, isliye hata dete hain.)

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: p = 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 ke liye L(p) = p7(1 − p)3 nikaalo. Kaunsa p jeetega?

  1. p = 0.3: 0.37 = 0.0002187, 0.73 = 0.343 → L = 0.0002187 × 0.343 = 0.0000750
  2. p = 0.5: 0.57 = 0.0078125, 0.53 = 0.125 → L = 0.0009766
  3. p = 0.7: 0.77 = 0.0823543, 0.33 = 0.027 → L = 0.0022236
  4. p = 0.9: 0.97 = 0.4782969, 0.13 = 0.001 → L = 0.0004783
  5. Compare: 0.0022236 sabse bada. p = 0.7 wala sikka is data ko seedhe sikke (0.5) se 0.0022236 / 0.0009766 ≈ 2.28 guna zyada achhe se explain karta hai.

Jawab: p = 0.7 likelihood ko maximum karta hai. Yahi MLE hai.

Derivative se pakka saboot

Sirf 4 values try karna proof nahi hai. Peak nikalne ka tareeka: derivative = 0 rakho (Chapter 2 wala "slope zero = top ya bottom").

Derivation step by step

  1. Seedha L ko differentiate karo (product rule): dL/dp = 7p6(1 − p)3 − 3p7(1 − p)2 = p6(1 − p)2 [7(1 − p) − 3p]. Kaam chal gaya par gandagi dekho — 10 cheezon ka guna hota to aur bura.
  2. Smart tareeka: pehle ln lo (agle section me iski wajah aur detail): ln L = 7 ln p + 3 ln(1 − p)
  3. Differentiate (yaad hai d/dp ln p = 1/p, aur chain rule se d/dp ln(1 − p) = −1/(1 − p)): d(ln L)/dp = 7/p − 3/(1 − p)
  4. Zero rakho: 7/p = 3/(1 − p) → 7(1 − p) = 3p → 7 − 7p = 3p → 7 = 10p → p = 0.7
  5. Maximum hi hai, minimum nahi? Second derivative: −7/p2 − 3/(1 − p)2 < 0 hamesha → ulta U (∩) → peak. ✓

General rule: sikke ke liye MLE p̂ = heads ki ginti / total tosses = 7/10. Jo dimaag ne bola, maths ne prove kiya.

Definition
