Kaunsa loss kab? (slide 34 ka decision tree)

  • Number predict karna (regression), outliers kam / badi galti mehngi → MSE (mean predictor, smooth gradient). Output layer linear.
  • Regression, outliers / noisy data, ya error original unit me samajhna hai → MAE (median predictor, robust).
  • Regression, pakka nahi ki outlier noise hai ya asli → Huber / Smooth L1.
  • 2 classes (binary) → BCE: nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss (logits) ya sigmoid + nn.BCELoss. Labels 0/1 float.
  • K classes, har example ki ek class (multi-class) → Categorical CE: nn.CrossEntropyLoss (logits + long indices).
  • Ek example ki kai classes saath me sahi ho sakti hain (multi-label, jaise photo me "dog" bhi aur "car" bhi) → har class ka alag binary sawaal → nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss with (N, C) float multi-hot targets.
  • Margin-based, SVM-style, ±1 labels → Hinge.

Exam Radar — poore chapter ke "pakke" facts

  • Loss = ek example; cost = average. Loss scalar, ≥ 0, differentiable. Goal minimize.
  • MLE: likelihood = i.i.d. probabilities ka product; log se sum (underflow se bachao); minus se NLL; maximize likelihood ⟺ minimize NLL.
  • Coin 7/10 heads → MLE p = 0.7 (L = 0.0022236 vs 0.0009766 at 0.5).
  • Gaussian → MSE; Laplace → MAE; Bernoulli → BCE; Categorical → CCE.
  • MSE optimal = mean; MAE optimal = median. MSE outlier-sensitive; MAE robust.
  • ∂MSE/∂ŷ = (2/n)(ŷ − y); ∂MAE/∂ŷ = sign(ŷ − y)/n; ∂BCE/∂ŷ = (ŷ − y)/(ŷ(1 − ŷ)); sigmoid+BCE aur softmax+CE: ∂/∂z = ŷ − y.
  • Sigmoid + MSE: gradient me σ′(z) (max 0.25) → confident galti par vanishing → classification me CE.
  • BCE at ŷ = 0.5: 0.6931 (ln 2). CE untrained K-class: ≈ ln K (10 → 2.3026).
  • −ln 0.9 = 0.1054, −ln 0.5 = 0.6931, −ln 0.1 = 2.3026, −ln 0.01 = 4.6052, −ln 0.7 = 0.3567.
  • Example yaad: y = [3, −0.5, 2, 7], ŷ = [2.5, 0, 2, 8] → MSE 0.375, MAE 0.5, RMSE 0.6124, Huber(δ=1) 0.1875.
  • Logits [2, 1, 0.1], class 0 → softmax [0.6590, 0.2424, 0.0986] → CE 0.4170.
  • nn.CrossEntropyLoss = LogSoftmax + NLLLoss; logits (N, C) + long (N,). nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss = Sigmoid + BCELoss (stable). nn.BCELoss log ko −100 par clamp.
  • Default reduction='mean' sab losses me. nn.L1Loss = MAE. HuberLoss default δ = 1.0, SmoothL1Loss default β = 1.0.

Galti mat karna — master list

  • Softmax ke baad CrossEntropyLoss → double softmax, koi error nahi, loss floor (3 classes: 0.5514), slow/stuck training. Logits seedha do.
  • Galat target dtype: CrossEntropyLoss/NLLLoss ko long chahiye (float → "expected target dtype to be Long…"); BCELoss/BCEWithLogitsLoss ko float chahiye (long → BCELoss: "Found dtype Long but expected Float"; BCEWithLogitsLoss: "result type Float can't be cast to the desired output type Long").
  • BCELoss ko logits → "all elements of input should be between 0 and 1". BCEWithLogitsLoss ko probabilities (ya model me sigmoid + WithLogits) → double sigmoid, chupchaap galat (Lab 4).
  • Shape mismatch broadcasting: (N, 1) vs (N,) — MSELoss/L1Loss warning ke saath (N, N) bana ke galat loss (0.3144 vs 0.0700); BCE family ValueError. Fix .view(-1, 1) / .squeeze(1) (Lab 5).
  • CE target (N, 1) → "0D or 1D target tensor expected". CE ko (N,) chahiye, BCE ko (N, 1) jaisa output-shape — ulta yaad mat karna.
  • NLLLoss ko probabilities → negative loss bakwaas. Pehle log_softmax.
  • Regression output par sigmoid lagaya aur target 1 se bada → model kabhi pahunch nahi paayega.
  • Classification ke liye MSE → σ′ wala vanishing gradient, non-convex. CE use karo.
  • From-scratch BCE/CE me clamp/log_softmax bhoolna → log(0) = −inf → nan.
  • reduction='none' par seedha backward() → "grad can be implicitly created only for scalar outputs".
  • Argument order: loss_fn(prediction, target).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Number → MSE/MAE (linear output). Haan/na → BCEWithLogits (float target, same shape). Kai me se ek → CrossEntropy (logits + long index). Margin → Hinge. Aur sab ke peeche ek hi maa: MLE → NLL.

Chapter 12

Computational Graph, Chain Rule, Forward & Backward Pass — galti ka hisaab peeche tak

Gradient kyun · Derivative refresher · Computational graph · Local × Upstream · Chain rule (single + multivariable) · Gate patterns · Sigmoid neuron graph · Forward vs Backward pass · PyTorch autograd

12.1 Gradient kyun chahiye? — kaunsa knob, kis taraf, kitna

Kahani

Yaad hai apna chai wala? Uski chai me teen "knobs" hain: cheeni kitni, patti kitni, doodh kitna. Customer ek sip leta hai aur muh bana ke bolta hai: "Bhaiya, maza nahi aaya, 10 me se 4." Ye "kitna bura laga" wala number hi hamara loss hai.

Ab chai wale ke paas teen sawaal hain:

  • Kaunsa knob? — Galti cheeni ki hai, patti ki, ya doodh ki? (kis cheez ka asar sabse zyada hai)
  • Kis taraf? — Cheeni badhaun ya ghataun?
  • Kitna? — Ek chammach ya aadha chammach?

Agar wo andaaze se har knob ghumata rahe, to 100 customer kharab ho jayenge. Lekin agar koi use bata de: "cheeni ko thoda badhane se rating itni badhegi, patti badhane se itni ghategi" — to wo seedha sahi taraf, sahi matra me knob ghuma dega. Yahi "kis knob ko thoda hilane se loss kitna hilta hai" wali jaankari ka naam hai gradient.

Neural network me ye knobs hain weights (w) aur biases (b) — ek chhote network me 9, ek bade model me crore. Loss function (Chapter 11) batata hai "kitna galat". Training ka matlab hai: knobs ko aise ghumao ki loss kam ho. Aur har knob ke liye "kis taraf, kitna" ka jawab deta hai us knob ka partial derivative ∂L/∂w.

Definition

Gradient = loss ke saare partial derivatives ki list (vector), har parameter ke liye ek: ∇L = [∂L/∂w1, ∂L/∂w2, …, ∂L/∂b]. Har entry batati hai: "ye ek knob thoda sa badhao (baaki sab same rakho) to loss kitni rate se badlega".

Gradient ki ek entry teen sawaalon ka jawab ek saath deti hai:

SawaalGradient se jawabExample: ∂L/∂w = −4
Kaunsa knob zyada important?Jiska |∂L/∂w| bada, uska asar bada|−4| = 4, kaafi asar hai
Kis taraf ghumaun?Sign ke ulta: gradient negative → w badhao; positive → w ghatao−4 negative hai → w badhao
Kitna ghumaun?Step = learning rate × gradientη = 0.1 → step = 0.4
wnew = wold − η · ∂L∂w
  • wold = abhi ka weight (knob ki abhi ki position)
  • ∂L/∂w = gradient: w ko thoda badhane par loss kitni tezi se badhta hai (slope)
  • η (eta, kabhi α bhi likhte hain) = learning rate: ek baar me kitna bada kadam lena hai
  • Minus kyun? Gradient "uphill" (loss badhne wali) direction batata hai. Hume loss ghatana hai, isliye ulti taraf chalte hain. Isi liye naam hai gradient descent (utarna).

Ye update rule detail me Chapter 14 me aayega. Is chapter ka kaam hai: ye ∂L/∂w nikalte kaise hain — har weight ke liye, efficiently. Us tareeke ka naam hai backpropagation.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: Maan lo loss sirf ek knob pe depend karta hai: L(w) = (w − 3)2 + 1. Abhi w = 1 hai. Gradient se batao kis taraf jaana hai, aur η = 0.1 se ek step lo.

  1. Abhi ka loss: L(1) = (1 − 3)2 + 1 = 4 + 1 = 5
  2. Derivative (power rule + chain rule): dL/dw = 2(w − 3)
  3. w = 1 pe slope: 2(1 − 3) = −4 → negative hai, matlab w badhane se loss ghatega. To w badhao.
  4. Update: wnew = 1 − 0.1 × (−4) = 1 + 0.4 = 1.4
  5. Naya loss: L(1.4) = (1.4 − 3)2 + 1 = 2.56 + 1 = 3.56

Jawab: loss 5 → 3.56 ho gaya. Sirf slope ka sign aur size dekh ke sahi taraf chale. Agar w = 5 hota to slope = 2(5 − 3) = +4 hota → w ghatana padta.

Teacher ke Lecture 4 slides isi sawaal se shuru hote hain: "Why do we even care about the derivatives of the loss?" Jawab: derivatives batate hain ki parameters me chhota sa change karne par loss kitna badlega; optimization algorithm (jaise SGD) isi jaankari se better parameters dhoondhta hai; aur backpropagation algorithm ye derivatives compute karta hai. Slides me network ko aise likha hai: h1 = a[β0 + Ω0x], h2 = a[β1 + Ω1h1], h3 = a[β2 + Ω2h2], f = β3 + Ω3h3 (β = bias vectors, Ω = weight matrices, a[•] = activation). SGD update ke liye har layer k ke har βk aur Ωk ka derivative, batch ke har example i ke liye chahiye. Lakhon parameters × har step — isliye ek efficient tareeka chahiye. Wahi backprop hai.

Exam Radar

  • Gradient = vector of partial derivatives of the loss w.r.t. every parameter. Direction of steepest increase of loss; hum negative gradient ki taraf chalte hain.
  • Sign → direction; magnitude → kitna sensitive. Gradient 0 → flat point (minimum / maximum / saddle).
  • Backpropagation gradient compute karta hai; gradient descent (optimizer) us gradient se weights update karta hai. Do alag kaam.
  • Teacher ki slide notation: βk = bias vector, Ωk = weight matrix, ϕ = {β0, Ω0, …, β3, Ω3} = saare parameters (Prince UDL book wali notation).

Galti mat karna

  • "Backprop weights update karta hai" — MCQ me ye trap ho sakta hai. Strictly: backprop sirf ∂L/∂w nikalta hai; update optimizer.step() (gradient descent) karta hai. (Teacher ki slide loosely kehti hai "backprop updates weights to minimize the loss" — matlab poora training process; agar option me "computes gradients" alag se diya ho, wahi zyada sahi hai.)
  • Gradient positive hai to weight ghatega (minus sign ki wajah se). Ulta mat padhna.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Gradient = knob ka GPS: sign bole "kidhar", size bole "kitna zor se". Hum hamesha ulti taraf chalte hain, kyunki pahaad se neeche utarna hai.

12.2 Derivative refresher — "thoda sa hilao, kitna hila?"

Kahani

Auto-rickshaw ka meter socho. Tum 1 km aur chale to meter ₹15 aur badha. To "fare ka distance ke saath derivative" = ₹15 per km. Derivative bas itna hai: input ko thoda sa badhao, output kitne guna badha? Rate of change. Speedometer bhi yahi hai — distance ka time ke saath derivative.

Lecture slide ki line yaad rakho: "A derivative tells us: if I change the input slightly, how much does the output change?" Isko formula me likhte hain:

dfdx ≈ f(x + h) − f(x)h   (h bahut chhota, jaise 0.0001)
  • h = input ko kitna hilaya (nudge)
  • f(x + h) − f(x) = output kitna hila
  • Dono ka ratio = "per unit input change, output change" = slope. h → 0 karne par ye exact derivative ban jata hai.
  • Central difference (zyada accurate): [f(x + h) − f(x − h)] / 2h. Isi se "gradient checking" karte hain — backprop ka answer sahi hai ya nahi, ye verify karne ke liye.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: f(x) = 3x2 − 4x + 5. (Ye wahi famous example hai jo Karpathy ke micrograd lecture me hai; teacher ki slide ka "x = 2/3 pe derivative ≈ 0, wahi minimum" wala point isi tarah ka function hai.) x = 3 pe slope kya hai? Aur minimum kahan hai?

  1. Value: f(3) = 3(9) − 12 + 5 = 27 − 12 + 5 = 20
  2. Numerically hilao, h = 0.0001: f(3.0001) = 20.00140003 → (20.00140003 − 20) / 0.0001 = 14.0003
  3. Formula se (power rule: d(xn)/dx = nxn−1): f′(x) = 6x − 4 → f′(3) = 18 − 4 = 14. Numeric 14.0003 ≈ 14. Match!
  4. Minimum kahan? Jahan slope 0: 6x − 4 = 0 → x = 4/6 = 2/3 ≈ 0.6667

Jawab: x = 3 pe slope 14 (yahan x badhao to f 14 guna tezi se badhega). x = 2/3 pe slope 0 → wahi minimum. Bilkul slide wali baat: "at x = 2/3 = 0.6667 the derivative is ≈ 0; this is where the function has a minimum."

Python · numerical derivative (Karpathy / Lecture 4 style)

# numerical derivative: "thoda hilao, dekho kitna hila"
def f(x):
    return 3*x**2 - 4*x + 5

h = 0.0001
x = 3.0
print("f(3)          =", f(x))
print("slope (numeric)=", (f(x + h) - f(x)) / h)          # one-sided
print("slope (central)=", (f(x + h) - f(x - h)) / (2*h))  # zyada accurate
print("slope at 2/3  =", (f(2/3 + h) - f(2/3 - h)) / (2*h))

Output

f(3)          = 20.0
slope (numeric)= 14.000300000063248
slope (central)= 14.000000000038426
slope at 2/3  = 0.0

Partial derivative — baaki sab ko freeze karo

Jab function me kai variables hon, jaise f(a, b) = a · b, to ∂f/∂a (padho "del f by del a") ka matlab: sirf a ko hilao, b ko constant maan lo. Yahan ∂f/∂a = b aur ∂f/∂b = a. Symbol "∂" (curly d) bas yaad dilata hai ki aur bhi variables hain jo freeze kiye gaye hain.

Backprop me hume sirf chhote-chhote operations ke derivatives yaad hone chahiye. Ye rahi poori "local derivative" ki potli:

OperationForwardLocal derivative
Addz = x + y∂z/∂x = 1, ∂z/∂y = 1
Multiplyz = x · y∂z/∂x = y, ∂z/∂y = x
Add constantz = x + c1
Scale by constantz = axa
Squarez = x22x
Exponentialz = exex
Reciprocalz = 1/x−1/x2
Logz = ln x1/x
Sigmoidz = σ(x)σ(x)(1 − σ(x)), max 0.25 at x = 0
Tanhz = tanh(x)1 − tanh2(x), max 1 at x = 0
ReLUz = max(0, x)1 if x > 0, else 0
Maxz = max(x, y)1 for the bigger one, 0 for the other
Half squared errorL = ½(ŷ − y)2∂L/∂ŷ = ŷ − y

Exam Radar

  • Derivative = rate of change = slope of tangent. Slope 0 → minimum/maximum/saddle point.
  • Numerical gradient (finite difference) ek check ke liye accha hai, lekin training ke liye slow hai: har parameter ke liye alag forward pass chahiye. Backprop saare gradients ek hi backward pass me deta hai.
  • Central difference error ~h2, one-sided error ~h → central zyada accurate.
  • σ′ ka max = 0.25 (at 0); tanh′ ka max = 1 (at 0); ReLU′ = 1 for positive input. Ye teen numbers vanishing gradient (13.6) ki jaan hain.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Derivative = "kitna hilaya" ke upar "kitna hila". Partial derivative = baaki sabko pause karke sirf ek ko hilao.

12.3 Computational graph — factory ki assembly line

Kahani

Ek biscuit factory socho. Assembly line pe har worker ka ek hi chhota kaam hai: pehla aata aur cheeni milata hai, doosra ghee daalta hai, teesra shape kaatta hai, chautha bake karta hai, paanchva pack karta hai. Box line pe aage badhta jaata hai — ye hai forward direction.

Ab customer complaint karta hai: "biscuit bahut meetha hai!" Manager complaint ko ulti taraf bhejta hai: packing wale se baker, baker se shape wala, ... aur har worker sirf ye sochta hai: "mere chhote se kaam ne is complaint me kitna hissa dala?" Kisi worker ko poori factory samajhne ki zaroorat nahi — sirf apna kaam. Relay race jaisa: baton ek haath se doosre haath tak jaata hai.

Computational graph yahi factory line hai, aur backprop yahi complaint ko peeche bhejne ka tareeka.

Definition

Computational graph = kisi bhi calculation ka naksha (graph), jisme nodes = operations (+, ×, σ, exp, ...) aur edges = values (numbers/tensors) jo ek operation se nikal ke agle operation me jaati hain. Inputs aur parameters (x, w, b) graph ke shuruaati "leaf" points hote hain, aur end me ek single number — loss L. Ye ek DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) hai: arrows ek hi direction me, koi loop nahi.

Teacher ki slide ka example: f = xy + zk. Variables hain x, y, z, k. Hum do intermediate variables banate hain: r = x · y aur s = z · k (dono × operator se), phir final node f = r + s (+ operator se).

Itna tod-phod kyun? Kyunki f ka seedha derivative nikalna mushkil lag sakta hai, lekin har chhote node ka derivative bachpan wala hai: × ka derivative "doosra input", + ka derivative "1". Graph me har node sirf apna chhota sa local derivative jaanta hai, aur chain rule (12.6) un sabko jod deta hai. Neural network bhi bas ek bahut bada computational graph hai: matmul → add bias → activation → matmul → ... → loss.

Exam Radar

  • Nodes = operations, edges = values (tensors). Graph = DAG (no cycles).
  • Forward pass graph ko left → right (inputs → loss) chalata hai; backward pass right → left (loss → inputs).
  • PyTorch ka graph dynamic hai ("define-by-run"): har forward pass me naya graph banta hai, isliye Python ka if/for model ke andar chal jata hai. Purana TensorFlow 1.x static graph ("define-and-run") use karta tha.
  • Course orientation slide: "We don't just call libraries; we implement the computational graph to verify our mathematical intuition."

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Graph = assembly line. Har worker (node) ek chhota kaam, ek chhota derivative. Complaint (gradient) ulti line me travel karti hai.

12.4 Classic worked graph: f = (x + y) · z

Kahani

Cricket ka hisaab: do openers ne runs banaye x aur y; dono ka total q = x + y. Phir ek "multiplier" z lagta hai (jaise koi bonus/penalty factor). Final score f = q · z. Sawaal: agar x ek run zyada banata, to final score kitna badalta? Yahi backward pass batayega.

Ye cs231n (Stanford) ka classic example hai: f(x, y, z) = (x + y) · z at x = −2, y = 5, z = −4. Graph me do nodes: ek add node jo q = x + y banata hai, aur ek multiply node jo f = q · z banata hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Forward pass (left se right, values nikalo aur yaad rakho):

  1. Add node: q = x + y = −2 + 5 = 3
  2. Multiply node: f = q · z = 3 × (−4) = −12

Backward pass (right se left, gradients nikalo):

  1. Shuruaat hamesha 1 se: ∂f/∂f = 1 (f ko 1 badhao to f 1 badhega — obviously)
  2. Multiply node ke local derivatives: ∂f/∂z = q = 3 aur ∂f/∂q = z = −4
  3. Add node ke local derivatives: ∂q/∂x = 1, ∂q/∂y = 1
  4. Chain rule se x tak: ∂f/∂x = ∂f/∂q × ∂q/∂x = (−4) × 1 = −4
  5. Usi tarah y: ∂f/∂y = (−4) × 1 = −4

Jawab: ∂f/∂x = −4, ∂f/∂y = −4, ∂f/∂z = 3. Matlab: x ko thoda badhao to f 4 guna tezi se ghatega; z ko badhao to f 3 guna tezi se badhega.

Check by nudging: x = −1.999 (0.001 badhaya) → q = 3.001 → f = 3.001 × (−4) = −12.004. Change = −0.004 = −4 × 0.001. Bilkul gradient jaisa!

Galti mat karna

  • Backward pass ki shuruaat output pe gradient 1 se hoti hai (∂f/∂f = 1), 0 se nahi.
  • Multiply node pe gradient "apna hi input" nahi, doosre input ka value hota hai: ∂f/∂z = q (z nahi).
  • Forward values yaad rakhna zaroori hai — multiply node ko backward me q aur z dono ki value chahiye. Isliye forward pass values cache karta hai.

12.5 Local gradient × Upstream gradient = Downstream gradient

Kahani

Shaadi me khaana pass karne ki line socho. Har insaan ke paas sirf ek chhoti si jaankari hai: "main jo plate aage bhejta hoon, wo mere haath me aayi plate ka kitna guna hai" (local rule). Backward me jab "complaint ka number" peeche aata hai, har insaan bas itna karta hai: aaya hua number × apna local rule, aur peeche pass. Kisi ko poori line samajhne ki zaroorat nahi.

Graph ke kisi bhi node ko dekho: inputs x, y aate hain, output z = g(x, y) jaata hai. Backward pass me ye node teen cheezein handle karta hai:

  • Upstream gradient ∂L/∂z — aage (loss ki taraf) se aaya hua gradient. "Mere output ne loss ko kitna hilaya?"
  • Local gradient ∂z/∂x — node ka apna derivative, sirf forward ki values se nikalta hai. Isko poore network ka kuch pata nahi hota.
  • Downstream gradient ∂L/∂x — jo peeche bhejna hai.
∂L∂x = ∂L∂z × ∂z∂x     i.e.   downstream = upstream × local
  • ∂L/∂z = upstream: z ka loss pe asar (peeche ki taraf aa raha hai)
  • ∂z/∂x = local: x ka z pe asar (node ka apna formula)
  • ∂L/∂x = downstream: x ka loss pe asar = dono asar ka product. Ye chain rule hi hai, bas har node pe ek-ek kadam.

12.4 ke graph me dekho: add node pe upstream = ∂f/∂q = −4, local = ∂q/∂x = 1, to downstream = −4 × 1 = −4. Multiply node pe upstream = 1, local (for z) = q = 3, to downstream = 3.

Teacher ki slide ka example: L = ((a · b) + c) · f

Lecture 4 slide 7–9 me ye graph hai: a, b, c, f inputs, L final output ("think: Loss"). Slide ke answers: ∂L/∂a = 6.0, ∂L/∂b = −4.0, ∂L/∂c = −2.0, ∂L/∂f = 4.0. Ye chaar gradients sirf ek hi set of values se aate hain: a = 2, b = −3, c = 10, f = −2 (Karpathy micrograd wale same numbers). Chalo khud nikaalte hain.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Intermediate names: e = a · b, d = e + c, L = d · f.

Forward:

  1. e = 2 × (−3) = −6
  2. d = −6 + 10 = 4
  3. L = 4 × (−2) = −8

Backward (upstream × local, har node pe):

  1. Start: ∂L/∂L = 1
  2. Multiply node L = d · f: ∂L/∂f = 1 × d = 4, ∂L/∂d = 1 × f = −2
  3. Add node d = e + c (local = 1): ∂L/∂c = −2 × 1 = −2, ∂L/∂e = −2 × 1 = −2
  4. Multiply node e = a · b: ∂L/∂a = −2 × b = −2 × (−3) = 6, ∂L/∂b = −2 × a = −2 × 2 = −4

Jawab: ∂L/∂a = 6, ∂L/∂b = −4, ∂L/∂c = −2, ∂L/∂f = 4 — slide se exact match.

Slide 9 ka matlab: "a ko 1 badhao to L lagbhag 6 badhega; b ko 1 badhao to L 4 ghatega" (chhote change ke liye linear andaaza). L ghatana ho to har input ko uske gradient ki ulti taraf hilao: a ghatao, b badhao, c badhao, f ghatao. Step 0.01 lo:

a = 2 − 0.01(6) = 1.94   b = −3 − 0.01(−4) = −2.96   c = 10 − 0.01(−2) = 10.02   f = −2 − 0.01(4) = −2.04
L = (1.94 × (−2.96) + 10.02) × (−2.04) = (−5.7424 + 10.02) × (−2.04) = 4.2776 × (−2.04)
= −8.7263   (pehle −8 tha → L ghat gaya)

PyTorch · slide example verify

import torch
# Teacher ka slide example: L = ((a*b) + c) * f
a = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)
b = torch.tensor(-3.0, requires_grad=True)
c = torch.tensor(10.0, requires_grad=True)
f = torch.tensor(-2.0, requires_grad=True)

e = a * b          # -6
d = e + c          #  4
L = d * f          # -8
L.backward()       # poora backward pass ek line me
print("L =", L.item())
print("dL/da =", a.grad.item(), "| dL/db =", b.grad.item())
print("dL/dc =", c.grad.item(), "| dL/df =", f.grad.item())

Output

L = -8.0
dL/da = 6.0 | dL/db = -4.0
dL/dc = -2.0 | dL/df = 4.0

Exam Radar

  • Downstream gradient = upstream gradient × local gradient. Har node sirf local computation karta hai — isi wajah se backprop modular aur fast hai.
  • Gradient ka matlab (slide 9): "∂L/∂a = 6 → a ko 1 badhao to L ~6 badhega". Negative gradient → badhane se L ghatega.
  • L kam karne ke liye: har variable = variable − (step × gradient).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

"Aaya hua × apna = aage bhejo." Upstream × local = downstream. Bas yahi ek line poora backprop hai.

12.6 Chain rule (single variable) — gears aur currency conversion

Kahani

Tum US trip se lautkar dollars ko yen me badalna chahte ho, lekin counter pe seedha rate nahi hai. Maan lo rate hai: 1 dollar = 80 rupaye, aur 1 rupaya = 2 yen. To 1 dollar = 80 × 2 = 160 yen. Rates multiply hote hain.

Cycle ke gears bhi aise hi: pedal wala gear 1 ghoomta hai to beech wala 3 baar, aur beech wala 1 ghoome to pichhla pahiya 4 baar → pedal ke 1 chakkar pe pahiya 3 × 4 = 12 chakkar. Chain rule ka poora funda yahi hai: ek ke baad ek jude hue badlaav ki rates ko multiply karo.

agar y = f(u) aur u = g(x)  ⇒  dydx = dydu · dudx
  • du/dx = x badalne se u kitni rate se badla (pehla gear / dollar → rupee rate)
  • dy/du = u badalne se y kitni rate se badla (doosra gear / rupee → yen rate)
  • Lambi chain ho to: dL/dx = dL/dun · dun/dun−1 · … · du1/dx — har link ka product. Neural network me ye chain layer-dar-layer lambi hoti hai.
  • Fraction jaisa dikhta hai: du "cancel" hota hua lagta hai. Yaad rakhne ki trick ke liye ye theek hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: y = (3x + 1)2. x = 2 pe dy/dx nikalo — chain rule se.

  1. Andar wala tukda naam do: u = 3x + 1 = 3(2) + 1 = 7, phir y = u2 = 49
  2. Bahar wala link: dy/du = 2u = 2 × 7 = 14
  3. Andar wala link: du/dx = 3
  4. Multiply: dy/dx = 14 × 3 = 42
  5. Nudge se check (h = 0.001): (3 × 2.001 + 1)2 = 7.0032 = 49.042009 → (49.042009 − 49) / 0.001 = 42.009 ≈ 42

Jawab: dy/dx = 42 at x = 2.

Neural network wala version: ek neuron ka output ŷ = σ(z), z = wx + b, loss L = ½(ŷ − y)2. To w se L tak ki chain: w → z → ŷ → L, aur

∂L∂w = ∂L∂ŷ · ∂ŷ∂z · ∂z∂w = (ŷ − y) · σ(z)(1 − σ(z)) · x
  • (ŷ − y) = "loss output ko kaise mehsoos karta hai" (½ aur square ka 2 cancel)
  • σ(z)(1 − σ(z)) = "output sum ko kaise mehsoos karta hai" (sigmoid ka slope)
  • x = "sum weight ko kaise mehsoos karta hai" (weight ka partner input)

Ye exactly Lab 2 ka "manual chain rule vs autograd" wala calculation hai: x = 2, w = 1, b = 0, target 0 → z = 2, ŷ = 0.880797, σ′ = 0.104994, ∂L/∂w = 0.880797 × 0.104994 × 2 = 0.184956, aur α = 0.5 se wnew = 1 − 0.5 × 0.184956 = 0.907522.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Chain rule = conversion rates ka product. Jitni lambi chain, utne factors multiply — aur yahi baad me vanishing/exploding ka raaz banega.

12.7 Multivariable chain rule — saare raaston ka total

Kahani

Chai wala chai ka daam p badhata hai. Profit pe asar do raaston se aata hai: (1) har cup pe margin badha (accha), (2) customer thode kam aaye (bura). Total asar = raasta 1 ka asar + raasta 2 ka asar. Ek raasta ignore kiya to hisaab galat. Jab ek variable kai raaston se output tak pahunchta hai, har raaste ka product nikalo aur sabko JODO.

agar f = f(u, v),  u = u(x),  v = v(x)  ⇒  dfdx = ∂f∂ududx + ∂f∂vdvdx
  • Pehla term = raasta 1 (x → u → f) ke links ka product
  • Doosra term = raasta 2 (x → v → f) ke links ka product
  • General rule: ∂L/∂x = Σ (over all paths from x to L) ∏ (local derivatives along that path)
  • Neural net me: ek hidden neuron kai output neurons ko feed karta hai → uska gradient = sab outputs se aaye gradients ka sum. Yahi WTδ wale formula me "sum" ban ke aata hai (13.4).

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: x = 2. Do branches: u = x2, v = 3x, aur f = u · v. df/dx nikalo.

  1. Forward: u = 4, v = 6, f = 4 × 6 = 24
  2. Multiply node ke local gradients: ∂f/∂u = v = 6, ∂f/∂v = u = 4
  3. Raasta 1 (via u): ∂f/∂u × du/dx = 6 × 2x = 6 × 4 = 24
  4. Raasta 2 (via v): ∂f/∂v × dv/dx = 4 × 3 = 12
  5. Jodo: df/dx = 24 + 12 = 36
  6. Check: f = x2 · 3x = 3x3 → f′ = 9x2 = 9 × 4 = 36. Match!

Jawab: df/dx = 36. Agar sirf ek raasta lete to 24 ya 12 aata — dono galat.

Galti mat karna

  • Ek path pe links ko multiply; alag-alag paths ko add. Ulta karna sabse common galti hai.
  • Agar ek weight/neuron ka output do jagah use hua, to dono jagah se aaye gradients jodne hain — ek bhool gaye to gradient adhoora.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

"Raaste ke andar guna, raaston ke beech jod." (Along a path multiply, across paths add.)

12.8 Gate patterns — add = distributor, multiply = swapper, max = router, copy = adder

Kahani

Factory me chaar type ke worker hain, aur complaint (gradient) aane par har type ka reaction fix hai:

  • Add worker = mithai baantne wala: jo aaya, sabko barabar poora de deta hai (distributor).
  • Multiply worker = jodi wala: apne partner ki value se scale karke deta hai — x ko y milta hai, y ko x (swapper).
  • Max worker = traffic police: poora gradient sirf us raaste ko bhejta hai jo forward me jeeta tha; baaki ko 0 (router).
  • Copy/branch = ek hi cheez do jagah gayi: dono jagah se aayi complaints jud jaati hain (adder).
GateForwardBackward (upstream = g)Yaad rakhne ka naam
Addz = x + y∂L/∂x = g, ∂L/∂y = gDistributor — same gradient sabko
Multiplyz = x · y∂L/∂x = g · y, ∂L/∂y = g · xSwapper — doosre input se scale
Maxz = max(x, y)bade input ko g, chhote ko 0Router — sirf winner ko
Copy / branchx do jagah use∂L/∂x = g1 + g2Adder — gradients jodo
ReLUmax(0, x)g if x > 0 else 0Max gate with 0 — "gate band ya khula"

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal (cs231n ka example): f = 2 · (x · y + max(z, w)) at x = 3, y = −4, z = 2, w = −1. Saare gradients nikalo.

Forward:

  1. x · y = 3 × (−4) = −12
  2. max(2, −1) = 2 (z jeeta)
  3. sum = −12 + 2 = −10
  4. f = 2 × (−10) = −20

Backward:

  1. ×2 gate (scale by constant): ∂f/∂sum = 1 × 2 = 2
  2. Add = distributor: ∂f/∂(xy) = 2, ∂f/∂max = 2
  3. Multiply = swapper: ∂f/∂x = 2 × y = 2 × (−4) = −8, ∂f/∂y = 2 × x = 2 × 3 = 6
  4. Max = router: ∂f/∂z = 2 (winner), ∂f/∂w = 0 (loser)

Jawab: ∂f/∂x = −8, ∂f/∂y = 6, ∂f/∂z = 2, ∂f/∂w = 0.

PyTorch · gate patterns verify

import torch
# f = 2 * (x*y + max(z, w))  -> add, multiply, max teeno gates ek saath
x = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)
y = torch.tensor(-4.0, requires_grad=True)
z = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)
w = torch.tensor(-1.0, requires_grad=True)

f = 2 * (x * y + torch.max(z, w))   # torch.max(a, b) = element-wise max
f.backward()
print("f =", f.item())
print("x.grad =", x.grad.item(), "| y.grad =", y.grad.item())
print("z.grad =", z.grad.item(), "| w.grad =", w.grad.item())

# copy gate: same a do jagah use hua -> gradients ADD
a = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)
g = a * a            # a ki do copies multiply gate me gayi
g.backward()
print("d(a*a)/da =", a.grad.item())   # 3 + 3 = 6 = 2a

Output

f = -20.0
x.grad = -8.0 | y.grad = 6.0
z.grad = 2.0 | w.grad = 0.0
d(a*a)/da = 6.0

Multiply gate ka ek gehra sabak: x ka gradient = upstream × y. Agar ek input bahut bada ho (jaise unscaled feature "area = 2000"), to doosre (weight) ka gradient bhi bahut bada ho jayega. Neuron me z = w · x, to ∂L/∂w ∝ x. Isi liye Lab 5 me StandardScaler lagate hain — warna bade features wale weights ke gradients bahut bade, chhote wale ke bahut chhote, aur training ladkhadati hai. (Teacher ki slide "Observation 1" bhi yahi kehti hai: weight ka asar source activation se amplify ya attenuate hota hai.)

Exam Radar

  • Add gate gradient ko unchanged sab inputs me copy karta hai (local gradient 1). Isi wajah se residual connection (x + F(x)) gradient ka "highway" banta hai — Chapter 25.
  • Multiply gate: gradient = upstream × other input. Bade inputs → bade gradients → feature scaling zaroori.
  • Max gate / ReLU / max-pooling: gradient sirf max wale element ko jaata hai, baaki ko 0.
  • Branch (fan-out) pe gradients add hote hain. PyTorch me .grad accumulate hone ka bhi yahi logic hai.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Add baante, Multiply adla-badli kare, Max sirf jeetne wale ko de, Copy sab jod de.

12.9 Worked sigmoid neuron graph — f = σ(w₀x₀ + w₁x₁ + w₂)

Kahani

Ab hamari factory ek asli neuron banati hai. Line pe workers: do multiply wale (w0x0, w1x1), do add wale (jodna + bias), aur end me "sigmoid packing machine". Sigmoid machine ko andar se kholo to wo bhi chhote workers ki line hai: ×(−1), exp, +1, 1/x. Hum pehle har chhote worker ke saath backward karenge, phir dikhayenge ki poori sigmoid machine ka ek shortcut hai.

Ye cs231n ka famous example hai. Neuron: f(w, x) = σ(w0x0 + w1x1 + w2), jahan w2 bias ka kaam karta hai. Values: w = [2, −3, −3], x = [−1, −2]. Sigmoid ko todke likho: σ(z) = 1 / (1 + e−z) → gates: ×(−1) → exp → +1 → 1/x.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Forward pass (har gate ki output value):

  1. w0x0 = 2 × (−1) = −2, w1x1 = (−3) × (−2) = 6
  2. −2 + 6 = 4, phir bias: z = 4 + (−3) = 1
  3. ×(−1): −1   exp: e−1 = 0.3679   +1: 1.3679   1/x: 1/1.3679 = 0.7311

Output f ≈ 0.73.

Backward pass (upstream × local, right se left):

  1. Start: ∂f/∂f = 1
  2. 1/x gate, local = −1/x2 at x = 1.3679: 1 × (−1/1.36792) = 1 × (−0.5344) = −0.5344
  3. +1 gate (local 1): −0.5344 × 1 = −0.5344
  4. exp gate, local = ex at x = −1, i.e. 0.3679: −0.5344 × 0.3679 = −0.1966
  5. ×(−1) gate (local −1): −0.1966 × (−1) = 0.1966 ← ye ∂f/∂z hai
  6. Add gates (distributor): w2, w0x0, w1x1 sabko 0.1966. So ∂f/∂w2 = 0.1966
  7. Multiply gates (swapper): ∂f/∂w0 = 0.1966 × x0 = 0.1966 × (−1) = −0.1966, ∂f/∂x0 = 0.1966 × w0 = 0.1966 × 2 = 0.3932
  8. ∂f/∂w1 = 0.1966 × x1 = 0.1966 × (−2) = −0.3932, ∂f/∂x1 = 0.1966 × w1 = 0.1966 × (−3) = −0.5898

Jawab: f ≈ 0.7311; ∂f/∂w = [−0.1966, −0.3932, 0.1966] ≈ [−0.20, −0.39, 0.20]; ∂f/∂x = [0.3932, −0.5898] ≈ [0.39, −0.59].

Shortcut: σ′(z) = σ(z)(1 − σ(z))

Chaar gates ka kaam ek line me ho sakta hai, kyunki sigmoid ka derivative khud sigmoid se likha ja sakta hai (derivation Chapter 9 me hai): σ′(z) = σ(z)(1 − σ(z)). Yahan: 0.7311 × (1 − 0.7311) = 0.7311 × 0.2689 = 0.1966 — bilkul wahi jo chaar steps se aaya tha! Aur forward me σ(z) to nikal hi chuke hain, to backward me exp dobara calculate karne ki zaroorat bhi nahi — sirf stored output se kaam ho gaya.

Sabak: graph ko kitna tod ke banana hai, ye hamari choice hai. Jis tukde ka local derivative simple ho, use ek "bada gate" maan lo. PyTorch ka torch.sigmoid bhi ek hi node (SigmoidBackward0) hai jo backward me σ(1 − σ) use karta hai.

PyTorch · sigmoid neuron verify

import torch

# sigmoid neuron: f = sigmoid(w0*x0 + w1*x1 + w2)
w = torch.tensor([2.0, -3.0, -3.0], requires_grad=True)   # w2 = bias
x = torch.tensor([-1.0, -2.0], requires_grad=True)

z = w[0]*x[0] + w[1]*x[1] + w[2]     # dot product + bias = 1.0
f = torch.sigmoid(z)                   # 0.7311
print("z =", z.item(), "| f =", round(f.item(), 4))

f.backward()
print("df/dw =", w.grad)               # [x0, x1, 1] * sigma'(z)
print("df/dx =", x.grad)               # [w0, w1] * sigma'(z)

# shortcut check: sigma'(z) = f*(1-f)
s = f.item()
print("sigma'(z) = f(1-f) =", round(s*(1-s), 4))

Output

z = 1.0 | f = 0.7311
df/dw = tensor([-0.1966, -0.3932,  0.1966])
df/dx = tensor([ 0.3932, -0.5898])
sigma'(z) = f(1-f) = 0.1966

Exam Radar

  • Output ≈ 0.73 (σ(1) = 0.7311). ∂f/∂z = 0.1966 ≈ 0.20. dw = [−0.20, −0.39, 0.20], dx = [0.39, −0.59].
  • Weight ka gradient = (∂f/∂z) × uska input; input ka gradient = (∂f/∂z) × uska weight. Bias ka gradient = ∂f/∂z (kyunki ∂z/∂b = 1).
  • σ′(z) = σ(z)(1 − σ(z)) — sirf output se nikal jata hai, isliye sigmoid backward sasta hai. Max value 0.25.
  • Gates ko group karke "bada gate" banana allowed hai, agar uska local derivative pata ho.

Galti mat karna

  • σ′ ko sum z pe evaluate karna hai, output pe nahi: σ′(z) = ŷ(1 − ŷ). Agar galti se σ′(ŷ) = σ(ŷ)(1 − σ(ŷ)) likh diya to answer galat. (Teacher ki worksheet bhi warn karti hai: "σ′ is evaluated at the SUM, not at the output.")
  • Bias ka gradient "0" nahi hota — uska local partner 1 hai, to gradient = ∂f/∂z.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Sigmoid ka backward: "output × (1 − output)". 0.73 × 0.27 ≈ 0.20 — yaad rakho, ye number MCQ me aata hai.

12.10 Forward pass vs Backward pass — kya store hota hai, aur kyun

Kahani

Trekking pe jaate waqt tum har mod pe ek chhota sa nishaan (chalk ka teer) lagate ho, aur likhte ho "yahan se left mude, 200 m chale". Wapas aate waqt wahi nishaan dekh ke ulta raasta pakadte ho. Agar jaate waqt nishaan nahi lagaye, to wapsi me har mod pe dobara soch-soch ke dhoondhna padega.

Forward pass = jaate waqt nishaan lagana (values store karna). Backward pass = wapsi me unhi nishaanon se gradient nikalna.

Forward pass

  • Direction: input → layers → output → loss (left to right)
  • Kaam: har node ki value compute karna: z = Wa + b, a = g(z), ... end me L
  • Store (cache) karta hai: har layer ke inputs a[l−1], pre-activations z[l], activations a[l] (jo bhi backward ko chahiye)
  • Inference (prediction) me sirf yahi chalta hai
  • Teacher slide: "Extracting information in 1st pass"

Backward pass

  • Direction: loss → output → layers → input (right to left)
  • Kaam: har node pe upstream × local se ∂L/∂(har value) aur ∂L/∂(har parameter)
  • Use karta hai forward ki stored values (× gate ko doosra input chahiye, σ gate ko σ(z) chahiye, ReLU ko z > 0 tha ya nahi)
  • Sirf training me chalta hai
  • Teacher slide: "Extracting more information in 2nd pass"

Teacher ke slides ka toy example (Prince UDL, Chapter 7 style)

Lecture 4 ke slides "Toy Example → Extracting information in 1st pass → Extracting more information in 2nd pass" Prince ki UDL book ke backprop chapter ko follow karte hain. Wahan ka toy model: f[x, ϕ] = β3 + ω3 · cos[β2 + ω2 · exp[β1 + ω1 · sin[β0 + ω0 · x]]], loss ℓ = (f − y)2. Isko chhote tukdon me todo:

1st pass (forward) — compute & store2nd pass (backward) — ulte order me
f0 = β0 + ω0x∂ℓ/∂f0 = cos(f0) · ∂ℓ/∂h1
h1 = sin(f0)∂ℓ/∂h1 = ω1 · ∂ℓ/∂f1
f1 = β1 + ω1h1∂ℓ/∂f1 = exp(f1) · ∂ℓ/∂h2  (= h2 · ∂ℓ/∂h2, stored h2 reuse!)
h2 = exp(f1)∂ℓ/∂h2 = ω2 · ∂ℓ/∂f2
f2 = β2 + ω2h2∂ℓ/∂f2 = −sin(f2) · ∂ℓ/∂h3
h3 = cos(f2)∂ℓ/∂h3 = ω3 · ∂ℓ/∂f3
f3 = β3 + ω3h3∂ℓ/∂f3 = 2(f3 − y)  ← yahan se shuru
ℓ = (f3 − y)2Parameters: ∂ℓ/∂βk = ∂ℓ/∂fk,   ∂ℓ/∂ωk = hk · ∂ℓ/∂fk (with h0 = x)

Dhyaan do: (1) backward ka har row pichhle row ka result reuse karta hai — kuch bhi dobara calculate nahi hota. (2) Har row ko forward ki stored value chahiye (f0, f2, hk). (3) Weight ka gradient = "source value hk × destination ka gradient" — yahi pattern 13.4 me δ × activation banega.

Exam Radar

  • Forward pass: computes outputs and loss, caches intermediate activations. Backward pass: computes gradients using chain rule, from loss to inputs, using the cache.
  • Training memory zyada lagti hai kyunki saari activations store karni padti hain (memory ∝ batch size × layers × width). Inference me (torch.no_grad()) ye storage nahi hota → kam memory.
  • Backprop = reverse-mode automatic differentiation. Ek scalar loss aur lakhon parameters ke liye reverse mode best hai: ek backward pass me saare gradients.
  • Forward pass training aur inference dono me; backward sirf training me.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Jaate waqt nishaan lagao (forward + cache), aate waqt nishaan padho (backward). Nishaan nahi to wapsi mehngi.

12.11 PyTorch autograd — graph khud banta hai, gradient khud nikalta hai

Kahani

Purani dukaan ke munim ji yaad karo — har len-den ek bahi-khata me likhte the: "itna aaya, kahan se aaya, kis hisaab se". Mahine ke end me agar hisaab milana ho, to bahi ko ulta padhte the. PyTorch ka autograd yahi munim ji hai: tum tensors pe jo bhi operation karte ho (+, ×, sigmoid, matmul), wo chupchaap ek bahi (computational graph) me likh leta hai. Jab tum loss.backward() bolte ho, wo bahi ulti padh ke har parameter ka gradient nikal deta hai.

Paanch keywords jo pakke yaad hone chahiye

CheezMatlabNote
requires_grad=True"Is tensor ka gradient chahiye — iske upar hone wale operations record karo"Manually banaye tensor me default False. nn.Linear ke weight/bias me default True.
dynamic graphGraph forward pass chalte-chalte banta hai (define-by-run), har iteration me nayaBackward ke baad graph free ho jaata hai (memory bachane ke liye)
grad_fnKis operation ne ye tensor banaya — uska "backward function" nodeAddBackward0, MulBackward0, SigmoidBackward0...; leaf tensor ka grad_fn = None
leaf tensorJo tensor user ne khud banaya (kisi operation ka result nahi) — jaise weights, inputs.is_leaf == True. Sirf leaf tensors (with requires_grad) ka .grad bharta hai
.backward() / .gradbackward() graph ulta chala ke gradients nikalta hai; result leaf ke .grad me add hota haibackward() scalar pe call hota hai (loss). Intermediate ka grad chahiye to .retain_grad()

PyTorch · 12.4 wala graph f = (x + y) * z

import torch

# 1) leaf tensors banao — requires_grad=True matlab "inka gradient chahiye"
x = torch.tensor(-2.0, requires_grad=True)
y = torch.tensor(5.0, requires_grad=True)
z = torch.tensor(-4.0, requires_grad=True)

# 2) forward pass — PyTorch chupke se graph bana raha hai
q = x + y          # add node
f = q * z          # multiply node
print("q =", q)
print("f =", f)
print("f.grad_fn =", f.grad_fn)
print("q.grad_fn =", q.grad_fn)
print("x.is_leaf:", x.is_leaf, "| q.is_leaf:", q.is_leaf)
print("x.grad_fn =", x.grad_fn)

# 3) backward pass — chain rule apne aap
f.backward()
print("df/dx =", x.grad)
print("df/dy =", y.grad)
print("df/dz =", z.grad)

Output

q = tensor(3., grad_fn=<AddBackward0>)
f = tensor(-12., grad_fn=<MulBackward0>)
f.grad_fn = <MulBackward0 object at 0x7f9f60b03a90>
q.grad_fn = <AddBackward0 object at 0x7f9f61933a30>
x.is_leaf: True | q.is_leaf: False
x.grad_fn = None
df/dx = tensor(-4.)
df/dy = tensor(-4.)
df/dz = tensor(3.)

Exactly haath wale answers: −4, −4, 3. (Memory address 0x7f... har run me alag aayega.) q non-leaf hai, to q.grad by default None rahega — uska gradient chahiye to backward se pehle q.retain_grad() likho.

Gradient ACCUMULATION — sabse important trap

Autograd naya gradient purane .grad me jodta hai (+=), replace nahi karta. Kyun? Kyunki "copy gate" (12.8) me ek hi tensor ke do raaston ke gradients jodne hote hain — PyTorch yahi kaam is accumulation se karta hai. Side effect: agar tum do baar backward chalao (do alag iterations me), to gradients jud jaate hain.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

x = 3, y = x2 → dy/dx = 2x = 6.

  1. Pehla backward: x.grad = 0 + 6 = 6
  2. Doosra backward (bina zero kiye): x.grad = 6 + 6 = 12 ← galat! Sahi gradient abhi bhi 6 hai.
  3. x.grad.zero_(): x.grad = 0
  4. Naya forward + backward: x.grad = 0 + 6 = 6 ← sahi

PyTorch · accumulation demo

import torch

x = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)

y = x ** 2                       # dy/dx = 2x = 6
y.backward(retain_graph=True)    # graph ko mat todo, dobara backward karna hai
print("1st backward:", x.grad)

y.backward()                     # same graph pe dobara backward
print("2nd backward:", x.grad)   # 6 + 6 = 12  (ACCUMULATE hua!)

x.grad.zero_()                   # underscore = in-place, grad ko 0 kar do
print("after zero_():", x.grad)

y = x ** 2                       # naya forward = naya graph
y.backward()
print("fresh backward:", x.grad) # phir se sahi 6

Output

1st backward: tensor(6.)
2nd backward: tensor(12.)
after zero_(): tensor(0.)
fresh backward: tensor(6.)

retain_graph=True kyun? Default me backward ke baad graph (aur uski cached values) free ho jaata hai. Same graph pe doosri baar backward karoge to error:

Output (retain_graph ke bina doosra backward)

RuntimeError: Trying to backward through the graph a second time (or directly access saved tensors after ...

Training loop me ye problem nahi aati kyunki har iteration me naya forward → naya graph banta hai. Lekin .grad to parameter ke saath rehta hai, isliye har iteration me backward se pehle optimizer.zero_grad() zaroori hai (ye sab parameters ka .grad saaf karta hai; PyTorch 2.x me default set_to_none=True — grad ko 0 ki jagah None bana deta hai, effect same). Bhool gaye to kya hota hai — 13.8 me numbers ke saath.

torch.no_grad() aur .detach() — recording band karo

  • with torch.no_grad(): — is block ke andar koi graph nahi banta. Use: (1) evaluation/inference (memory + time bachta hai), (2) manual weight update w -= lr * w.grad (update ko graph me record nahi karna).
  • t.detach() — same data wala naya tensor jo graph se kata hua hai (requires_grad=False). Use: value ko numpy me badalna (t.detach().numpy()), plotting, ya kisi value ko "constant" treat karna.
  • loss.item() — scalar tensor se plain Python number; logging ke liye (graph pakad ke nahi rakhta).

PyTorch · no_grad, detach, manual update

import torch

w = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)

# (a) normal: graph banta hai
y = w * 3
print("normal   :", y.requires_grad, y.grad_fn)

# (b) torch.no_grad(): is block me graph NAHI banta
with torch.no_grad():
    y2 = w * 3
print("no_grad  :", y2.requires_grad, y2.grad_fn)

# (c) .detach(): same value, but graph se kata hua naya tensor
y3 = (w * 3).detach()
print("detach   :", y3.requires_grad, y3.grad_fn)

# (d) .numpy() ke liye detach zaroori
print("numpy    :", (w * 3).detach().numpy())

# (e) manual update hamesha no_grad ke andar
loss = (w * 3 - 9) ** 2       # L = (3w - 9)^2, dL/dw = 6(3w - 9) = -18 at w = 2
loss.backward()
print("w.grad   :", w.grad)
with torch.no_grad():
    w -= 0.01 * w.grad        # in-place update, graph me record nahi hoga
print("new w    :", w)

Output

normal   : True <MulBackward0 object at 0x7f6920c5b4c0>
no_grad  : False None
detach   : False None
numpy    : 6.0
w.grad   : tensor(-18.)
new w    : tensor(2.1800, requires_grad=True)

Vector output pe backward — pehle scalar banao

.backward() bina argument ke sirf scalar (ek number) pe chalta hai — kyunki "gradient of a single number w.r.t. sab cheezein" hi well-defined hai. Agar output vector ho (jaise Lab 2/3 me activation ki curve), to .sum() karke backward karo: sum ka har element ke saath derivative 1 hai, to har element ko apna local derivative mil jaata hai. Lab 2/3 isi liye torch.autograd.grad(y.sum(), z)[0] use karte hain — ye .grad me jodne ke bajaye gradient seedha return karta hai.

PyTorch · vector output (Lab 2/3 style)

import torch
z = torch.tensor([-1.0, 0.0, 2.0], requires_grad=True)
y = torch.sigmoid(z)            # shape (3,) -> scalar nahi hai
try:
    y.backward()
except RuntimeError as e:
    print("RuntimeError:", e)
y.sum().backward()              # sum ka gradient = har element ka apna sigma'(z)
print(z.grad)
g = torch.autograd.grad(torch.sigmoid(z).sum(), z)[0]   # Lab 2/3 wala style
print(g)

Output

RuntimeError: grad can be implicitly created only for scalar outputs
tensor([0.1966, 0.2500, 0.1050])
tensor([0.1966, 0.2500, 0.1050])

Dekho: σ′(0) = 0.25 (maximum), σ′(−1) = 0.1966, σ′(2) = 0.1050. Vector functions ke liye "local gradient" ek matrix (Jacobian) ban jaata hai; autograd poora Jacobian banaye bina "vector × Jacobian" product nikalta hai — isi liye ye fast hai (Lecture 4 slide: "Generalizing for vector functions in Deep NNs").

Exam Radar

  • requires_grad default False for torch.tensor(...); True for nn.Parameter / layer weights.
  • .grad sirf leaf tensors ka populate hota hai. Leaf ka grad_fn = None. Result tensors ka grad_fn = <XxxBackward0>.
  • Gradients accumulate by default → optimizer.zero_grad() (ya tensor.grad.zero_()) har step pe.
  • Same graph pe 2nd backward → RuntimeError, jab tak retain_graph=True na do.
  • backward() non-scalar pe → "grad can be implicitly created only for scalar outputs".
  • torch.no_grad() = graph recording off (eval, manual update). .detach() = graph se alag tensor. .item() = Python number.
  • PyTorch = dynamic graph (define-by-run).

Galti mat karna

  • w = w - lr * w.grad bina no_grad ke likhoge to naya w non-leaf ban jayega (graph ka hissa) aur agli baar uska .grad None aayega. Manual update hamesha with torch.no_grad(): me, in-place (-=).
  • Requires-grad wale tensor pe seedha .numpy() → error. Pehle .detach().
  • zero_() ka underscore matlab in-place. x.grad.zero() naam ka function nahi hai.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Autograd = munim ji ki bahi: requires_grad se likhna shuru, backward() se ulta padhna, .grad me jama — aur jama hota hi rehta hai jab tak zero_grad() se saaf na karo.

Chapter 13

Backpropagation Algorithm, Gradient Flow, Vanishing & Exploding Gradients — aur poora PyTorch training loop

1-1-1 network by hand · 2-2-1 network by hand · δ notation & general algorithm · Gradient flow · Vanishing gradients · Exploding gradients & clipping · Lab 5 training pipeline

13.1 Backpropagation kya hai — ek line me, phir detail me

Kahani

India match haar gayi — 10 run se. Coach ko har player ka "blame" nikalna hai. Wo result se peeche chalta hai: aakhri over ke bowler ne kitne diye, usse pehle wale ne, batsman ne kitne dot balls khele... Har player ka hissa uske kaam aur uske baad ke asar dono se banta hai. Ye "result se ulta chal ke har player ka hissa (blame) nikalna" hi backpropagation hai — blame assignment. Phir coach har player ko bolta hai: "tum itna sudharo" — wo hai gradient descent.

Definition

Backpropagation (backward propagation of errors) = chain rule ko computational graph pe output se input ki taraf systematically lagane ka algorithm, jo ek forward + ek backward pass me loss ka gradient har weight aur bias ke respect me nikal deta hai. Teacher ki slide: "Backpropagation is crucial for training neural networks. It is an efficient method for computing the gradient. The concept relies on the chain rule of calculus."

Ek training step ke chaar kadam (MLP worksheet + Lab 5 dono yahi kehte hain):

  1. Forward pass: input se prediction ŷ (beech ki values store karo).
  2. Loss: ŷ ko target y se compare karo → L.
  3. Backward pass (backprop): L se peeche chalte hue ∂L/∂w, ∂L/∂b sab parameters ke liye.
  4. Update (gradient descent): w ← w − η ∂L/∂w. Phir agla example/batch, phir se.

Teacher ki slide ke do "Intuitive Observations" yaad rakho — poora algorithm inhi do baaton pe khada hai:

  • Observation 1: Har weight ek source unit ki activation ko multiply karke destination unit me jodta hai. Isliye weight me chhote change ka asar source activation se amplify ya attenuate hota hai. (→ ∂L/∂w = destination ki error × source ki activation.)
  • Observation 2: Kisi bias ya weight me chhota change ek ripple effect banata hai — aage ke saare network se hote hue output tak, aur phir loss tak. (→ isliye gradient ko loss se peeche-peeche laana padta hai.)

Exam Radar

  • Backprop popular hua Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) ke Nature paper "Learning representations by back-propagating errors" se. (Reverse-mode differentiation ke ideas pehle Linnainmaa 1970, Werbos 1974 me bhi the.)
  • Backprop = chain rule + dynamic programming (intermediate gradients reuse). Gradient compute karta hai; update optimizer karta hai.
  • Backprop ko differentiable operations chahiye. Step function (perceptron) ka derivative almost everywhere 0 hai → backprop se train nahi hota. Isliye sigmoid/ReLU jaise activations (Chapter 9).

13.2 1-1-1 network — poora backprop haath se (classroom projection numbers)

Kahani

Teen dost line me khade hain: Input (x), Hidden (h), Output (ŷ). Input ek number hidden ko deta hai (weight w1 ke saath), hidden apna mood (sigmoid) laga ke output ko deta hai (weight w2 ke saath), output bhi sigmoid laga ke final answer deta hai. Teacher (loss) bolti hai: "jawab 1 hona chahiye tha". Ab dekhte hain kis dost ka kitna kasoor hai.

Ye exactly classroom projection document aur MLP worksheet (Part 6) ka network hai: ek input, ek hidden neuron, ek output; sigmoid activation; squared-error loss.

z1 = w1x + b1,   h = σ(z1),   z2 = w2h + b2,   ŷ = σ(z2),   L = ½(ŷ − y)2
  • x = input, y = true label (target)
  • w1, b1 = input → hidden ka weight aur hidden ka bias; z1 = hidden ka weighted input
  • h = hidden ki activation (worksheet me isko a[1] likha hai)
  • w2, b2 = hidden → output; z2 = output ka weighted input; ŷ = a[2] = prediction
  • ½ isliye ki differentiate karne pe square ka 2 cancel ho jaaye: ∂L/∂ŷ = ŷ − y

Initial values: x = 2, y = 1, w1 = 0.5, b1 = 0, w2 = 0.5, b2 = 0, learning rate η = 0.1.

Step 1 — Forward propagation

  1. Hidden weighted input: z1 = (0.5)(2) + 0 = 1
  2. Hidden activation: h = σ(1) = 1/(1 + e−1) = 1/1.36788 = 0.73106
  3. Output weighted input: z2 = (0.5)(0.73106) + 0 = 0.36553
  4. Prediction: ŷ = σ(0.36553) = 1/(1 + e−0.36553) = 0.59038
  5. Loss: L = ½(0.59038 − 1)2 = ½(−0.40962)2 = ½(0.16779) = 0.083895

Prediction 0.59038 target 1 se kam hai → network ko parameters aise badalne hain ki prediction badhe aur loss ghate.

Step 2 — Backward: pehle saare local derivatives

Classroom document ka tareeka: pehle poora derivative path likho, phir har local derivative substitute karo.

  1. Loss → output: ∂L/∂ŷ = ŷ − y = 0.59038 − 1 = −0.40962
  2. Output sigmoid: ∂ŷ/∂z2 = ŷ(1 − ŷ) = 0.59038 × 0.40962 = 0.24183
  3. Sum → weight: ∂z2/∂w2 = h = 0.73106 (weight ka partner)
  4. Sum → bias: ∂z2/∂b2 = 1
  5. Sum → hidden: ∂z2/∂h = w2 = 0.5 ← ye raasta hai jisse error hidden tak jaata hai
  6. Hidden sigmoid: ∂h/∂z1 = h(1 − h) = 0.73106 × 0.26894 = 0.19661
  7. Hidden sum → weight: ∂z1/∂w1 = x = 2; → bias: ∂z1/∂b1 = 1

Step 3 — Gradients (chain = local derivatives ka product)

w₂ — path: w2 → z2 → ŷ → L

∂L/∂w2 = ∂L/∂ŷ × ∂ŷ/∂z2 × ∂z2/∂w2 = (ŷ − y) × ŷ(1 − ŷ) × h
= (−0.40962)(0.59038)(0.40962)(0.73106)
= (−0.09906)(0.73106) = −0.07242

b₂ — same path, last link 1:

∂L/∂b2 = (ŷ − y) × ŷ(1 − ŷ) × 1 = (−0.40962)(0.24183) = −0.09906

w₁ — lamba path: w1 → z1 → h → z2 → ŷ → L

∂L/∂w1 = ∂L/∂ŷ × ∂ŷ/∂z2 × ∂z2/∂h × ∂h/∂z1 × ∂z1/∂w1
= (ŷ − y) × ŷ(1 − ŷ) × w2 × h(1 − h) × x
= (−0.40962)(0.59038)(0.40962)(0.5)(0.73106)(0.26894)(2)
= (−0.09906)(0.5)(0.19661)(2) = −0.01948

b₁ — same lamba path, last link 1:

∂L/∂b1 = (−0.09906)(0.5)(0.19661)(1) = −0.009738

Saare char gradients negative → char parameters badhenge (minus × minus = plus). Prediction kam thi, badhni chahiye — consistent!

Dhyaan se dekho: (ŷ − y) × ŷ(1 − ŷ) = −0.09906 chaaron gradients me common hai. Isko naam do δ2 = ∂L/∂z2 ("output neuron ki error"). Aur δ2 × w2 × h(1 − h) = −0.009738 = δ1 = ∂L/∂z1 ("hidden neuron ki error"). Phir:

  • ∂L/∂w2 = δ2 × h   (destination ki error × source ki activation)
  • ∂L/∂b2 = δ2
  • ∂L/∂w1 = δ1 × x = −0.009738 × 2 = −0.01948
  • ∂L/∂b1 = δ1

Yahi δ wala pattern 13.4 me general algorithm banega. δ ek baar nikalo, sab jagah reuse karo — yahi backprop ki efficiency hai.

Step 4 — Update (η = 0.1) aur verification

Rule: new parameter = old parameter − η × gradient

  1. w2 = 0.5 − 0.1(−0.07242) = 0.5 + 0.007242 = 0.50724
  2. w1 = 0.5 − 0.1(−0.01948) = 0.5 + 0.001948 = 0.50195
  3. b2 = 0 − 0.1(−0.09906) = 0.009906
  4. b1 = 0 − 0.1(−0.009738) = 0.000974

Naye parameters se dobara forward pass:

z1 = 0.50195 × 2 + 0.000974 = 1.00487 → h = σ(1.00487) = 0.73202
z2 = 0.50724 × 0.73202 + 0.009906 = 0.38121 → ŷ = σ(0.38121) = 0.59417
L = ½(0.59417 − 1)2 = 0.082351

Loss 0.083895 → 0.082351. Ghata! Gradients ne parameters ko sahi direction me hilaya. Training = yahi step hazaaron baar.

ParameterGradientInitialUpdated
w1−0.019480.500000.50195
b1−0.0097380.000000.000974
w2−0.072420.500000.50724
b2−0.099060.000000.009906

Ek aur cheez notice karo: |∂L/∂w1| = 0.0195 < |∂L/∂w2| = 0.0724. Pehli layer ka gradient chhota hai, kyunki uske path me do extra factors hain: w2 = 0.5 aur h(1 − h) = 0.1966. Ye "peeche jaate-jaate gradient chhota hona" hi vanishing gradient ka beej hai (13.6).

Code (a): manual backprop vs autograd — same answer

PyTorch · 1-1-1 manual chain rule vs autograd (Lab 2 style assert)

import torch

x, y = torch.tensor(2.0), torch.tensor(1.0)
w1 = torch.tensor(0.5, requires_grad=True)
b1 = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)
w2 = torch.tensor(0.5, requires_grad=True)
b2 = torch.tensor(0.0, requires_grad=True)

# ---------- forward pass (values store ho rahe hain) ----------
z1 = w1 * x + b1
h = torch.sigmoid(z1)
z2 = w2 * h + b2
y_hat = torch.sigmoid(z2)
L = 0.5 * (y_hat - y) ** 2
print(f"forward: h={h.item():.6f}  y_hat={y_hat.item():.6f}  L={L.item():.6f}")

# ---------- manual backward (haath se chain rule) ----------
with torch.no_grad():
    dL_dyhat = y_hat - y                         # dL/dy_hat
    delta2 = dL_dyhat * y_hat * (1 - y_hat)      # dL/dz2
    g_w2 = delta2 * h                            # dz2/dw2 = h
    g_b2 = delta2 * 1                            # dz2/db2 = 1
    delta1 = delta2 * w2 * h * (1 - h)           # dL/dz1 (w2 se peeche aaya)
    g_w1 = delta1 * x                            # dz1/dw1 = x
    g_b1 = delta1 * 1

# ---------- autograd backward ----------
L.backward()

print("param   manual      autograd")
for name, m, p in [("w1", g_w1, w1), ("b1", g_b1, b1), ("w2", g_w2, w2), ("b2", g_b2, b2)]:
    print(f"{name}   {m.item():+.6f}   {p.grad.item():+.6f}")
assert all(torch.allclose(m, p.grad) for m, p in [(g_w1, w1), (g_b1, b1), (g_w2, w2), (g_b2, b2)])
print("Manual chain rule == autograd")

# ---------- ek gradient-descent step, eta = 0.1 ----------
eta = 0.1
with torch.no_grad():
    for p in (w1, b1, w2, b2):
        p -= eta * p.grad
    y_new = torch.sigmoid(w2 * torch.sigmoid(w1 * x + b1) + b2)
    L_new = 0.5 * (y_new - y) ** 2
print(f"new: w1={w1.item():.5f} b1={b1.item():.6f} w2={w2.item():.5f} b2={b2.item():.6f}")
print(f"loss: {L.item():.6f} -> {L_new.item():.6f}")

Output

forward: h=0.731059  y_hat=0.590378  L=0.083895
param   manual      autograd
w1   -0.019476   -0.019476
b1   -0.009738   -0.009738
w2   -0.072418   -0.072418
b2   -0.099060   -0.099060
Manual chain rule == autograd
new: w1=0.50195 b1=0.000974 w2=0.50724 b2=0.009906
loss: 0.083895 -> 0.082351

Line-by-line: x, y data hain (gradient nahi chahiye) to requires_grad nahi diya; parameters pe diya. Manual part no_grad me hai taaki ye extra calculations graph me na judein. torch.allclose float ke chhote rounding farak ko ignore karke compare karta hai. Update bhi no_grad me in-place (-=), taaki parameters leaf hi rahein.

Exam Radar

  • 1-1-1 (x = 2, y = 1, w = 0.5, b = 0): h = 0.73106, ŷ = 0.59038, L = 0.083895; ∂L/∂w2 = −0.07242, ∂L/∂w1 = −0.01948, ∂L/∂b2 = −0.09906, ∂L/∂b1 = −0.009738; η = 0.1 ke baad L = 0.082351.
  • ∂z/∂w = us weight ka input (source activation); ∂z/∂b = 1; ∂z2/∂h = w2 (error hidden tak weight ke through jaati hai).
  • Saare gradients negative → saare parameters badhe → ŷ badha (target 1 ki taraf).
  • Pehli layer ka gradient chhota (extra factors w2·h(1−h) ≈ 0.098).

Galti mat karna

  • ∂L/∂w1 me w2 (purana value 0.5) use hota hai, updated nahi. Pehle saare gradients purane parameters se nikalo, phir sab ek saath update karo.
  • Sigmoid derivative hidden me h(1 − h) aur output me ŷ(1 − ŷ) — dono ko mix mat karo.
  • Bias gradient me last factor 1 hai (input x nahi).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Weight gradient = "aage ki error (δ) × peeche ki activation". Output pe δ = (ŷ − y)·ŷ(1 − ŷ); hidden pe δ = aage ka δ × weight × h(1 − h).

13.3 2-2-1 network — saare chhe weights ka backprop (student activity)

Kahani

Ab class project me do students (x1, x2) do group leaders (h1, h2) ko report dete hain, aur dono leaders milke principal (ŷ) ko final report dete hain. Result kharab aaya to blame do parallel branches me baTega: h1 wali branch aur h2 wali branch. Har branch apne students tak blame pahunchayegi.

Guided worksheet ka network: 2 inputs, 2 hidden neurons, 1 output, 6 weights. Notation worksheet jaisa: w1, w2 → h1 me; w3, w4 → h2 me; w5, w6 → output me.

z1 = w1x1 + w2x2 + b1,   z2 = w3x1 + w4x2 + b2,   z3 = w5h1 + w6h2 + b3
  • h1 = σ(z1), h2 = σ(z2), ŷ = σ(z3), L = ½(ŷ − y)2
  • Rule: w(new) = w(old) − α(∂L/∂w); σ′(z) = σ(z)[1 − σ(z)]
  • Given: x1 = 1, x2 = 2, y = 1, α = 0.10; w1…w6 = 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60; b1 = b2 = b3 = 0 (is activity me biases update nahi karne)
  • Worksheet ki salah: calculation me kam se kam 6 decimal places rakho.

Part 2 — Forward propagation

  1. z1 = (0.10)(1) + (0.20)(2) + 0 = 0.500000
  2. h1 = σ(0.5) = 0.622459
  3. z2 = (0.30)(1) + (0.40)(2) + 0 = 1.100000
  4. h2 = σ(1.1) = 0.750260
  5. z3 = (0.50)(0.622459) + (0.60)(0.750260) + 0 = 0.311230 + 0.450156 = 0.761386
  6. ŷ = σ(0.761386) = 0.681655
  7. L = ½(0.681655 − 1)2 = ½(0.101343) = 0.050672

Checkpoint: prediction target se kam hai → expect karo ki chhe weights mostly badhenge.

Part 3 — Output weights w₅, w₆

  1. ∂L/∂ŷ = ŷ − y = 0.681655 − 1 = −0.318345
  2. ∂ŷ/∂z3 = ŷ(1 − ŷ) = (0.681655)(0.318345) = 0.217002
  3. Output signal (dono output weights share karte hain): δ3 = (−0.318345)(0.217002) = −0.069081
  4. ∂L/∂w5 = δ3 × h1 = (−0.069081)(0.622459) = −0.043000 → w5 = 0.50 − 0.10(−0.043000) = 0.504300
  5. ∂L/∂w6 = δ3 × h2 = (−0.069081)(0.750260) = −0.051829 → w6 = 0.60 − 0.10(−0.051829) = 0.605183

Checkpoint: h₂ (0.7503) > h₁ (0.6225), isliye |∂L/∂w₆| > |∂L/∂w₅|. Jiska source zyada "on" hai, uska weight zyada blame leta hai (Observation 1).

Part 4 — h₁ branch: w₁, w₂

  1. Local derivatives: ∂z3/∂h1 = w5 = 0.50, ∂h1/∂z1 = h1(1 − h1) = (0.622459)(0.377541) = 0.235004, ∂z1/∂w1 = x1 = 1, ∂z1/∂w2 = x2 = 2
  2. ∂L/∂w1 = (−0.318345)(0.217002)(0.50)(0.235004)(1) = −0.008117 → w1 = 0.10 − 0.10(−0.008117) = 0.100812
  3. ∂L/∂w2 = (−0.318345)(0.217002)(0.50)(0.235004)(2) = −0.016234 → w2 = 0.20 − 0.10(−0.016234) = 0.201623

Checkpoint: x₂ = 2x₁, isliye ∂L/∂w₂ = 2 × ∂L/∂w₁ (−0.016234 = 2 × −0.008117).

Part 5 — h₂ branch: w₃, w₄

  1. Local derivatives: ∂z3/∂h2 = w6 = 0.60, ∂h2/∂z2 = (0.750260)(0.249740) = 0.187370, ∂z2/∂w3 = x1 = 1, ∂z2/∂w4 = x2 = 2
  2. ∂L/∂w3 = (−0.318345)(0.217002)(0.60)(0.187370)(1) = −0.007766 → w3 = 0.30 − 0.10(−0.007766) = 0.300777
  3. ∂L/∂w4 = (−0.318345)(0.217002)(0.60)(0.187370)(2) = −0.015533 → w4 = 0.40 − 0.10(−0.015533) = 0.401553

Checkpoint: phir se x₂ = 2x₁ ⇒ ∂L/∂w₄ = 2 × ∂L/∂w₃.

Part 6 — Verification after one update

z1(new) = 0.100812(1) + 0.201623(2) = 0.504059 → h1(new) = 0.623413
z2(new) = 0.300777(1) + 0.401553(2) = 1.103883 → h2(new) = 0.750987
z3(new) = 0.504300(0.623413) + 0.605183(0.750987) = 0.768872 → ŷ(new) = 0.683277
