L: 0.050672 → 0.050157. Loss ghata → update sahi direction me tha. Saare chhe gradients negative the, saare chhe weights badhe.

Bias ka kya? Is activity me biases freeze the, lekin unke gradients bhi bas δ hain: ∂L/∂b3 = δ3 = −0.069081, ∂L/∂b1 = δ1 = −0.008117, ∂L/∂b2 = δ2 = −0.007766 (jahan δ1 = δ3·w5·h1(1−h1), δ2 = δ3·w6·h2(1−h2)). Dekho, ∂L/∂w1 = δ1 × x1 = δ1 × 1, isliye number same aaya.

Exam Radar

  • 2-2-1 (x = [1, 2], y = 1, w = 0.1…0.6, α = 0.1): ŷ = 0.681655, L = 0.050672, δ3 = −0.069081; L(new) = 0.050157.
  • Hidden weight ka gradient path me 5 factors: (ŷ − y) · ŷ(1−ŷ) · wout · h(1−h) · x.
  • Same neuron me aane wale weights ka gradient ratio = unke inputs ka ratio (x2 = 2x1 ⇒ gradient double).
  • 2-2-1 me kitne parameters? Har layer: nin×nout + nout → (2×2 + 2) + (2×1 + 1) = 6 + 3 = 9 (6 weights + 3 biases).

Galti mat karna

  • h1 branch me w5 aata hai, h2 branch me w6. Branch mix ki to gradient galat.
  • Update karte waqt purani values use karo; w5 update karke uska naya value w1 ke gradient me mat daalo.

13.4 General algorithm — δ notation, kisi bhi network ke liye

Kahani

Ek company me complaint upar se (CEO = loss) aati hai. Har manager ka "blame" (δ) aise nikalta hai: uske neeche ke jin logon ko usne kaam diya tha, unke blame ko connection ki strength (weight) se weight karke JODO, phir multiply karo manager ki apni "sensitivity" (activation ka slope g′) se. Aur kisi ek connection (weight) ka blame = "jisko report gayi uska blame × jisne report bheji uska output". Bas — har layer pe yahi do kaam, upar se neeche.

Notation (Backprop Worksheet 03 aur MLP worksheet wali)

  • w[l]jk = layer l ka weight, jo layer l ke neuron j me jaata hai, previous layer ke neuron k se aata hai. (j = destination, k = source.) Example: w[1]21 = layer 1, hidden neuron 2 me, input 1 se.
  • b[l]j, z[l]j, a[l]j, δ[l]j — sab layer l ke neuron j ke. a[0] = input x. Output layer L ki activation ko ŷ bolte hain.
  • Matrix form: W[l] ka shape (nl, nl−1) — row j = neuron j me aane wale saare weights. (PyTorch nn.Linear(in, out).weight ka shape bhi (out, in) hai.)
  • Forward: z[l] = W[l]a[l−1] + b[l],   a[l] = g(z[l])

Definition

δ[l]j = ∂L/∂z[l]j = neuron j (layer l) ki "error" — agar is neuron ka weighted sum thoda badhe to loss kitna badhega. Ye neuron ki property hai, kisi ek weight ki nahi. Ek baar nikalo, us neuron ke saare weights aur bias ke liye reuse karo.

(BP1)   δ[L] = ∂L∂a[L] ⊙ g′(z[L])     (output layer)
(BP2)   δ[l] = (W[l+1]T δ[l+1]) ⊙ g′(z[l])     (hidden layers, peeche ki taraf)
(BP3)   ∂L∂W[l] = δ[l] a[l−1]T    i.e.   ∂L∂w[l]jk = δ[l]j · a[l−1]k
(BP4)   ∂L∂b[l] = δ[l]
  • ⊙ = element-wise (Hadamard) multiply — har neuron apne hi g′ se multiply hota hai
  • g′(z[l]) = activation ka slope us layer pe (sigmoid: a(1 − a); tanh: 1 − a2; ReLU: 1 if z > 0 else 0)
  • W[l+1]T (transpose) kyun? Forward me neuron k (layer l) ne layer l+1 ke saare neurons j ko feed kiya tha. Multivariable chain rule (12.7): uski error = saare raaston ka sum = Σj w[l+1]jk δ[l+1]j. Ye exactly WTδ ka row k hai. Matlab error same edges pe ulti chalti hai.
  • BP3: "gradient = error at destination × signal at source" (worksheet ki line). Weight ka local derivative uska source activation hai (multiply gate = swapper).
  • BP4: bias ka partner 1 hai, to gradient = δ khud.

Output layer ka δ — loss + activation ki jodi pe depend

Output activation + Lossδ[L] = ∂L/∂z[L]Kyun
Sigmoid + BCEŷ − y∂L/∂ŷ = (ŷ − y)/(ŷ(1 − ŷ)); × σ′ = ŷ(1 − ŷ) → cancel
Sigmoid + MSE (½ wala)(ŷ − y) · σ′(z) = (ŷ − y)ŷ(1 − ŷ)σ′ cancel nahi hota (hamare 1-1-1, 2-2-1, 2-3-2 examples)
Softmax + Cross-Entropyŷ − y (vector, y one-hot)Softmax ka Jacobian aur log cancel ho jaate hain
Linear (identity) + MSE (½)ŷ − yg′ = 1

Chalo numbers se samjhein — BCE ka magic cancel

Sawaal: ŷ = 0.8, y = 1, sigmoid output. BCE: L = −[y ln ŷ + (1 − y) ln(1 − ŷ)]. δ nikalo.

  1. ∂L/∂ŷ = −y/ŷ + (1 − y)/(1 − ŷ) = −1/0.8 + 0 = −1.25
  2. σ′(z) = ŷ(1 − ŷ) = 0.8 × 0.2 = 0.16
  3. δ = −1.25 × 0.16 = −0.2   aur shortcut: ŷ − y = 0.8 − 1 = −0.2. Same!

Ab saturation wala case dekho (activation worksheet): z = 6, ŷ = 0.99753, y = 0. MSE ke saath δ = (ŷ − y)σ′(z) = 0.99753 × 0.00247 ≈ 0.00246 — network "99.75% galat" hai fir bhi gradient chhota! BCE ke saath δ = ŷ − y = 0.99753 — bada, seedha galti ke barabar. Isi liye classification me sigmoid + BCE preferred hai.

Worked: 2-3-2 network (Backprop Worksheet 03) — output layer, phir "page 2" hidden layer

Worksheet ka fixed network: x = (1, 2), targets y = (1, 0), α = 0.5, sigmoid everywhere, loss L = ½[(ŷ1 − y1)2 + (ŷ2 − y2)2]. Weights:

Layer 1 (into hidden): rows = neuron j

0.20.1
0.30.2
−0.4−0.6

b[1] = (0.1, 0.3, 0.1)

Layer 2 (into outputs): rows = output neuron (destination)

0.5−0.30.8
−0.60.40.2

b[2] = (0.2, −0.1)

12 weights + 5 biases = 17 parameters. (Sheet har step ko 4 decimals pe round karti hai; isliye kahin-kahin last digit me full-precision se 1 ka farak dikhega.)

Forward (sheet ke numbers)

  1. z[1] = (0.2·1 + 0.1·2 + 0.1,  0.3·1 + 0.2·2 + 0.3,  −0.4·1 − 0.6·2 + 0.1) = (0.5, 1.0, −1.5)
  2. a[1] = σ(z[1]) = (0.6225, 0.7311, 0.1824)
  3. z[2]1 = 0.3113 − 0.2193 + 0.1459 + 0.2 ≈ 0.4379 (full precision 0.43785), z[2]2 = −0.3735 + 0.2924 + 0.0365 − 0.1 = −0.1446
  4. ŷ = (σ(0.43785), σ(−0.1446)) = (0.6077, 0.4639)
  5. L = ½[(−0.3923)2 + (0.4639)2] = ½(0.1539 + 0.2152) = ½(0.3691) ≈ 0.1846 (sheet; full precision 0.1845)

Output 1 bahut kam hai (chahiye 1), output 2 bahut zyada hai (chahiye 0).

Output layer — BP1, BP3

  1. σ′(z[2]1) = 0.6077 × 0.3923 = 0.2384, σ′(z[2]2) = 0.4639 × 0.5361 = 0.2487
  2. δ[2]1 = (ŷ1 − y1)σ′ = (−0.3923)(0.2384) = −0.0935
  3. δ[2]2 = (0.4639)(0.2487) = 0.1154
  4. BP3 (δ × source activation):
    ∂L/∂w[2]11 = (−0.0935)(0.6225) = −0.0582   ∂L/∂w[2]12 = (−0.0935)(0.7311) = −0.0684   ∂L/∂w[2]13 = (−0.0935)(0.1824) = −0.0171
    ∂L/∂w[2]21 = (0.1154)(0.6225) = 0.0718   ∂L/∂w[2]22 = (0.1154)(0.7311) = 0.0844   ∂L/∂w[2]23 = (0.1154)(0.1824) = 0.0210
  5. Update (α = 0.5): w[2]11 = 0.5 − 0.5(−0.0582) = 0.5291, w[2]12 = −0.3 + 0.0342 = −0.2658, w[2]13 = 0.8086, w[2]21 = −0.6 − 0.0359 = −0.6359, w[2]22 = 0.3578, w[2]23 = 0.1895

Sheet ka result: sirf ye chhe output weights badle to ŷ = (0.6183, 0.4502) aur L: 0.1846 → 0.1742. Output 1 (too low) ke saare weights UP gaye; output 2 (too high) ke saare DOWN. Sign δ me rehta hai; size source activation se aata hai — hidden 3 barely on (0.1824) tha, to uske weights barely hile.

Sheet ka "open question" tha: "Every δ we used came from a target. A hidden neuron has no target of its own. So where does its error come from?" Jawab = BP2: aage wale neurons ke δ, unhi weights se ulte bheje gaye.

Hidden layer — BP2 (sheet ka "page 2")

  1. Pehle W[2]Tδ[2] (har hidden neuron ko dono outputs se aayi error ka sum):
    hidden 1: (0.5)(−0.0935) + (−0.6)(0.1154) = −0.04675 − 0.06924 = −0.11599
    hidden 2: (−0.3)(−0.0935) + (0.4)(0.1154) = 0.02805 + 0.04616 = 0.07421
    hidden 3: (0.8)(−0.0935) + (0.2)(0.1154) = −0.07480 + 0.02308 = −0.05172
  2. σ′(z[1]) = a(1 − a): 0.6225 × 0.3775 = 0.2350, 0.7311 × 0.2689 = 0.1966, 0.1824 × 0.8176 = 0.1491
  3. ⊙ multiply: δ[1] = (−0.11599 × 0.2350,  0.07421 × 0.1966,  −0.05172 × 0.1491) = (−0.02726, 0.01459, −0.00771) ≈ (−0.0273, 0.0146, −0.0077)
  4. BP3 with source = input x = (1, 2):
    ∂L/∂W[1] = δ[1] xT = row 1: (−0.0273, −0.0545)   row 2: (0.0146, 0.0292)   row 3: (−0.0077, −0.0154)
  5. BP4: ∂L/∂b[1] = δ[1] = (−0.0273, 0.0146, −0.0077)

Interesting: hidden 2 ka δ positive hai. Kyun? Hidden 2 output 1 ko −0.3 se (neeche) dhakelta hai jabki output 1 ko upar jaana hai, aur output 2 ko +0.4 se (upar) dhakelta hai jabki output 2 ko neeche jaana hai. Dono taraf nuksaan → hidden 2 ko "kam on" hona chahiye → positive δ → uske incoming weights ghatenge.

PyTorch · vectorized manual backprop (BP1–BP4) vs autograd, 2-3-2 network

import torch

torch.set_printoptions(precision=4)
# 2-3-2 network (Backprop Worksheet 03 ke numbers)
x  = torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0])                       # a[0] = x, shape (2,)
y  = torch.tensor([1.0, 0.0])
W1 = torch.tensor([[0.2, 0.1], [0.3, 0.2], [-0.4, -0.6]], requires_grad=True)  # (3, 2)
b1 = torch.tensor([0.1, 0.3, 0.1], requires_grad=True)                         # (3,)
W2 = torch.tensor([[0.5, -0.3, 0.8], [-0.6, 0.4, 0.2]], requires_grad=True)    # (2, 3)
b2 = torch.tensor([0.2, -0.1], requires_grad=True)                             # (2,)

# ----- forward -----
z1 = W1 @ x + b1;  a1 = torch.sigmoid(z1)          # (3,)
z2 = W2 @ a1 + b2; yh = torch.sigmoid(z2)          # (2,)
L = 0.5 * ((yh - y) ** 2).sum()
print("a1 =", a1.detach(), "| y_hat =", yh.detach(), "| L =", round(L.item(), 4))

# ----- manual backward (BP1-BP4) -----
with torch.no_grad():
    d2 = (yh - y) * yh * (1 - yh)                  # BP1: delta[2], (2,)
    gW2 = torch.outer(d2, a1)                       # BP3: delta[2] a[1]^T, (2, 3)
    gb2 = d2                                        # BP4
    d1 = (W2.T @ d2) * a1 * (1 - a1)               # BP2: (W^T delta) * sigma'(z1), (3,)
    gW1 = torch.outer(d1, x)                        # (3, 2)
    gb1 = d1
print("delta2 =", d2, "| delta1 =", d1)
print("dL/dW2 =\n", gW2)
print("dL/dW1 =\n", gW1)

# ----- autograd se match -----
L.backward()
print("match:", all(torch.allclose(a, b) for a, b in
      [(gW2, W2.grad), (gb2, b2.grad), (gW1, W1.grad), (gb1, b1.grad)]))

Output

a1 = tensor([0.6225, 0.7311, 0.1824]) | y_hat = tensor([0.6077, 0.4639]) | L = 0.1845
delta2 = tensor([-0.0935,  0.1154]) | delta1 = tensor([-0.0273,  0.0146, -0.0077])
dL/dW2 =
 tensor([[-0.0582, -0.0684, -0.0171],
        [ 0.0718,  0.0843,  0.0210]])
dL/dW1 =
 tensor([[-0.0273, -0.0545],
        [ 0.0146,  0.0292],
        [-0.0077, -0.0154]])
match: True

Full precision me L = 0.1845 aur ∂L/∂w[2]22 = 0.0843 (sheet me step-rounding se 0.1846 aur 0.0844). torch.outer(a, b) = column × row = matrix (yahi δaT hai). W2.T = transpose. * = element-wise (⊙).

Mini-batch me shapes (PyTorch convention)

PyTorch me data rows me hota hai: X shape (N, nin), aur nn.Linear karta hai Z = XWT + b. Tab δ bhi (N, nout) shape ka matrix hai (har example ki ek row), aur:

CheezShapeFormula (batch)
A[l−1] (input to layer)(N, nin)forward me store
W[l](nout, nin)∂L/∂W = ΔT A[l−1] → (nout, nin)
b[l](nout,)∂L/∂b = Δ.sum(dim=0)
Δ[l] (deltas)(N, nout)Δ[l] = (Δ[l+1] W[l+1]) ⊙ g′(Z[l])

Rule of thumb: kisi bhi cheez ka gradient us cheez ke shape ka hi hota hai. W.grad.shape == W.shape hamesha. Loss mean ho (reduction='mean', default) to batch ka 1/N factor bhi δ me aa jaata hai.

Pseudo-code — poora algorithm

Backpropagation · pseudo-code

# FORWARD (cache sab kuch)
a[0] = x
for l in 1 .. L:
    z[l] = W[l] @ a[l-1] + b[l]          # store z[l]
    a[l] = g(z[l])                        # store a[l]
loss = Loss(a[L], y)

# BACKWARD (ulte order me)
delta[L] = dLoss/da[L] * g'(z[L])        # sigmoid+BCE / softmax+CE: a[L] - y
for l in L .. 1:
    dW[l] = outer(delta[l], a[l-1])       # error at destination x signal at source
    db[l] = delta[l]
    if l > 1:
        delta[l-1] = (W[l].T @ delta[l]) * g'(z[l-1])   # error ko peeche bhejo

# UPDATE (gradient descent - optimizer ka kaam)
for l in 1 .. L:
    W[l] -= lr * dW[l]
    b[l] -= lr * db[l]

Teacher ki slide notation (Prince UDL) me same cheez

Slides me: f0 = β0 + Ω0x, hk = a[fk−1], fk = βk + Ωkhk. Yahan fk = pre-activation (hamara z), hk = activation (hamara a), β = bias, Ω = weight matrix, ℓ = loss. Backward equations:

UDL / slide formδ formMatlab
∂ℓ/∂fkδ[k+1]pre-activation ka gradient
∂ℓ/∂βk = ∂ℓ/∂fk∂L/∂b = δbias gradient = δ
∂ℓ/∂Ωk = (∂ℓ/∂fk) hkT∂L/∂W = δ aTerror × source activation
∂ℓ/∂fk−1 = 𝕀[fk−1 > 0] ⊙ (ΩkT ∂ℓ/∂fk)δ[l] = (WTδ[l+1]) ⊙ g′(z)ReLU ka g′ = indicator 𝕀[z > 0] (1 if positive else 0)

Backward pass kitna mehnga? — "almost free"

  • Backward pass ka cost forward pass ke same order ka hota hai — roughly 1–2× forward ke FLOPs (har layer pe ek matmul δ peeche bhejne ke liye, ek weight gradient ke liye). Poora training step ≈ 3× forward. Memory: forward ki cached activations.
  • Compare: numerical gradient (finite difference) se har parameter ke liye alag forward pass → P parameters = P+1 forward passes. 10 lakh parameters → 10 lakh forward passes vs backprop ka ~1 forward + 1 backward.
  • Aur har weight ke liye chain rule ke saare paths alag-alag gino to paths ki ginti depth ke saath exponentially badhti hai. Backprop δ ko reuse karta hai (dynamic programming), isliye linear time.

Exam Radar

  • δ[l] = ∂L/∂z[l]. Output: sigmoid+BCE → ŷ − y; sigmoid+MSE → (ŷ − y)σ′(z); softmax+CE → ŷ − y.
  • δ[l] = (W[l+1]T δ[l+1]) ⊙ g′(z[l]) — transpose of the next layer's weights, element-wise with own activation slope.
  • ∂L/∂W[l] = δ[l] a[l−1]T (outer product); ∂L/∂b[l] = δ[l]. Gradient shape = parameter shape.
  • Notation w[l]jk: j = destination (this layer), k = source (previous layer).
  • Backward cost ≈ forward cost (same order); backprop = reverse-mode autodiff = chain rule + reuse.
  • MSE with sigmoid output → saturated output pe slow learning; BCE removes σ′ factor.

Galti mat karna

  • BP2 me W[l+1] (agli layer ka) transpose lagta hai, apni layer ka W[l] nahi.
  • BP2 me ⊙ (element-wise) hai, matrix multiply nahi. Shapes check karo: (nl,) ⊙ (nl,).
  • BP3 me source activation a[l−1] (pichhli layer) aata hai, apni activation a[l] nahi. Sheet ka hint: "ŷ1 is the destination's output, not the source's."
  • Sigmoid+BCE ka δ = ŷ − y hai; agar code me nn.Sigmoid + nn.BCELoss lagaya to autograd khud ye cancel handle karta hai — tumhe manually σ′ multiply nahi karna.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

"δ peeche aata hai Wᵀ ke raaste, apne g′ se guna hota hai; weight ka gradient = δ (aage) × a (peeche); bias ka = δ."

13.5 Gradient flow — gradient = raaste ke saare factors ka product

Kahani

Paani ki pipeline socho jo tanki (loss) se shuru hoke ghar-ghar (layers) jaati hai. Har ghar pe ek valve hai jo paani ko kuch percent aage jaane deta hai. Agar har valve sirf 25% aage bhejta hai, to 10 ghar baad paani ki boond bhi nahi bachegi. Agar har valve pump hai jo 1.5 guna kar deta hai, to 20 ghar baad pipe phat jayegi. Backward pass me gradient bhi aise hi har layer ke "valve" se guzarta hai.

Ek simple chain network lo (har layer me ek neuron): x → (w1, σ) → a1 → (w2, σ) → a2 → (w3, σ) → ŷ → L. Chain rule se:

∂L∂w1 = ∂L∂ŷ · σ′(z3) · w3 · σ′(z2) · w2 · σ′(z1) · x
  • Har layer jo gradient ne cross ki, wo ek factor wk · σ′(zk−1) jod deti hai ("valve")
  • General: δ[l] = (W[l+1]Tδ[l+1]) ⊙ g′(z[l]) ko baar-baar lagao → δ[1] me L−1 baar (weight × activation slope) multiply hota hai
  • Product ka size: factors < 1 → gradient vanish; factors > 1 → gradient explode; factors ≈ 1 → healthy flow

Chalo numbers se samjhein

1-1-1 network (13.2) me dekho: δ2 = −0.09906 aur δ1 = −0.009738. Ek layer peeche jaane me gradient kitna chhota hua?

  1. Valve factor: w2 × σ′(z1) = 0.5 × 0.19661 = 0.0983
  2. Check: δ1/δ2 = −0.009738 / −0.09906 = 0.0983

Ek layer me gradient ~10 guna chhota! Agar aisi 5 layers hoti (har baar ~0.1), to pehli layer tak 0.15 = 0.00001 bachta.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Gradient = valves ka product. Har valve = (weight) × (activation ka slope). Valve < 1 → sukha; valve > 1 → baadh.

13.6 Vanishing gradients — gradient peeche jaate-jaate gayab

Kahani

Class me "kaan me baat" (Chinese whispers) game khela hai? Pehla bachcha bolta hai "kal picnic jayenge", aur 15 bachchon ke baad aakhri tak kuch aur hi pahunchta hai — ya bas hulki si fusfusahat. Deep sigmoid network me loss ka sandesh (gradient) bhi pehli layers tak pahunchte-pahunchte itna halka ho jaata hai ki pehli layers ko pata hi nahi chalta unhe kya sudharna hai. Wo bechari random hi reh jaati hain.

Definition

Vanishing gradient problem: deep network me backprop ke dauraan gradients peeche ki (early) layers tak pahunchte-pahunchte exponentially chhote ho jaate hain (≈ 0), kyunki chain rule me bahut saare < 1 factors multiply hote hain. Result: early layers ke weights almost update hi nahi hote — wo seekhna band kar dete hain.

σ′(z) = σ(z)(1 − σ(z)) ≤ 0.25   ⇒   n sigmoid layers ke baad gradient ≤ (0.25)n × (weights ka product)
  • 0.25 = sigmoid ke slope ka maximum (sirf z = 0 pe, jab σ = 0.5: 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.25). Baaki har jagah isse kam.
  • Saturation me (|z| bada) to aur bhi kam: σ′(6) = 0.00247 (activation worksheet ka example).
  • Agar |w| ≤ 1 bhi ho to har layer ka factor ≤ 0.25 — depth ke saath exponential decay.
Layers n (sigmoid)Best case 0.25nMatlab
10.25chauthai bacha
20.0625
30.015625
59.77 × 10−4hazaar guna chhota
109.54 × 10−7~ ek million guna chhota
209.09 × 10−13practically zero

Calculation: 0.2510 = (1/4)10 = 1/1,048,576 ≈ 9.54 × 10−7. Ye bhi "best case" hai — har neuron exactly z = 0 pe ho tab. Asli me aur kam.

Symptoms — kaise pehchaanein?

  • Early (input ke paas wali) layers ke weights almost nahi badalte; unke gradient norms bahut chhote (10−6, 10−9) — jabki last layers ke normal.
  • Loss jaldi plateau pe atak jaata hai (high value pe flat), ya bahut dheere girta hai.
  • Deep model shallow model se bhi kharab train hota hai.
  • Sigmoid/tanh activations saturated (outputs 0/1 ya ±1 ke paas chipke).

Causes — kyun hota hai?

  • Saturating activations: sigmoid (σ′ ≤ 0.25), tanh (tanh′ ≤ 1, aur saturation me ≈ 0).
  • Chhote weights: |w| < 1 ka product (bahut chhota init).
  • Depth: zyada layers = zyada factors multiply. RNN me lambi sequence = time me deep network.
  • Bade weights se bhi ho sakta hai: z bahut bada → sigmoid saturate → σ′ ≈ 0.

Fixes — aur kis chapter me

FixKaise madad karta haiChapter
ReLU family (ReLU, Leaky ReLU, ELU)Positive side pe derivative exactly 1 → factor shrink nahi hotaCh 9
Xavier / He initializationWeights ka variance aisa ki per-layer signal/gradient factor ≈ 1 (Xavier: tanh/sigmoid, He: ReLU)Ch 21
Batch NormalizationHar layer ke z ko normalize → saturation zone se bahar, healthy gradientsCh 20
Residual / skip connectionsy = x + F(x) → ∂y/∂x = 1 + F′ — add gate ka "1" gradient highwayCh 25
LSTM / GRU (RNNs ke liye)Gates + additive cell state → time ke saath gradient multiply-multiply karke nahi marta(syllabus ke bahar, naam yaad rakho)
Output pe sigmoid + BCE (MSE nahi)Output δ = ŷ − y, σ′ factor hat jaata haiCh 11

Code (b): deep Sigmoid MLP vs deep ReLU MLP — layer-wise gradient norms

PyTorch · gradient norm per layer (10 hidden layers, width 64)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

def make_mlp(act, depth=10, width=64, he=False):
    layers, n_in = [], 20
    for _ in range(depth):
        lin = nn.Linear(n_in, width)
        if he:   # He (Kaiming) init: ReLU ke liye variance 2/fan_in
            nn.init.kaiming_normal_(lin.weight, nonlinearity='relu')
            nn.init.zeros_(lin.bias)
        layers += [lin, act()]
        n_in = width
    layers.append(nn.Linear(n_in, 1))           # output layer
    return nn.Sequential(*layers)

def layer_grad_norms(model):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    X = torch.randn(256, 20)                     # 256 fake samples, 20 features
    y = torch.randn(256, 1)
    loss = nn.MSELoss()(model(X), y)
    model.zero_grad()
    loss.backward()
    # har nn.Linear ke weight ka gradient norm (L2)
    return [m.weight.grad.norm().item() for m in model if isinstance(m, nn.Linear)]

torch.manual_seed(42); sig = layer_grad_norms(make_mlp(nn.Sigmoid))
torch.manual_seed(42); rel = layer_grad_norms(make_mlp(nn.ReLU))
torch.manual_seed(42); he  = layer_grad_norms(make_mlp(nn.ReLU, he=True))

print("layer   Sigmoid      ReLU(default)  ReLU+He")
for i, (a, b, c) in enumerate(zip(sig, rel, he), start=1):
    print(f"{i:>5}   {a:.2e}     {b:.2e}       {c:.2e}")
print(f"first/last ratio: sigmoid {sig[0]/sig[-1]:.1e} | relu {rel[0]/rel[-1]:.1e} | relu+he {he[0]/he[-1]:.1e}")

Output

layer   Sigmoid      ReLU(default)  ReLU+He
    1   2.03e-09     7.83e-05       1.07e+00
    2   2.82e-08     1.90e-04       4.38e+00
    3   2.12e-07     2.90e-04       4.83e+00
    4   1.60e-06     4.72e-04       5.30e+00
    5   1.00e-05     7.90e-04       5.41e+00
    6   6.90e-05     2.03e-03       6.42e+00
    7   5.11e-04     3.77e-03       8.50e+00
    8   3.58e-03     1.13e-02       7.95e+00
    9   2.66e-02     2.52e-02       7.46e+00
   10   1.73e-01     6.59e-02       7.49e+00
   11   1.27e+00     1.76e-01       2.33e+01
first/last ratio: sigmoid 1.6e-09 | relu 4.4e-04 | relu+he 4.6e-02

Padho isko (layer 1 = input ke paas, layer 11 = output layer):

  • Sigmoid: output layer pe gradient 1.27, pehli layer pe 2 × 10−9 — arab guna chhota. Har layer pe ~7× girawat (σ′ ≤ 0.25 × chhote default weights). Pehli layers kuch nahi seekhengi.
  • ReLU (default PyTorch init): girawat kaafi kam (~1.5–3× per layer), lekin phir bhi 10−4 ratio. Kyun? PyTorch ka default nn.Linear init (uniform ±1/√fan_in) ReLU ke liye thoda chhota hai.
  • ReLU + He init: layers 2–10 sab ~4–8 ke range me — gradient poore network me barabar beh raha hai. Yahi fix ka combo hai: sahi activation + sahi init (Chapter 21).

Naye APIs: nn.init.kaiming_normal_(tensor, nonlinearity='relu') = He init in-place (underscore); nn.init.zeros_ bias zero; p.grad.norm() = gradient ka L2 norm (√ of sum of squares) — gradient health check karne ka standard tareeka; isinstance(m, nn.Linear) se Sequential me se sirf Linear layers chuni.

Exam Radar

  • σ′ max = 0.25 ⇒ n sigmoid layers ⇒ gradient ≤ 0.25n; 0.2510 ≈ 9.5 × 10−7.
  • Vanishing hits early layers (input ke paas) sabse zyada; ye sabse dheere seekhti hain.
  • tanh better than sigmoid (max slope 1, zero-centered) lekin phir bhi vanish karta hai. ReLU: slope 1 for z > 0 → "no vanishing gradient for positive inputs" (teacher slide), lekin dying ReLU (z < 0 pe slope 0) ka risk → Leaky ReLU.
  • Fixes: ReLU family, Xavier/He init, BatchNorm, residual connections, LSTM/GRU (RNN), gradient-friendly loss (BCE with sigmoid).
  • History: Hochreiter (1991) aur Bengio, Simard & Frasconi (1994) ne vanishing gradient formally dikhaya.
  • Learning rate badhane se vanishing theek nahi hota — early aur late layers ka ratio wahi rehta hai.

Galti mat karna

  • Vanishing gradient ka matlab "loss zero ho gaya" nahi hai. Loss high pe atka hota hai; gradient zero ke paas hota hai.
  • Vanishing gradient (bahut saare chhote factors ka product) aur dying ReLU (neuron hamesha z < 0, gradient exactly 0) alag cheezein hain.
  • "Last layers pe vanish hota hai" — galat. Gradient loss ke paas (last layers) sabse bada, input ke paas (first layers) sabse chhota.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

"0.25 ka pahaada": 0.25, 0.0625, 0.0156... 10 layers me ek-millionth. Sigmoid ko hidden layers se nikaalo, ReLU + He lagao.

13.7 Exploding gradients — gradient ka visphot, aur gradient clipping

Kahani

Shaadi ke function me mic speaker ke paas le jao — "kuuuuueeeee!" Speaker ki awaaz mic me jaati hai, amplify hoke speaker se nikalti hai, phir mic me... har round me awaaz badhti hai, aur kuch hi second me kaan phaad screech. Ye hai feedback loop with gain > 1. Deep/recurrent network me agar har layer ka factor 1 se bada ho, to gradient bhi aise hi har layer me badh-badh ke "inf" ho jaata hai, aur weights NaN ban jaate hain.

Definition

Exploding gradient problem: backprop me gradients layers (ya RNN me time steps) ke through multiply hote-hote exponentially bade ho jaate hain. Result: weight updates itne bade ki training unstable — loss upar-neeche koodta hai, aur aakhir me inf/NaN.

per-layer factor |w · g′(z)| > 1   ⇒   gradient ∝ (factor)n → ∞
  • Example: w = 6 aur σ′ = 0.25 → factor 6 × 0.25 = 1.5 per layer
  • ReLU/linear layers me factor = |w| (active part) → bade weights seedhe explode
  • RNN me same weight matrix har time step pe multiply → 100 time steps = 100 factors
Layers n1.5n
11.5
57.59
1057.67
203325.3 ≈ 3.3 × 103
301.92 × 105
506.38 × 108

Sirf 1.5 ka chhota sa factor, aur 20 layers me gradient 3325 guna! Learning rate 0.01 ho to bhi step 33 ka — weights kahan ke kahan.

Symptoms

  • Loss achanak NaN ya inf print hone lagta hai.
  • Loss wild jumps karta hai (293 → 15 → 246 → inf) — smooth decrease nahi.
  • Weights bahut bade ho jaate hain ya NaN; gradient norm me badi spikes.

Causes

  • Bade initial weights (|w| > 1 ka product).
  • Deep networks aur khaaskar RNNs (same weight baar-baar).
  • High learning rate: bada step → bade activations → aur bade gradients (feedback).
  • Unscaled input features (multiply gate: gradient ∝ input) — isliye StandardScaler.

Fixes

FixKaiseChapter
Gradient clipping (by norm / by value)Backward ke baad, step se pehle, gradient ka size cap kar doyahin, neeche
Lower learning rate / LR scheduleChhote steps, feedback loop todoCh 15
Proper init (Xavier/He)Per-layer factor ≈ 1 rakhoCh 21
Batch NormalizationActivations ka scale controlCh 20
Weight decay (L2)Weights ko bada hone se rokta haiCh 19
Input scalingStandardScaler: features ~ mean 0, std 113.8

Gradient clipping — do tareeke

By norm:   agar ‖g‖ > c   to   g ← g · c‖g‖
By value:   gi ← clamp(gi, −c, c)   (har component alag se)
  • ‖g‖ = saare parameters ke gradients ko ek lamba vector maan ke L2 norm: √(Σ gi2)
  • c = threshold (max_norm ya clip_value), jaise 1.0
  • By norm: direction same, sirf length chhoti — isliye zyada popular (Pascanu et al., 2013, RNNs ke liye)
  • By value: har component ±c pe kaata → direction badal sakti hai
  • Agar ‖g‖ ≤ c to clip-by-norm kuch nahi karta

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: gradient g = (3, 4). (a) max_norm = 1 se clip by norm; (b) clip_value = 0.5 se clip by value.

  1. Norm: ‖g‖ = √(32 + 42) = √25 = 5 > 1, to clip karna hai
  2. (a) Scale factor: 1/5 = 0.2 → g = (3 × 0.2, 4 × 0.2) = (0.6, 0.8), naya norm = √(0.36 + 0.64) = 1. Direction same (ratio 3:4 bacha).
  3. (b) Har component ko [−0.5, 0.5] me kaato: (min(3, 0.5), min(4, 0.5)) = (0.5, 0.5). Ratio 3:4 se 1:1 ho gaya → direction badal gayi.

Jawab: by norm → (0.6, 0.8); by value → (0.5, 0.5).

PyTorch · clip_grad_norm_ vs clip_grad_value_

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# ek chhota parameter jiska gradient hum khud set karenge: g = [3, 4] -> norm 5
p = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(2))
p.grad = torch.tensor([3.0, 4.0])
total = torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_([p], max_norm=1.0)
print("norm before:", total)          # returns the ORIGINAL total norm
print("after clip_grad_norm_ :", p.grad, "| new norm:", p.grad.norm())

p.grad = torch.tensor([3.0, 4.0])
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_value_([p], clip_value=0.5)
print("after clip_grad_value_:", p.grad)

p.grad = torch.tensor([0.3, 0.4])     # norm 0.5 < 1 -> kuch nahi badlega
torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_([p], max_norm=1.0)
print("small grad untouched  :", p.grad)

Output

norm before: tensor(5.)
after clip_grad_norm_ : tensor([0.6000, 0.8000]) | new norm: tensor(1.0000)
after clip_grad_value_: tensor([0.5000, 0.5000])
small grad untouched  : tensor([0.3000, 0.4000])

API details: torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(parameters, max_norm, norm_type=2.0) — parameters = model.parameters() (ya list), max_norm = threshold, norm_type default 2 (L2). Saare parameters ka combined norm nikalta hai, in-place scale karta hai (underscore), aur clipping se pehle wala total norm return karta hai (logging ke liye useful). clip_grad_value_(parameters, clip_value) har gradient element ko [−clip_value, clip_value] me clamp karta hai, kuch return nahi karta.

Clipping training loop me kahan? — backward() ke BAAD, step() se PEHLE

PyTorch · exploding vs clipped training

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

def train(clip):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    X = torch.randn(64, 3) * 10            # bade-bade input (scaling nahi kiya!)
    y = X.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)         # target bhi bada: (64, 1)
    model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(3, 16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16, 1))
    opt = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
    loss_fn = nn.MSELoss()
    out = []
    for epoch in range(1, 31):
        model.train()
        pred = model(X)                    # forward
        loss = loss_fn(pred, y)            # loss
        opt.zero_grad()                    # purane grads saaf
        loss.backward()                    # backward: grads bharo
        if clip:
            nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0)  # backward ke BAAD, step se PEHLE
        opt.step()                         # update
        if epoch in (1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 30):
            out.append(f"{epoch}:{loss.item():.4g}")
    return out

print("no clip  :", "  ".join(train(False)))
print("with clip:", "  ".join(train(True)))

Output

no clip  : 1:293.2  2:15.38  3:19.2  5:246.4  10:inf  30:nan
with clip: 1:293.2  2:290.9  3:288.7  5:284.2  10:273.1  30:229.5

Bina clipping: loss 293 → 15 → 19 → 246 → inf → nan — exploding ke saare lakshan (wild jumps, phir inf/NaN). Clipping ke saath: dheere lekin stable girawat. (Asli ilaaj yahan inputs ko StandardScaler se scale karna aur LR kam karna bhi hai — clipping emergency brake hai.) Clip ko backward() se pehle lagaoge to clip karne ko gradient hi nahi hoga; step() ke baad lagaoge to update pehle hi bade gradient se ho chuka hoga.

VanishingExploding
Per-layer factor< 1 (e.g. σ′ ≤ 0.25)> 1 (e.g. 1.5)
Gradient at early layers≈ 0huge / inf
Loss behaviourplateau, bahut slowwild jumps, NaN/inf
Common causesigmoid/tanh saturation, small weights, depthlarge weights, RNNs, high LR
Main fixesReLU, He/Xavier, BN, residual, LSTM/GRUclipping, lower LR, init, BN, weight decay
Clipping helps?Nahi (chhote gradient ko bada nahi karta)Haan

Exam Radar

  • 1.520 ≈ 3325; 1.510 ≈ 57.7. Factor > 1 → explode.
  • Gradient clipping: torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), max_norm=1.0) — between loss.backward() and optimizer.step().
  • Clip by norm keeps direction; clip by value may change direction. Clipping exploding ke liye hai, vanishing ke liye nahi.
  • RNNs me exploding + vanishing dono common (same weight repeated) → clipping (exploding) + LSTM/GRU (vanishing).
  • Symptom NaN loss → pehle LR kam karo / clip / input scaling check karo.

Galti mat karna

  • clip_grad_norm_ ka order: zero_grad → backward → clip → step. Clip ko step ke baad likhna bekaar hai.
  • Underscore wala naam (clip_grad_norm_) in-place version hai; purana clip_grad_norm (bina underscore) deprecated hai.
  • max_norm poore model ke combined norm pe lagta hai, har layer pe alag-alag nahi.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Mic-speaker screech = exploding; kaan-me-baat = vanishing. Screech ka ilaaj volume knob (clipping + kam LR); fusfusahat ka ilaaj behtar raasta (ReLU, He, BN, residual).

13.8 Poora PyTorch training pipeline (Lab 5) — har line kyun hai

Kahani

Maa biryani banati hai to teen phase hote hain: tayyari (chawal dhona, sabzi kaatna, masale naapna), pakana (baar-baar chakhna aur namak-mirch adjust karna), aur parosna (mehmaan ko dena — ab adjust nahi karte, bas khilate hain). Deep learning pipeline bhi bilkul aisa: data ki tayyari → training loop (forward = chakhna, backward = kya kam-zyada hai, step = adjust) → evaluation (bas test, koi adjust nahi).

Lab 5 ka goal (unke shabdon me): "By the end of this lab, the training loop and the custom model class should no longer feel like magic — you should be able to explain why every line exists." Task: Wisconsin Breast Cancer dataset — 569 patients, 30 numeric features, label M (malignant) / B (benign). Model: logistic regression as nn.Module (nn.Linear(30, 1) + nn.Sigmoid), BCE loss, SGD, lr = 0.1, 25 epochs, full-batch.

PyTorch · Lab 5 full pipeline (breast cancer, nn.Module, full-batch GD)

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler, LabelEncoder

# ---------- Step 1: reproducibility ----------
SEED = 42
np.random.seed(SEED)                 # numpy ka random fix
torch.manual_seed(SEED)              # torch ka random fix (weights ka init same aayega)

# ---------- Step 2: load + clean ----------
url = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gscdit/Breast-Cancer-Detection/refs/heads/master/data.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(url)                                  # (569, 33)
df.drop(columns=['id', 'Unnamed: 32'], inplace=True)   # id = sirf naam, Unnamed: 32 = khaali column -> (569, 31)
X = df.drop(columns=['diagnosis'])                     # 30 features
y = df['diagnosis']                                    # 'M' / 'B'

# ---------- Step 3: split PEHLE, scaling BAAD me ----------
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.2, random_state=SEED)

scaler = StandardScaler()                 # x' = (x - mean) / std
X_train = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)   # mean/std SIRF train se seekho
X_test = scaler.transform(X_test)         # test pe wahi mean/std lagao (fit nahi!)

encoder = LabelEncoder()                  # alphabetical: 'B' -> 0, 'M' -> 1
y_train = encoder.fit_transform(y_train)
y_test = encoder.transform(y_test)

# ---------- Step 4: numpy -> tensors (float32!) ----------
X_train_tensor = torch.from_numpy(X_train.astype(np.float32))   # (455, 30)
X_test_tensor = torch.from_numpy(X_test.astype(np.float32))     # (114, 30)
y_train_tensor = torch.from_numpy(y_train.astype(np.float32))   # (455,)  1-D!
y_test_tensor = torch.from_numpy(y_test.astype(np.float32))     # (114,)
print("X_train_tensor:", X_train_tensor.shape, X_train_tensor.dtype)
print("y_train_tensor:", y_train_tensor.shape)

# ---------- Step 5: model as nn.Module ----------
class MySimpleNN(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, num_features):
        super().__init__()                          # nn.Module ki machinery register karo
        self.linear = nn.Linear(num_features, 1)    # (N, 30) -> (N, 1), weight (1, 30) + bias (1,)
        self.sigmoid = nn.Sigmoid()                 # raw score -> probability (0, 1)

    def forward(self, features):
        out = self.linear(features)                 # z = w.x + b
        out = self.sigmoid(out)                     # y_hat = sigmoid(z)
        return out

model = MySimpleNN(X_train_tensor.shape[1])         # 30 features
loss_function = nn.BCELoss()                        # probabilities + float targets, SAME shape
optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)   # model.parameters() = sab weights/biases
epochs = 25

# ---------- Step 6: training loop ----------
for epoch in range(epochs):
    model.train()                                   # training mode (dropout/BN on)
    y_pred = model(X_train_tensor)                  # 1. forward: (455, 30) -> (455, 1)
    loss = loss_function(y_pred, y_train_tensor.view(-1, 1))   # 2. loss: target (455,) -> (455, 1)
    optimizer.zero_grad()                           # 3. purane gradients saaf
    loss.backward()                                 # 4. backprop: har parameter ka .grad bharo
    optimizer.step()                                # 5. update: w = w - lr * w.grad
    if epoch in (0, 1, 2, 9, 24):
        print(f'Epoch: {epoch + 1}, Loss: {loss.item():.4f}')

# ---------- Step 7: evaluation ----------
model.eval()                                        # evaluation mode
with torch.no_grad():                               # graph mat banao: memory + time bachao
    y_prob = model(X_test_tensor)                   # (114, 1) probabilities
    y_pred_labels = (y_prob > 0.5).float()          # threshold 0.5 -> 0/1
    accuracy = (y_pred_labels == y_test_tensor.view(-1, 1)).float().mean()
print(f'Accuracy: {accuracy.item():.4f}')

Output

X_train_tensor: torch.Size([455, 30]) torch.float32
y_train_tensor: torch.Size([455])
Epoch: 1, Loss: 0.6704
Epoch: 2, Loss: 0.5365
Epoch: 3, Loss: 0.4555
Epoch: 10, Loss: 0.2672
Epoch: 25, Loss: 0.1793
Accuracy: 0.9825

Ye numbers Lab 5 notebook ke run se exact match karte hain (Epoch 1: 0.6704 … Epoch 25: 0.1793, Accuracy 0.9825). Loss har epoch girta gaya — training kaam kar rahi hai.

Har line ka role — ek table me

LineKya karti haiHata do to?
torch.manual_seed(42)Random init fix → har run same resultHar run me alag loss/accuracy
df.drop(columns=[...])Non-feature columns (id, khaali column) hataoid ek bekaar "feature" ban jaata; NaN column error deta
train_test_split(..., test_size=0.2)20% data test ke liye alag (455 train / 114 test)Model ko unseen data pe judge hi nahi kar paoge
scaler.fit_transform(X_train)Train ka mean/std seekh ke scale karoUnscaled features (area ~2000 vs smoothness ~0.1) → bade-chhote gradients, slow/unstable training
scaler.transform(X_test)Test pe train wala mean/std lagaoTest pe fit kiya to data leakage (test ki info training me ghus gayi)
LabelEncoder'B'/'M' strings → 0/1 numbersStrings tensor nahi ban sakti
.astype(np.float32)numpy float64 → float32RuntimeError: Double vs Float
super().__init__()nn.Module ki machinery (parameter registry) chaluLayers assign karte hi error
self.linear = nn.Linear(30, 1)Learnable w (1×30) + b; auto-registeredKoi parameter hi nahi
forward()Computation define karta hai; call model(x) se (hooks bhi chalte hain)Model kuch compute nahi karega
nn.BCELoss()Binary cross-entropy: probabilities vs 0/1 targetsLoss hi nahi → backward kis cheez ka?
optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)Optimizer ko parameters ki list aur step sizestep() kise update kare?
model.train()Training mode (Dropout/BatchNorm training behaviour)Is model me farak nahi (dropout/BN nahi); bade models me galat behaviour
y_pred = model(X)Forward pass + graph banta hai—
.view(-1, 1)Target (455,) → (455, 1), prediction ke shape jaisaBCELoss ValueError; MSE-type losses me silent (N, N) broadcasting bug
optimizer.zero_grad()Sab .grad saaf (accumulation rokna)Gradients jud-jud ke galat updates (neeche demo)
loss.backward()Backprop: har parameter ka ∂L/∂θ .grad me.grad None/purana → step kuch nahi / galat karega
optimizer.step()θ ← θ − lr · θ.grad (SGD)Weights kabhi nahi badlenge, loss constant
loss.item()Tensor → Python float (logging)Tensor store karoge to graph bhi pakda rahega (memory)
model.eval()Evaluation mode (Dropout off, BN running stats)Dropout wale models me random, galat predictions
torch.no_grad()Eval me graph mat banaoMemory + compute waste (galat answer nahi, par mehnga)
(y_prob > 0.5).float()Probability → class label (threshold 0.5)Accuracy compare nahi hoga
(... == ...).float().mean()Sahi predictions ka fraction = accuracy—

Paanch kadam ka loop — andar kya hota hai

  1. Forward y_pred = model(X): z = XWT + b, ŷ = σ(z). Autograd graph banata hai aur X, ŷ jaisi values cache karta hai.
  2. Loss loss = loss_function(...): ek scalar; graph ka last node.
  3. zero_grad: model.parameters() ke sabka .grad saaf (PyTorch 2.x: None set). Lab ka note: "The call must happen every epoch, before backward() — the exact position relative to forward()/loss computation does not matter." Isliye Lab 6 me order zero_grad → forward → loss → backward → step hai aur Lab 5 me forward → loss → zero_grad → backward → step — dono sahi.
  4. Backward loss.backward(): graph ulta chalta hai (13.4 wala BP1–BP4 automatically); har leaf parameter ke .grad me ∂L/∂θ (shape = θ ka shape). Graph phir free.
  5. Step optimizer.step(): SGD ke liye θ ← θ − lr · θ.grad, har parameter pe (andar no_grad me). Momentum/Adam ka step alag formula (Ch 16, Ch 17), lekin loop same.

Mini-batch version (Lab 6 Part 2 style) — preview

Lab 5 full-batch hai (455 rows ek saath, 1 update per epoch). Lab 6 me DataLoader(batch_size=32, shuffle=True) se mini-batches — loop me ek andar wala for aa jaata hai. Details Chapter 14 me; yahan sirf shape dekho:

PyTorch · same pipeline, mini-batch loop

from torch.utils.data import TensorDataset, DataLoader

torch.manual_seed(42)
model = MySimpleNN(X_train_tensor.shape[1])                    # fresh model
optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)

train_ds = TensorDataset(X_train_tensor, y_train_tensor.view(-1, 1))   # (455, 30), (455, 1)
train_loader = DataLoader(train_ds, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)

for epoch in range(5):
    model.train()
    epoch_loss = 0.0
    for xb, yb in train_loader:                 # har batch: xb (32, 30), yb (32, 1)
        y_pred = model(xb)                      # forward
        loss = loss_function(y_pred, yb)        # loss
        optimizer.zero_grad()                   # grads saaf
        loss.backward()                         # backprop
        optimizer.step()                        # update
        epoch_loss += loss.item() * xb.size(0)  # batch loss x batch size
    print(f"Epoch {epoch + 1}: avg loss = {epoch_loss / len(train_ds):.4f}, updates = {len(train_loader)}")

Output

Epoch 1: avg loss = 0.3472, updates = 15
Epoch 2: avg loss = 0.1901, updates = 15
Epoch 3: avg loss = 0.1534, updates = 15
Epoch 4: avg loss = 0.1337, updates = 15
Epoch 5: avg loss = 0.1226, updates = 15

455/32 = 14.2 → 15 batches (aakhri batch 7 rows ka) → 15 updates per epoch. Isliye 5 epochs me hi loss 0.12 tak, jabki full-batch me 25 epochs ke baad 0.18.

model.train() vs model.eval()

Kuch layers training aur testing me alag behave karti hain: Dropout (training me random neurons band karta hai, eval me sab on) aur BatchNorm (training me batch ke mean/var, eval me running averages) — details Chapter 20. model.train() / model.eval() sirf ek flag (module.training) set karte hain jo ye layers padhti hain.

PyTorch · train vs eval mode (Dropout demo)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

torch.manual_seed(3)
drop = nn.Dropout(p=0.5)
x = torch.ones(6)

drop.train()                 # training mode (default)
print("train mode:", drop(x))
drop.eval()                  # evaluation mode
print("eval mode :", drop(x))
print("drop.training =", drop.training)

Output

train mode: tensor([2., 2., 0., 2., 0., 0.])
eval mode : tensor([1., 1., 1., 1., 1., 1.])
drop.training = False

Training me aadhe zero, baaki ×2 (1/(1−p) scaling, taaki expected value same rahe); eval me sab as-it-is. model.eval() aur torch.no_grad() alag kaam hain: eval() layers ka behaviour badalta hai, no_grad() gradient recording band karta hai. Evaluation me dono chahiye (Lab 6: "use model.eval() + torch.no_grad() for evaluation"). Aur eval ke baad training dobara shuru karo to model.train() wapas lagana mat bhoolo — isliye loop ke andar har epoch ki shuruaat me likhte hain.

Lab ke pitfalls — numbers ke saath

Pitfall 1: zero_grad() bhool gaye.

PyTorch · with vs without zero_grad

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

def run(use_zero_grad):
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    X = torch.randn(100, 2)
    y = (X @ torch.tensor([[2.0], [-1.0]])) + 0.5      # simple linear target, (100, 1)
    model = nn.Linear(2, 1)
    opt = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.1)
    losses = []
    for epoch in range(1, 21):
        loss = nn.MSELoss()(model(X), y)
        if use_zero_grad:
            opt.zero_grad()
        loss.backward()
        opt.step()
        if epoch in (1, 3, 5, 10, 20):
            losses.append(f"{epoch}:{loss.item():.3f}")
    return "  ".join(losses)

print("with zero_grad   :", run(True))
print("WITHOUT zero_grad:", run(False))

Output

with zero_grad   : 1:4.992  3:2.658  5:1.428  10:0.308  20:0.015
WITHOUT zero_grad: 1:4.992  3:1.710  5:0.196  10:3.956  20:1.465

Bina zero_grad: har step ka gradient = ab tak ke saare gradients ka sum → step bade hote jaate hain → pehle tez girta hai, phir overshoot karke loss upar-neeche (0.196 → 3.956). Sahi version smoothly 0.015 tak. (Lab 5 activity ka reflection sawaal: symptom = loss curve erratic/upar-neeche.)

Pitfall 2: (N,) vs (N, 1) shape — broadcasting. Model output (N, 1), labels (N,).

PyTorch · shape aur dtype pitfalls

import warnings
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
warnings.simplefilter("always")

pred = torch.tensor([[0.9], [0.2], [0.8], [0.3]])   # (4, 1)  model output
y    = torch.tensor([1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0])           # (4,)    labels

print("(pred - y).shape :", (pred - y).shape)        # broadcasting -> (4, 4) !!

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    bad = nn.MSELoss()(pred, y)
    print("MSELoss mismatched:", round(bad.item(), 4), "| warning:", str(w[0].message)[:60], "...")
good = nn.MSELoss()(pred, y.view(-1, 1))
print("MSELoss matched   :", round(good.item(), 4))

try:
    nn.BCELoss()(pred, y)
except ValueError as e:
    print("BCELoss mismatched -> ValueError:", str(e)[:70], "...")
print("BCELoss matched   :", round(nn.BCELoss()(pred, y.view(-1, 1)).item(), 4))

# Double vs Float
layer = nn.Linear(3, 1)
x64 = torch.from_numpy(np.ones((2, 3)))             # numpy default float64
print("dtype:", x64.dtype)
try:
    layer(x64)
except RuntimeError as e:
    print("RuntimeError:", e)
print("fixed:", layer(x64.float()).dtype)

Output

(pred - y).shape : torch.Size([4, 4])
MSELoss mismatched: 0.345 | warning: Using a target size (torch.Size([4])) that is different to t ...
MSELoss matched   : 0.045
BCELoss mismatched -> ValueError: Using a target size (torch.Size([4])) that is different to the input s ...
BCELoss matched   : 0.2271
dtype: torch.float64
RuntimeError: mat1 and mat2 must have the same dtype, but got Double and Float
fixed: torch.float32
  • (4, 1) − (4,) → (4, 4): har prediction har label se compare — bakwas. MSELoss sirf ek warning deta hai aur galat number (0.345 vs sahi 0.045) de deta hai — silent bug. Lab ki warning ("PyTorch broadcasts (N,) against (N,1) into an (N,N) tensor ... silently producing a nonsensical loss") isi ke baare me hai.
  • Current PyTorch me nn.BCELoss mismatch pe seedha ValueError deta hai (achha hai, bug pakda gaya). Dono case me ilaaj same: y.view(-1, 1) (ya .reshape(-1, 1), ya .unsqueeze(1)).
  • -1 in view(-1, 1) = "is dimension ka size khud calculate karo".

Pitfall 3: Double vs Float. NumPy default float64 ("Double"), nn.Linear weights float32 ("Float"). Error message purane version me "expected scalar type Float but found Double", naye me "mat1 and mat2 must have the same dtype". Ilaaj: .astype(np.float32) before torch.from_numpy, ya torch.tensor(arr, dtype=torch.float32), ya .float().

Pitfall 4: eval me torch.no_grad() bhool gaye.

PyTorch · no_grad ke bina eval

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

model = nn.Linear(3, 1)
X_test = torch.randn(4, 3)

out = model(X_test)                      # bina no_grad
print("without no_grad:", out.requires_grad, out.grad_fn)

with torch.no_grad():
    out = model(X_test)                  # no_grad ke andar
print("with no_grad   :", out.requires_grad, out.grad_fn)

Output

without no_grad: True <AddmmBackward0 object at 0x7fde0e90ce20>
with no_grad   : False None

Bina no_grad har eval forward graph banata hai (AddmmBackward0 = matmul + add ka backward node) aur activations memory me rakhta hai — bade test set pe memory khatam ho sakti hai. Answer galat nahi hota, bas faltu kharcha.

Pitfall 5: data leakage. scaler.fit_transform poore data pe (split se pehle) ya test pe → test ka mean/std training me ghus jaata hai, accuracy jhoothi achhi. Rule: split pehle, fit sirf train pe, transform dono pe.

Aur chhote traps: nn.BCELoss ko probabilities chahiye (sigmoid ke baad) — agar model raw logits deta hai to nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss use karo (sigmoid + BCE ek saath, numerically zyada stable; Lab 5 post-lab Q2). Targets float hone chahiye (isliye labels bhi float32). model(x) likho, model.forward(x) nahi (hooks skip ho jaate hain).

Exam Radar

  • Loop order: forward → loss → zero_grad → backward → step (zero_grad kahin bhi backward se pehle chalega).
  • loss.backward() gradients compute karta hai; optimizer.step() parameters update karta hai; optimizer.zero_grad() gradients reset karta hai.
  • Gradients accumulate by default → zero_grad zaroori. (Kabhi jaan-boojh ke accumulate karte hain: bada effective batch, "gradient accumulation".)
  • Scaler: fit_transform on train, transform on test. LabelEncoder alphabetical: B → 0, M → 1.
  • Lab 5 numbers: 569 rows, 30 features, split 455/114, lr 0.1, 25 epochs, final loss 0.1793, test accuracy 0.9825.
  • Shapes: nn.Linear(30, 1): input (N, 30) → output (N, 1); weight shape (1, 30), bias (1,). Labels ko .view(-1, 1).
  • Evaluation: model.eval() + with torch.no_grad(); prediction = (prob > 0.5).float(); accuracy = (pred == y).float().mean().
  • model.train()/eval() Dropout aur BatchNorm ka behaviour badalte hain; no_grad gradient tracking.

Galti mat karna

  • optimizer.step() ko loss.backward() se pehle mat likhna — step ko gradient chahiye.
  • model.eval() ko torch.no_grad() ka replacement mat samajhna (aur ulta bhi nahi).
  • Test set pe fit_transform = leakage. Test pe sirf transform.
  • train_losses.append(loss) (tensor) ke bajaye loss.item() append karo.
  • Optimizer banate waqt model.parameters() pass karna — model nahi.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

"Forward, Loss, Zero, Backward, Step" — "Falooda Lene Zaroor Bazaar Saath" chalo. Aur khilate waqt (eval) chakhna band: eval() + no_grad().

Chapter 14

Gradient Descent ke Types (Vanilla/Batch, SGD, Mini-batch)

Loss landscape · update rule θ ← θ − η∇L · w² wala hisaab · convex / non-convex · saddle · plateau · Batch GD · SGD · Mini-batch · epoch / iteration · DataLoader

Ab tak humne seekha: model ek guess deta hai, loss batata hai ki guess kitna galat hai (Chapter 11), aur backprop / autograd batata hai ki har weight ke liye loss ka gradient kya hai (Chapter 12, Chapter 13). Training loop me ek line thi optimizer.step(). Is chapter me hum dekhenge ki wo line andar se kya karti hai, aur ek bahut important sawaal: ek update ke liye kitna data use karein? Saara data? Ek row? Ya chhota group? Isi se teen naam bante hain: Batch GD, SGD, Mini-batch GD.

14.1 Kahani: kohre wala pahad (loss landscape)

Kahani

Socho tum Manali ke ek pahad par ho. Raat hai, ghana kohra (fog) hai, aur tumhari aankhon par patti bandhi hai. Tumhe neeche gaon tak pahunchna hai, jo ghaati (valley) ki sabse neechi jagah par hai. Tum poora pahad dekh nahi sakte. Bas ek cheez kar sakte ho: pairon se mehsoos karo ki zameen kis taraf dhalaan (slope) le rahi hai.

Smart tareeka kya hoga? Jis taraf zameen sabse tez upar ja rahi hai, uska ulta pakdo, aur ek chhota kadam lo. Phir ruk kar dobara mehsoos karo. Phir kadam. Phir mehsoos. Jab zameen bilkul sapaat lage (slope ≈ 0), samjho tum neeche pahunch gaye.

Bas, yahi Gradient Descent hai. Pahad = loss surface. Tumhari position = model ke weights. Uchaai (height) = loss. Pairon se slope mehsoos karna = gradient nikalna. Kadam = update.

Ab is kahani ko model ki duniya me translate karte hain:

Kahani meDeep Learning me
Pahad ki zameen (poora terrain)Loss landscape / loss surface: har possible weight-combination par loss kitna hai
Tum kahan khade ho (latitude, longitude)Parameters θ (saare weights aur biases)
Wahan ki uchaaiLoss L(θ) — ek number
Pairon se dhalaan mehsoos karnaGradient ∇L(θ) nikalna (backprop / loss.backward())
Kadam ki lambaiLearning rate η (eta), code me lr
Ek kadam lenaEk update (optimizer.step())
Gaon (sabse neechi jagah)Minimum — jahan loss sabse kam hai

Training ka asli goal ek line me: woh θ dhoondho jisse loss sabse chhota ho. Isko math me likhte hain:

θ̂ = argminθ L(θ)
  • argmin = "woh value batao jahan cheez minimum hoti hai" (minimum value nahi, balki kahan minimum hai — uska address).
  • θ̂ (theta-hat) = sabse achhe parameters. Lecture slides me isi ko ϕ̂ = argminϕ L[ϕ] likha hai (Prince ki book ki notation, ϕ = phi = parameters).

Seedha saare options try kyun nahi kar lete?

Teacher ke lecture me ek delivery company ka example tha: ek hi parameter w (minutes per km). Unhone w ki 561 alag values par loss nikaal kar poora bowl-shaped curve bana diya, aur neeche wala point aankh se dikh gaya (bottom w ≈ 2.56 par tha). Par ye luxury sirf 1 parameter me milti hai. Ek neural network me laakhon parameters hote hain. Agar har parameter ki sirf 10 values bhi try karo, to 1010,00,000 combinations — brahmand khatam ho jayega, gin nahi paoge. Isliye humein chahiye ek smart, iterative search: jahan khade ho, wahin ki jaankari se agla kadam decide karo.

Aur dhyaan do: ek jagah ka loss (sirf uchaai) se direction nahi pata chalti. "Loss = 28.149" sunke tum nahi bata sakte ki w badhana hai ya ghatana. Direction ke liye chahiye aas-paas ki jaankari = slope = gradient.

14.2 Gradient upar ki taraf, isliye ulta chalo — update rule

Yaad karo Chapter 2: derivative = slope. Agar slope positive hai, matlab w badhane se loss badhta hai. Gradient (saare partial derivatives ka vector) hamesha steepest increase, yaani sabse tez uphill direction point karta hai. Humein neeche jaana hai, to hum gradient ka ulta (negative) lete hain.

Definition

Gradient Descent: ek iterative optimization algorithm jo baar-baar do kaam karta hai — (1) abhi ki position par loss ka gradient nikalo, (2) gradient ke ulte direction me ek chhota kadam lo. Ye tab tak chalta hai jab tak gradient lagbhag zero na ho jaye (ya steps khatam na ho jayein).

θt+1 = θt − η · ∇L(θt)
  • θt = abhi ke parameters (step number t par). θt+1 = update ke baad naye parameters.
  • ∇L(θt) = "nabla L" = gradient: har parameter ke liye ∂L/∂θ ka vector. Ye direction deta hai (uphill), aur iska size batata hai slope kitna tez hai.
  • η (eta) = learning rate, ek chhota positive number (jaise 0.1, 0.01). Ye kadam ka size control karta hai.
  • minus (−) sign = "ulta chalo". Gradient uphill bolta hai, hum downhill jaate hain. Yahi poore formula ki jaan hai.

Ek hi formula, alag-alag kapde: course ke alag files me ye same rule alag notation me likha hai. MCQ me koi bhi aa sakta hai, sab ek hi cheez hain:

  • Lecture slides (Prince): ϕ ← ϕ − α · ∂L/∂ϕ (ϕ = parameters, α = learning rate)
  • Worksheet 05: θt+1 = θt − α∇L(θt)
  • Colab notebook: θt+1 = θt − η∇J(θt) (J = loss ka doosra naam, "cost function")
  • Lab 6: Wn = W0 − η · ∂L/∂w (W0 = purana weight, Wn = naya weight)

Toh α = η = lr = learning rate, aur L = J = loss = cost. Bas naam alag hain.

Sign ka khel (MCQ favourite)

  • Gradient positive (+) → θ − η·(+) → θ ghatega (left/negative direction me jayega). Kyun? Kyunki positive slope ka matlab hai right side upar ja rahi hai, to left jao.
  • Gradient negative (−) → θ − η·(−) = θ + kuch → θ badhega (right jayega).
  • Gradient zero → θ change nahi hoga. Flat jagah: minimum ho sakta hai (ya saddle/plateau — 14.8 me dekhenge).

Gradient ek saath do kaam karta hai: direction AUR distance

Teacher ke lecture me ek mazedaar experiment tha. Maan lo koi tumhe sirf direction bata de ("left jao" ya "right jao") aur tum hamesha fixed size c ka kadam lo. Kya hoga? Tum bottom ke paas pahunchoge, usko cross karoge, palat ke wapas aaoge, phir cross karoge... hamesha ke liye bottom ke aas-paas lagbhag c chaudi patti (band) me ulat-palat karte rahoge. Lecture ki table: c = 2.1 kabhi 0.2 ke andar nahi aaya, c = 0.36 nau steps me pahuncha phir hamesha 0.36 ki patti me uchhalta raha, c = 0.0069 itna chhota ki 200 steps me pahuncha hi nahi. Fixed step size ki koi achhi value nahi hoti: bada c = jaldi pahunchta par kabhi settle nahi hota; chhota c = accurate par khatam hi nahi hota.

Gradient is problem ko apne aap solve karta hai: jab tum minimum se door ho, slope bada hai → kadam bada; jab paas ho, slope chhota → kadam chhota; bottom par slope 0 → kadam 0. Lecture ki table (lr = 0.30, start w = 6): step size 2.054 → 0.828 → 0.334 → 0.134 → ... step 20 tak 0.00000. Kisi ne kadam chhota karne ko nahi bola, slope khud chhota hota gaya. Isliye update me η × gradient hota hai, sirf η nahi.

GD kab rokte hain? (stopping rules)

  • Fixed number of steps/epochs poore ho gaye (sabse common).
  • Loss me sudhaar bahut chhota ho gaya (improvement < tolerance).
  • Gradient ka size lagbhag zero ho gaya.
  • Validation loss badhne laga (early stopping — Chapter 19).

Exam Radar

  • Gradient = direction of steepest ascent (uphill). Negative gradient = steepest descent. Isliye update me minus sign.
  • Update rule: θ ← θ − η∇L(θ). η (ya α) = learning rate = step size; gradient = direction (+ slope ki tezi).
  • Agar gradient positive hai to θ ghatega (negative direction me move karega) — Worksheet 05 ka MCQ.
  • GD ek local, iterative, first-order method hai: sirf jahan khade ho wahan ka slope (first derivative) padhta hai. Poora landscape kabhi nahi dekhta.
  • Gradient har update ke baad nayi position par dobara nikalna padta hai.
  • η badalne se loss curve ki shape nahi badalti; sirf curve par kaunse points visit honge, wo badalta hai.

Galti mat karna

  • "θ + η∇L" likh diya to tum gradient ascent kar rahe ho — loss badhega. Descent me hamesha minus.
  • Gradient zero hone ka matlab "pakka global minimum" nahi hai. Wo local minimum, maximum, saddle point ya plateau bhi ho sakta hai.
  • Learning rate gradient ki direction nahi badalta (η positive hai); sirf kadam lamba-chhota karta hai.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

"Gradient bole upar, hum chalein neeche. Slope bada to kadam bada, slope chhota to kadam chhota." θ ← θ − η∇L.

14.3 Haath se GD: f(w) = w², w₀ = 5, η = 0.1

Kahani

Sabse simple pahad lo: ek katori (bowl). Loss L(w) = w². Iska minimum sabko pata hai: w = 0 par L = 0. Par GD ko ye pata nahi. Use bas ek starting point diya gaya hai, w₀ = 5, aur learning rate η = 0.1. Dekhte hain wo khud neeche kaise aata hai.

L(w) = w²  ⇒  dLdw = 2w  ⇒  wnew = w − η · 2w
  • 2w = slope (power rule: w² ka derivative 2w).
  • η = 0.1 rakha to wnew = w − 0.2w = 0.8 w. Matlab har step me w apna 80% reh jata hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Sawaal: L(w) = w², w₀ = 5, η = 0.1. Pehle 6 updates karo.

  1. Step 1: gradient g = 2 × 5 = 10, update w₁ = 5 − 0.1 × 10 = 5 − 1 = 4, loss 4² = 16 (pehle 25 tha).
  2. Step 2: g = 2 × 4 = 8, w₂ = 4 − 0.8 = 3.2, loss 3.2² = 10.24.
  3. Step 3: g = 6.4, w₃ = 3.2 − 0.64 = 2.56, loss 6.5536.
  4. Step 4: g = 5.12, w₄ = 2.56 − 0.512 = 2.048, loss 4.1943.
  5. Step 5: g = 4.096, w₅ = 2.048 − 0.4096 = 1.6384, loss 2.6844.
  6. Step 6: g = 3.2768, w₆ = 1.6384 − 0.32768 = 1.31072, loss 1.7180.
twtL = wt²gradient 2wtkadam η·gwt+1

141680.83.2

42.0484.19434.0960.40961.6384
