ScheduleFormulaShape / pehchaanTotal epochs pata hone chahiye?Val loss dekhta hai?PyTorchKab use karein
Fixedηt = ηseedhi flat lineNahiNahisirf optimizer ka lrSimple baseline; Adam ke saath aksar theek
Step decayη₀ γ⌊e/s⌋staircase, achanak dropsRoughly (milestones chunne ke liye)NahiStepLR(opt, step_size, gamma=0.1), MultiStepLR(opt, milestones, gamma=0.1)Classic CNN training (SGD + momentum)
Exponentialη₀ γt = η₀ e−ktsmooth percentage-style fallNahiNahiExponentialLR(opt, gamma)Smooth steady decay chahiye
Time-based 1/tη₀ / (1 + k t)shuru me tez, lambi poonchhNahiNahiLambdaLR(opt, lambda e: 1/(1+k*e))Classic SGD theory / simple decay
Cosine annealingηmin + ½(ηmax − ηmin)(1 + cos(πt/T))half-cosine, smooth soft landingHaan (T_max)NahiCosineAnnealingLR(opt, T_max, eta_min=0)Known budget; modern default (aksar warmup ke saath)
Linear warmupηmax(t+1)/W, t < Wnear-zero se upar chadhnaSirf WNahiLambdaLR, LinearLRAdam / Transformers / large batch; unstable early updates
ReduceLROnPlateaubad > patience ⇒ η × factortab drop jab val loss atkeNahiHaanReduceLROnPlateau(opt, mode='min', factor=0.1, patience=10) + step(val_loss)Total epochs pata nahi; feedback-based
Cyclical / One-cyclebase ↔ max (triangle) / ek baar upar-neecheupar-neeche wave / ek pahadOne-cycle: haanNahiCyclicLR, OneCycleLR (per batch step)Fast training, super-convergence

Exam Radar

  • Learning rate = step size; sabse important hyperparameter. Log scale par search (1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1). Adam default lr = 1e-3.
  • Too small → slow / stagnation; slightly high → oscillation near minimum; much too high → divergence, NaN. NaN aaye to pehle LR kam karo.
  • L = w² ya (w − 3)² par: 0 < η < 1 converge, η = 1 forever oscillate, η > 1 diverge; boundary par loss constant rehta hai.
  • Fixed LR ki problem: ek size do phases (door se tez aana, paas aake settle) serve nahi kar sakta; SGD/mini-batch noise ki wajah se kabhi settle nahi hota.
  • Scheduling: high LR = explore (valley to valley), low LR = refine (settle). Decay bahut bade starting LR ko nahi bacha sakta.
  • Step: η₀γ⌊e/s⌋ (staircase). Exponential: η₀γt = η₀e−kt, γ = e−k. 1/t: η₀/(1+kt). Cosine: ηmin + ½(ηmax − ηmin)(1 + cos(πt/T)); t = T/2 par exactly beech.
  • Warmup: chhote LR se shuru karke badhana — early instability rokta hai (random weights, Adam ke kachche estimates, large batch).
  • ReduceLROnPlateau: val loss monitor; defaults mode='min', factor=0.1, patience=10, min_lr=0; scheduler.step(val_loss); patience = p → (p+1)-th lagataar bad epoch par cut.
  • StepLR gamma default 0.1; ExponentialLR gamma required; CosineAnnealingLR eta_min default 0; LambdaLR: lr = initial_lr × lambda(epoch).
  • Order: optimizer.step() phir scheduler.step(); epoch-based scheduler epoch me ek baar; OneCycleLR/CyclicLR har batch. LR padho: optimizer.param_groups[0]['lr'] ya scheduler.get_last_lr()[0].
  • Pehchaan: staircase = step; smooth percentage fall = exponential; half-cosine soft landing = cosine; near-zero se rise = warmup; val loss atke tab cut = reduce on plateau.

Galti mat karna

  • scheduler.step() ko batch loop ke andar daal diya (epoch-based scheduler ke liye) → StepLR(step_size=10) har 10 batches par girega, epochs par nahi. LR bahut jaldi khatam.
  • ReduceLROnPlateau me scheduler.step() bina metric ke → error. Isko scheduler.step(val_loss) chahiye. Aur training loss nahi, validation loss do.
  • get_last_lr() list lautata hai, number nahi — [0] lagao.
  • Cosine me T_max total epochs se chhota rakha to baad me LR wapas badhne lagega.
  • LambdaLR ka function LR nahi, multiplier lautata hai: lambda 0.5 lautaye to lr = initial_lr × 0.5.
  • "Exponential decay me har epoch same amount kam hota hai" — galat. Same percentage (ratio) kam hota hai; amount chhota hota jata hai. Har epoch same amount = linear decay.
  • patience = 5 ka matlab "5th bad epoch par cut" nahi — 5 bad epochs tak bardasht, 6th lagataar bad epoch par cut.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Geyser ka nal: shuru me bada ghumao, paas aake chhota. Step = seedhi, Exponential = mithai ka 5% roz, Cosine = jahaz ki soft landing, Warmup = thande engine ko garam karna, Plateau = trainer jo result dekh ke diet badle. Aur hamesha: optimizer.step() pehle, scheduler.step() baad me.

Chapter 16

Momentum-Based Methods: EWMA, SGD with Momentum, NAG

Gradient ko yaaddasht do · EWMA · bias correction · velocity · Nesterov ka look-ahead

Chapter 14 aur Chapter 15 me humne seekha: gradient batata hai ki upar kidhar hai, aur hum ulti taraf ek chhota kadam lete hain: w ← w − α·g. Ye rule bilkul sahi hai, par ek dikkat hai: plain SGD bhulakkad hai. Har step pe wo sirf abhi wala gradient dekhta hai, aur pichhle saare gradients bhool jaata hai. Teacher ki worksheet ki pehli line yaad rakhna: "A gradient step is useful; a remembered gradient can be better."

Is chapter ki poori kahani ek seedhi line hai (Worksheet 06 isi order me chalti hai):

  • SGD — reacts: sirf aaj ka gradient dekhta hai.
  • EWMA — remembers: ek number me poori history ka "fading" average.
  • Momentum — uses direction: gradients ka EWMA = velocity, usi direction me chalo.
  • NAG — checks ahead: jahan velocity le ja rahi hai, gradient wahan naapo.

Agla chapter (Chapter 17) isi memory ko size ke liye use karega (AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam). Pehle samjho ki plain SGD phasta kahan hai.

16.1 Plain SGD kahan-kahan phasta hai

Kahani

Raat ka time hai, light chali gayi hai, aur tum ek lambe, patle naale (drain) ke andar khade ho. Naale ki dono deewarein bahut tedhi (steep) hain, aur naale ka farsh bahut halka sa dhalaan le kar door nadi ki taraf jaata hai. Tumhe nadi tak pahunchna hai (wahi minimum hai). Andhere me tum sirf pair ke neeche ki dhalaan feel kar sakte ho.

Problem: pair ke neeche sabse tedhi dhalaan hamesha saamne wali deewar ki taraf hoti hai, nadi ki taraf nahi. To tum ek deewar se doosri deewar pe uchhalte rehte ho — left, right, left, right — aur nadi ki taraf bas zara-zara khisakte ho. Yahi plain gradient descent ka zig-zag hai.

Plain SGD (aur plain GD) ki paanch badi problems hain. Inhi ko theek karne ke liye saare "advanced optimizers" bane:

Problem 1: Ravine (lambi patli ghaati) — zig-zag across, slow along

Jab loss surface ek direction me bahut steep ho aur doosri me bahut flat (isko ravine, ya elongated valley, ya ill-conditioned surface kehte hain), to contour lines lambe patle ellipse ban jaate hain. Gradient hamesha contour ke perpendicular hota hai, isliye wo zyada-tar steep deewar ki taraf point karta hai, minimum ki taraf nahi.

Lab 7 (Optimizer Zoo) ka ravine yaad rakhna: f(w0, w1) = 0.5·(0.1w02 + 2.0w12). Gradient = (0.1w0, 2w1). Yaani w1 wali direction 20 guna steeper hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein

Is ravine pe ek GD step: w0 ← w0 − α(0.1w0) = (1 − 0.1α)w0 aur w1 ← (1 − 2α)w1. Har step pe dono coordinate ek fixed number se multiply hote hain.

  1. α = 0.9 lo. Steep direction ka multiplier: 1 − 2(0.9) = −0.8. Minus sign ka matlab: har step pe w1 ka sign palat jaata hai — yahi zig-zag hai (deewar se deewar).
  2. Flat direction ka multiplier: 1 − 0.1(0.9) = 0.91. Yaani har step me w0 sirf 9% minimum ki taraf khisakta hai — bahut slow.
  3. Kya α badha dein? Agar α > 1 hua to steep multiplier |1 − 2α| > 1 ho jaayega, aur w1 har step bada hota jaayega — diverge. Matlab learning rate ki upper limit steep direction tay karti hai, aur flat direction ko us chhote α ke saath ghisatna padta hai.

Ek hi learning rate dono directions ke liye theek nahi: bada α → steep wall pe uchhalna/diverge; chhota α → flat floor pe rengna.

Problem 2: Noisy gradients — har sample ki apni raay

SGD / mini-batch me gradient poore data se nahi, ek chhote sample se aata hai, to wo noisy estimate hota hai. Teacher ka Worksheet 07 example (delivery data) dekho. Model: ŷ = w·x (minutes per km), loss ek sample pe L = ½(ŷ − y)2, gradient g = x(ŷ − y). Chhe deliveries, w = 2.0000 pe har sample ka gradient:

samplex (km)y (min)ŷ = 2xerror ŷ − ygradient x(ŷ − y)ye sample kya kehta hai
1224+2+4w ghatao
2478+1+4w ghatao
3132−1−1w badhao
4356+1+3w ghatao
5254−1−2w badhao
65910+1+5w ghatao

Full-batch gradient = (4 + 4 − 1 + 3 − 2 + 5)/6 = 13/6 = +2.1667 — hamesha ek hi sign. Par SGD ek-ek sample pe chalta hai (α = 0.05, cycle order me), to wo jo gradient haath me hai usi taraf bhaagta hai: 12 steps me gradient ka sign 11 me se 8 transitions pe palta. 10 epochs (60 steps) me 59 me se 40 reversals, kul chala 6.3909 units, par net displacement sirf 0.2217! (Least-squares best answer w* = 1.7797.) Jo information SGD phenk raha hai wo current gradient me nahi, pichhle bhule hue gradients me hai.

Problem 3: Plateau (sapaat maidaan)

Kuch jagah loss surface lagbhag flat hoti hai — gradient bahut chhota. Step = α × (chhota gradient) = bahut chhota step. Training curve kai epochs tak "atki" dikhti hai. Jo optimizer pichhli speed yaad rakhe (momentum), wo plateau pe bhi chalta rehta hai.

Problem 4: Saddle point (ghode ki kaathi)

Saddle point pe gradient zero hota hai, par wo minimum nahi hai: ek direction me upar jaata hai, doosri me neeche (jaise ghode ki kaathi ya Pringles chip). High-dimensional neural nets me saddle points local minima se kahin zyada common hote hain. Lab 7 ka mini-challenge: f = 0.2w02 − 0.5w12, start [−2.0, 0.01]. w1 ka gradient = −w1 ≈ −0.01, itna chhota ki SGD (lr = 0.1) ko escape karne me bahut time lagta hai: 10 steps baad w1 ≈ 0.026, 40 steps baad ≈ 0.45. Adam (lr = 0.2) 10 steps me hi w1 ≈ 1.86 tak nikal jaata hai (numbers: PyTorch ke update rules numpy me chala ke). Kyun? Ye Chapter 17 me samjhoge.

Problem 5: Local minima

Agar loss me do ghaatiyan hain aur tum chhoti (shallow) ghaati me utar gaye, to wahan gradient zero hai aur plain GD wahin ruk jaata hai. Teacher ka two-valley example (16.7 me) dikhayega ki momentum kabhi-kabhi is chhoti ghaati se bahar nikal jaata hai.

Exam Radar

  • Ravine / ill-conditioned surface pe plain GD: steep direction me oscillate (zig-zag), flat direction me slow progress.
  • Learning rate ki upper limit steep direction tay karti hai (quadratic λw2/2 pe GD tab diverge karta hai jab α > 2/λ).
  • Saddle point aur local minimum dono pe gradient = 0. Plateau pe gradient ≈ 0.
  • Mini-batch gradient = full gradient ka noisy estimate; SGD "no memory" hai.

16.2 EWMA — ek number me poori history

Kahani

Mohalle ki cricket team ke coach hain Pappu bhaiya. Unhe har batsman ka "form" pata rehta hai. Kya wo har match ka score diary me likh ke rakhte hain? Nahi! Unke dimaag me har player ke liye bas ek number hota hai — "iska form kaisa chal raha hai". Naya match hua to wo us number ko thoda update kar dete hain:

naya form = 0.8 × purana form + 0.2 × aaj ka score

Kal ka match sabse zyada matter karta hai, pichhle hafte wala thoda kam, pichhle mahine wala bahut kam. Purane matches dheere-dheere fade hote hain, achanak delete nahi hote. Yahi hai Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA). (Worksheet 06 me bhi yahi analogy hai: "a coach judging a player's form".)

Simple average kyun nahi?

Socho "pichhle k values ka plain average" le lete. Teacher ke Worksheet 07 ke hisaab se ye do jagah fail hota hai:

  • Ye purani information ko bhi utni hi value deta hai jitni nayi ko. 500 step purana gradient bilkul alag w pe naapa gaya tha!
  • Tumhe saare k numbers store karne padenge. Ek million parameters ho to million × k numbers. EWMA ko sirf ek number per parameter chahiye.

Definition

EWMA (Exponentially Weighted Moving Average) ek running average hai jisme har purani value ka weight har step pe β se multiply ho kar exponentially (geometrically) ghatta hai. Isko store karne ke liye sirf ek state number chahiye.

Vt = β·Vt−1 + (1 − β)·θt
  • θt = step/din t ka naya observation (aaj ka temperature, aaj ka score, ya aage chal ke aaj ka gradient). Worksheet isi ko xt likhti hai.
  • Vt = naya observation dekhne ke baad ka average — yahi ek number hum yaad rakhte hain. Worksheet me iska naam st.
  • Vt−1 = pichhle step ka average (purana form).
  • β (beta) = purane average ka weight, 0 ≤ β < 1. Bada β = lambi memory.
  • (1 − β) = naye observation ka weight. Jo β nahi leta, wo isko milta hai.
  • V0 = 0 hamesha (average khaali shuru hota hai).

Formula aisa kyun dikhta hai? Ye do cheezon ka weighted average hai: "jo main pehle maanta tha" (Vt−1) aur "aaj jo dikha" (θt). Dono weights ka sum β + (1 − β) = 1 hai, isliye average observations ke hi scale pe rehta hai (temperature ka average temperature jaisa hi number hoga). Zor se padho: "naya average = β hissa purane average ka + (1 − β) hissa naye observation ka."

Dhyaan: EWMA formula me θt ka matlab "aaj ka data point" hai, model ka weight nahi. Classroom notebook isi notation me likhta hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 06 ladder

Sawaal: s0 = 0, β = 0.8, x1 = 5, x2 = 1. Rule: st = 0.8st−1 + 0.2xt.

  1. Initial memory: s0 = 0
  2. Pehla observation: s1 = 0.8(0) + 0.2(5) = 0 + 1.0 = 1.0
  3. Doosra: s2 = 0.8(1.0) + 0.2(1) = 0.8 + 0.2 = 1.0
  4. Direction check — s2 me kiska asar zyada? Kholo: s2 = 0.2·x2 + 0.8·0.2·x1 = 0.2·x2 + 0.16·x1. Naye x2 ka coefficient 0.2 > purane x1 ka 0.16.

Jawab: s1 = 1.0, s2 = 1.0; naya sample zyada influence karta hai (0.2 vs 0.16). EWMA saari history store nahi karta — sirf ek state st.

Practice (worksheet): β = 0.6, x1 = 4, x2 = 2 → s1 = 0.6(0) + 0.4(4) = 1.6, s2 = 0.6(1.6) + 0.4(2) = 0.96 + 0.8 = 1.76. Ye 4 aur 2 ka simple average (3) kyun nahi? Kyunki naye 2 ko weight 0.4, purane 4 ko 0.24, aur bacha hua 0.36 weight abhi bhi shuruaati s0 = 0 pe baitha hai: 0.4(2) + 0.24(4) + 0.36(0) = 1.76.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 07: smooth hona hi point hai

Sawaal: s0 = 0, β = 0.8, observations 5, 3, 1 (tezi se gir rahe hain).

  1. s1 = 0.8(0) + 0.2(5) = 0 + 1.0 = 1.0000
  2. s2 = 0.8(1.0000) + 0.2(3) = 0.8 + 0.6 = 1.4000
  3. s3 = 0.8(1.4000) + 0.2(1) = 1.12 + 0.2 = 1.3200

Observations 5 → 3 → 1 gire, average 1.0 → 1.4 → 1.32 aaram se chala. Average apne data se zyada smooth hai — yahi poora point hai.

Par dhyaan do: 3 observations ke baad average 1.32 hai, plain average 3.0 ke paas bhi nahi! Kyunki s0 = 0 ka weight abhi bhi 0.83 = 0.512 hai. Ye yaad rakhna — yahi problem Adam ka bias correction theek karta hai (16.4 me).

Chalo numbers se samjhein — ek ulta observation sign nahi palatta

Sawaal (Worksheet 07 "your turn"): β = 0.8, s0 = 0, observations 6, 6, −2.

  1. s1 = 0.8(0) + 0.2(6) = 0 + 1.2 = 1.2000
  2. s2 = 0.8(1.2000) + 0.2(6) = 0.9600 + 1.2000 = 2.1600
  3. Ab pehla negative observation. s3 = 0.8(2.1600) + 0.2(−2) = 1.7280 − 0.4000 = 1.3280
  4. Direction check: average 2.1600 se 1.3280 gira, yaani drop = 0.8320 (38.5%), par negative nahi hua, kyunki naye observation ka weight sirf 0.2 tha.

s = 1.2000 → 2.1600 → 1.3280. Ek ulti value average ko kam karti hai, palat-ti nahi. Isi property ki wajah se hum gradients ko EWMA me daalne wale hain.

Python · EWMA by hand (worksheet numbers verify karo)

def ewma(values, beta, s0=0.0):
    s = s0                         # memory khaali shuru: s0 = 0
    history = []
    for x in values:
        s = beta * s + (1 - beta) * x   # purana hissa + naya hissa
        history.append(round(s, 4))
    return history

print(ewma([5, 1], 0.8))       # Worksheet 06
print(ewma([4, 2], 0.6))       # Worksheet 06 practice
print(ewma([5, 3, 1], 0.8))    # Worksheet 07 worked example
print(ewma([6, 6, -2], 0.8))   # Worksheet 07 your turn

Output

[1.0, 1.0]
[1.6, 1.76]
[1.0, 1.4, 1.32]
[1.2, 2.16, 1.328]

16.3 EWMA ko khol ke dekho: weights, memory length aur β ka khel

Unroll karo (substitute karte jao)

Rule me st−1 = βst−2 + (1 − β)xt−1 daalo, phir st−2 ko bhi kholo, aur aise hi peeche chalte jao:

st = (1−β)xt + β(1−β)xt−1 + β2(1−β)xt−2 + β3(1−β)xt−3 + ··· + βts0
  • k step purane observation ka weight = (1 − β)βk. Har step peeche jaane pe ek aur β ka factor lagta hai → weights geometrically / exponentially girte hain. Isi liye naam "exponentially weighted".
  • Koi observation kabhi poori tarah delete nahi hota — bas fade hota jaata hai.
  • Worksheet 06 ka subjective Q1: xt−2 ka coefficient = β2(1 − β).
kitna puranaweight, β = 0.8weight, β = 0.9
newest (aaj)0.20000.1000
1 step purana0.16000.0900
2 steps purana0.12800.0810
3 steps purana0.10240.0729
4 steps purana0.08190.0656
5 steps purana0.06550.0590

β = 0.8 tezi se bhoolta hai (0.2 → 0.0655), β = 0.9 aaram se (0.1 → 0.059). Bada β = har purani value ko zyada der tak yaad rakhna.

Saare weights ka total = 1 − βt

Asli observations ke weights jodo: (1−β)(1 + β + β2 + ··· + βt−1). Ye geometric series hai, iska sum = 1 − βt. Bacha hua βt weight shuruaati s0 = 0 pe baitha hai. Ye line 16.4 (bias correction) ki neev hai.

Memory kitni lambi? Effective window ≈ 1/(1 − β)

effective memory ≈ 11 − β steps
  • Seedhi soch: newest ka weight (1 − β) hai. Agar itne hi weight wale N recent observations hon to unka total 1 tab hoga jab N = 1/(1 − β).
  • Doosri soch: 1/(1 − β) steps peeche weight lagbhag 1/e ≈ 0.37 guna reh jaata hai (jaise 0.910 = 0.3487). Usse purana "kam matter karta hai".
  • Half-life (weight aadha hone me steps) = ln 0.5 / ln β; β = 0.9 pe ≈ 6.58 steps.
βnewest weight (1 − β)effective memory 1/(1 − β)kaisa behave karta hai
0.50.500~2 stepsbahut jumpy, turant react
0.80.200~5 stepsbeech ka
0.90.100~10 stepstypical choice (pichhle ~10 din ka temperature)
0.980.020~50 stepsbahut smooth, par der se react (lag)

β ka trade-off: smoothness vs lag

Bada β → curve smooth (noise dab jaata hai) par lag zyada: data badal jaaye to average der se maanta hai. Chhota β → turant react karta hai par noisy. Neeche 40 din ka temperature hai jisme din 21 pe mausam achanak ~20°C se ~30°C ho jaata hai:

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

β = "kitna purana yaad rakhna hai" ka knob. 1/(1 − β) = kitne steps ki memory. 0.9 → 10, 0.98 → 50, 0.5 → 2.

16.4 Start-up bias aur bias correction

Kahani

Naye class register me teacher ne galti se har bachche ke naam ke aage pehle se kuch imaginary zero marks likh diye. Ab pehle test me Golu ko 25/25 mile, par average nikalte waqt wo zeros bhi gine gaye — to average aaya 2.5! Golu ka asli performance 25 hai, register 2.5 bata raha hai. Ilaaj: un imaginary zeros ka weight hata do (Worksheet 06 ki analogy).

EWMA me V0 = 0 se shuru karna convenient hai, par shuru ke kuch steps me average me "bahut saara zero" mila hota hai, isliye Vt asli value se chhota (biased towards zero) aata hai. Ise start-up bias ya initialization bias kehte hain.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — temperature (classroom notebook)

Sawaal: temperatures 25, 13, 17, 31 °C, β = 0.9, V0 = 0. Raw EWMA aur corrected EWMA nikalo.

  1. V1 = 0.9(0) + 0.1(25) = 2.5 — 25°C ke din average 2.5°C? Bilkul galat! Bias.
  2. V2 = 0.9(2.5) + 0.1(13) = 2.25 + 1.3 = 3.55
  3. V3 = 0.9(3.55) + 0.1(17) = 3.195 + 1.7 = 4.895
  4. V4 = 0.9(4.895) + 0.1(31) = 4.4055 + 3.1 = 7.5055
  5. Ab har ek ko (1 − 0.9t) se divide karo:
    V̂1 = 2.5 / (1 − 0.9) = 2.5 / 0.1 = 25.0000
    V̂2 = 3.55 / (1 − 0.81) = 3.55 / 0.19 = 18.6842
    V̂3 = 4.895 / (1 − 0.729) = 4.895 / 0.271 = 18.0627
    V̂4 = 7.5055 / (1 − 0.6561) = 7.5055 / 0.3439 = 21.8247
  6. Check V̂2: asli weights 25 pe 0.09 aur 13 pe 0.1 the, total 0.19. Weighted average = (0.09×25 + 0.1×13)/0.19 = (2.25 + 1.3)/0.19 = 18.6842. Matlab correction ne bas weighted sum ko total weight se divide kiya — isi se wo sachcha average bana.

Raw: 2.5, 3.55, 4.895, 7.5055 (bekaar, bahut chhote). Corrected: 25.0, 18.68, 18.06, 21.82 (asli temperature range me).

V̂t = Vt1 − βt
  • V̂t = bias-corrected average ("V-hat").
  • t = step number (pehla update t = 1, doosra t = 2 ...). βt yaani β ki power t: 0.91 = 0.9, 0.92 = 0.81, 0.93 = 0.729.
  • 1 − βt = asli data pe ab tak laga total weight (16.3 wali geometric series). Usse divide karna = weights ko 1 tak normalize karna.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — constant signal test (Worksheet 08)

Har step observation = 1 (hamesha). Imaandaar average 1 hona chahiye. β = 0.9:

  1. m1 = 0.9(0) + 0.1(1) = 0.1000
  2. m2 = 0.9(0.1000) + 0.1(1) = 0.0900 + 0.1000 = 0.1900
  3. m3 = 0.9(0.1900) + 0.1(1) = 0.1710 + 0.1000 = 0.2710
  4. Dekho: 0.1, 0.19, 0.271 bilkul 1 − 0.91, 1 − 0.92, 1 − 0.93 hain. Constant g ke liye rule (1 − βt)g deta hai, kabhi g nahi.
  5. Correction: 0.2710 / (1 − 0.93) = 0.2710 / 0.2710 = 1.0000 ✓

Average galat nahi tha, adhoora tha: 3 steps baad 0.729 weight abhi bhi m0 = 0 pe baitha tha.

t steps baad1 − βt (β = 0.9)1 − βt (β = 0.999)matlab
10.10000.00100.9 wala 90% chhota, 0.999 wala ~100% chhota
20.19000.0020
30.27100.0030
100.65130.01000.9 wala abhi 35% chhota
500.99480.04880.9 lagbhag theek; 0.999 abhi 95% chhota
3001.00000.2593
30001.00000.95030.999 bhi ab sirf 5% chhota

Correction khud band ho jaata hai: t bada hone pe βt → 0, to 1 − βt → 1, aur 1 se divide karne se kuch nahi badalta. Isliye bias correction shuruaati steps me hi important hai — aur jitna bada β, utni der tak important (β = 0.999 pe hazaaron steps tak!). Yahi wajah hai ki Adam me bias correction zaroori hai (uska β2 = 0.999), jabki plain momentum (β = 0.9) me practice me log aksar correction nahi lagate — PyTorch ka optim.SGD bhi momentum pe koi bias correction nahi karta; 10–20 steps baad farak khatam.

Python · EWMA + bias correction (classroom temperatures)

temps = [25, 13, 17, 31]
beta = 0.9
V = 0.0                                   # V0 = 0: yahin se bias aata hai
for t, theta in enumerate(temps, start=1):    # t = 1, 2, 3, 4 (step number)
    V = beta * V + (1 - beta) * theta     # raw EWMA
    V_hat = V / (1 - beta ** t)           # bias correction: total weight se divide
    print(f"t={t}: raw V={V:.4f}  corrected V_hat={V_hat:.4f}")

Output

t=1: raw V=2.5000  corrected V_hat=25.0000
t=2: raw V=3.5500  corrected V_hat=18.6842
t=3: raw V=4.8950  corrected V_hat=18.0627
t=4: raw V=7.5055  corrected V_hat=21.8247

Exam Radar

  • EWMA: Vt = βVt−1 + (1 − β)θt; V0 = 0; dono weights ka sum 1.
  • k step purane observation ka weight = (1 − β)βk → exponential decay.
  • Effective window ≈ 1/(1 − β): 0.5 → 2, 0.8 → 5, 0.9 → 10, 0.98 → 50, 0.999 → 1000.
  • β badhao → smoother + longer memory + slower reaction (more lag). β ghatao → noisy par fast.
  • Bias correction: V̂t = Vt/(1 − βt). Wajah: V0 = 0 → early estimates zero ki taraf biased (too small). Correction early steps me estimate bada karta hai; large t pe effect khatam.
  • t = 1 pe: V̂1 = θ1 exactly (correction pehle observation ko hi lauta deta hai).

Galti mat karna

  • "β bada = naye data ko zyada weight" — ulta hai. β purane average ka weight hai; naye ka weight (1 − β) hai.
  • Bias correction divide karta hai (1 − βt) se, multiply nahi. 1 − βt < 1 hai, to divide karne se value badi hoti hai.
  • Exponent t step number hai, βt ko β·t mat padhna.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Register me imaginary zeros = V0 = 0. Unka hissa hai βt. Asli hissa 1 − βt. Asli hisse se divide karo, sachcha average mil jaayega.

16.5 SGD with Momentum — gradients ka EWMA = velocity

Kahani

Pahadi dhalaan pe ek bhaari gend (ball) chhodo. Gend har pal sirf apne neeche ki dhalaan nahi dekhti — uske paas pehle se ek speed (velocity) hai. Lambi seedhi dhalaan ho to speed badhti jaati hai. Raaste me chhota gaddha ya thodi ulti dhalaan aaye to wo turant palat-ti nahi; bas thodi dheemi hoti hai aur aage nikal jaati hai. Naale (ravine) me left-right uchhalne wali harkatein ek doosre ko cancel kar deti hain, aur neeche ki taraf wali harkat jud-ti jaati hai.

Worksheet 06 ki line: "A rolling bicycle does not instantly face a new direction after one small wobble." Plain SGD wo cycle hai jo har wobble pe handle ghuma deti hai.

Idea ek line ka hai: 16.2 me EWMA kisi bhi sequence pe chal sakta tha. Ab sequence = gradients. Gradients ka EWMA hi "velocity" vt hai, aur hum raw gradient ki jagah velocity ki direction me chalte hain. Classroom notebook ka key idea: Momentum = EWMA of gradients.

vt = β·vt−1 + (1 − β)·gt     wt = wt−1 − α·vt
  • gt = is step pe naapa gaya gradient ∂L/∂w (noisy observation).
  • vt = velocity = ab tak ke gradients ka running (EWMA) average = jis direction me hum asal me chal rahe hain.
  • v0 = 0 (pehle step pe koi history nahi).
  • β = momentum coefficient: purani velocity ka kitna hissa bachega. Ye tay karta hai kitne purane gradients abhi bhi matter karte hain (direction). Typical 0.9.
  • α = learning rate: velocity ki direction me kitna door jaana hai (distance). Lab/PyTorch me isi ko η ya lr kehte hain; kai books me parameter ko θ likhte hain.

Ye course ka (Worksheets 06–07, classroom notebook, Prince UDL Ch. 6) convention hai. Doosri line bilkul plain GD jaisi hai, bas gt ki jagah vt. Do hyperparameters, do alag kaam: β batata hai kidhar chalna hai, α batata hai kitna. (PyTorch wala form thoda alag dikhta hai — 16.6 me teeno forms milayenge.)

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 07 ka "hook" (noisy gradients)

Sawaal: delivery data ke pehle teen gradients +4, +4, −1 (fixed maan lo). w0 = 2.0000, v0 = 0, β = 0.9, α = 0.1. Do baar sample "w ghatao" bole, teesra thoda sa "w badhao". Kya optimizer ko poora palat jaana chahiye?

  1. Step 1: 0.9 × 0 = 0, 0.1 × 4 = 0.4000 → v1 = 0.4000; w1 = 2.0000 − 0.1(0.4000) = 1.9600
  2. Step 2: 0.9 × 0.4000 = 0.3600, 0.1 × 4 = 0.4000 → v2 = 0.7600; w2 = 1.9600 − 0.0760 = 1.8840
  3. Step 3 (gradient ulta): 0.9 × 0.7600 = 0.6840, 0.1 × (−1) = −0.1000 → v3 = 0.5840; w3 = 1.8840 − 0.0584 = 1.8256
  4. Plain SGD, same gradients, same α: 2.0 − 0.1(4) = 1.6 → 1.6 − 0.1(4) = 1.2 → 1.2 − 0.1(−1) = 1.3 ← palat gaya!
step 1step 2step 3w* = 1.7797 se doori
plain SGD1.60001.20001.30000.4797 (1 reversal)
Momentum1.96001.88401.82560.0459 (0 reversal)

Jawab: Nahi palatna chahiye. v3 = 0.5840 abhi bhi positive hai — ulte gradient ne velocity ka sirf 23.2% kaata, 100% nahi. Momentum w* ke ~10 guna zyada paas hai.

Teacher ne poora 10-epoch (60 steps, α = 0.05) run bhi naapa: plain SGD final 1.7783, wobble (last 12 ka sd) 0.0795, 40/59 reversals, 6.3909 units chala; Momentum β = 0.9: final 1.7960, wobble 0.0073, 21/59 reversals, sirf 0.7309 units chala. Momentum ki wobble 11× chhoti aur wo 8.7× kam chala. SGD sahi jagah pahunch ke bhi kabhi rukta nahi.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 06 ladder (state pehle, parameter baad me)

Sawaal: v0 = 0, θ0 = 2.00, β = 0.9, α = 0.1, g1 = 4, g2 = −2, phir g3 = −2.

  1. Purani velocity ka hissa: βv0 = 0.9(0) = 0; naye gradient ka hissa: (1 − β)g1 = 0.1(4) = 0.4
  2. v1 = 0 + 0.4 = 0.4; parameter me velocity use karo, raw gradient nahi: θ1 = 2.00 − 0.1(0.4) = 1.96
  3. Ulta gradient: v2 = 0.9(0.4) + 0.1(−2) = 0.36 − 0.2 = 0.16; θ2 = 1.96 − 0.1(0.16) = 1.944
  4. Direction check: g2 negative hai, par yaad wali velocity positive → θ ab bhi ghat raha hai, bas dheere.
  5. Ek aur ulta gradient: v3 = 0.9(0.16) + 0.1(−2) = 0.144 − 0.2 = −0.056; θ3 = 1.944 − 0.1(−0.056) = 1.9496

Do lagataar ulte gradients ke baad hi velocity ka sign palta (−0.056) aur θ badhne laga. Momentum gradients ki list nahi, ek direction yaad rakhta hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — asli function pe momentum (Worksheet 07 "your turn")

Ek sample x = 2, y = 2: L = ½(2w − 2)2, to g(w) = x(wx − y) = 2(2w − 2) = 4(w − 1). Minimum w = 1 pe. Start w0 = 2.0000, v0 = 0, β = 0.8, α = 0.25. Rules: vt = 0.8vt−1 + 0.2gt, wt = wt−1 − 0.25vt. Har naye w pe gradient dobara nikalo.

  1. Step 1: g1 = 4(2.0000 − 1) = 4.0000; v1 = 0.8(0) + 0.2(4.0000) = 0.8000; w1 = 2.0000 − 0.25(0.8000) = 1.8000 (velocity nahi thi, to pehla step chhota)
  2. Step 2: g2 = 4(1.8000 − 1) = 3.2000; v2 = 0.6400 + 0.6400 = 1.2800; w2 = 1.8000 − 0.3200 = 1.4800
  3. v2 = 1.28 > v1 = 0.8 kyun? Gradient to chhota hua (4 → 3.2)! Kyunki do gradients lagataar ek hi direction me the, to wo jud gaye.
  4. Step 3: g3 = 4(1.4800 − 1) = 1.9200; v3 = 0.8(1.2800) + 0.2(1.9200) = 1.0240 + 0.3840 = 1.4080; w3 = 1.4800 − 0.25(1.4080) = 1.1280
  5. Ab minimum sirf 0.128 door hai, par velocity 1.4080 hai! Step 4: g4 = 4(1.1280 − 1) = 0.5120; v4 = 1.1264 + 0.1024 = 1.2288; w4 = 1.1280 − 0.3072 = 0.8208 → minimum se 0.1792 aage nikal gaya.
  6. Run chalate raho: step 5 → 0.6109, step 6 → 0.5208 (sabse neeche, minimum se 0.4792 paar). Phir wapas aata hai, aur w = 1 ke 0.01 ke andar step 42 se hi tikta hai.

Momentum: 1.8000 → 1.4800 → 1.1280 → 0.8208. Step 4 pe gradient lagbhag khatam (4 → 0.512) tha, par velocity (1.2288) ne w ko minimum ke paar dhakel diya. Ye momentum ki apni problem hai: overshoot.

Comparison ke liye plain GD ko same pehla step do (α = 0.05, kyunki momentum ka pehla step α(1 − β)g = 0.25 × 0.2 × 4 = 0.2 tha): w ← w − 0.05·4(w − 1) deta hai 1.8000 → 1.6400 → 1.5120 → 1.4096. Har step bas 20% paas. Momentum ne speed pakdi aur 4 steps me minimum tak (balki paar) pahunch gaya. Is table me NAG wala column 16.9 me bharenge:

stepplain GD (α = 0.05)Momentum (α = 0.25, β = 0.8)momentum ki velocity v

16.6 Momentum ke teen roop — ek hi cheez, alag scaling

MCQ me ya PyTorch docs me tumhe momentum teen tarah likha milega. Ghabrana nahi — ye learning rate ki rescaling tak ek hi algorithm hain.

formvelocity updateweight updatekahan milega
(c) EWMA formvt = βvt−1 + (1 − β)gtw ← w − αvthamara course (worksheets, Prince UDL), Andrew Ng
(b) PyTorch formvt = βvt−1 + gtw ← w − ηvtPyTorch optim.SGD, Lab 7, Keras-style "framework note"
(a) classic formvt = βvt−1 + ηgtw ← w − vtSutskever et al. 2013, cs231n notes

Inhe barabar kaise dikhayein?

  1. (b) aur (a): (b) ki velocity equation ko η se multiply karo: ηvt = β(ηvt−1) + ηgt. Naam do u = ηv. To ut = βut−1 + ηgt aur w ← w − ut — yahi (a) hai. Same η pe bilkul same weights (sirf velocity ka scale alag).
  2. (c) aur (b): (c) ki velocity = (1 − β) × (b) ki velocity. To (c) ka update αv(c) = α(1 − β)v(b). Matlab (c) with α ≡ (b) with η = α(1 − β). Example: course ka α = 0.1, β = 0.9 ≡ PyTorch lr=0.01, momentum=0.9.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — teeno forms same weights dete hain

g(w) = 4(w − 1), w0 = 2, β = 0.9. Form (c) α = 0.1; forms (b) aur (a) η = 0.1 × (1 − 0.9) = 0.01.

step(c): v, w(b): v, w(a): v, w
10.4, 1.964.0, 1.960.04, 1.96
20.744, 1.88567.44, 1.88560.0744, 1.8856
31.02384, 1.78321610.2384, 1.7832160.102384, 1.783216
41.234742, 1.65974212.347424, 1.6597420.123474, 1.659742

Weights har form me identical; velocity sirf scale (1 : 10 : 0.1) me alag. (Python se verify.)

Terminal velocity — "momentum = 10× learning rate" wali baat

Agar gradient hamesha same g rahe (lambi seedhi dhalaan), velocity kahan tak badhegi? Steady state me v = βv + (...) solve karo:

  • (c) EWMA form: v → g. Step → αg, yaani plain GD jitna. (Shuru me chhota, dheere-dheere poora — "ramp-up".)
  • (b) PyTorch form: v → g/(1 − β). β = 0.9 pe 10g! Step → 10ηg. Classroom notebook ki table: gradient hamesha 10 ho to velocity 10 → 0.9(10) + 10 = 19 → 0.9(19) + 10 = 27.1 → 0.9(27.1) + 10 = 34.39 → ... → 100. Isi liye kehte hain ki β = 0.9 wala momentum consistent direction me effective learning rate ko ~10 guna kar deta hai.

Iska practical matlab: PyTorch me momentum on karte hi agar purana lr hi rakha to effective step kaafi bada ho sakta hai — isliye momentum ke saath lr aksar chhota rakhte hain (Lab 7: plain SGD lr 0.18, momentum ke saath 0.08).

Galti mat karna

  • PyTorch ka dampening argument velocity me (1 − dampening)·g jodta hai, par pehle step pe buffer = g hi hota hai (dampening nahi lagta). Isliye dampening=0.8, momentum=0.8, lr=0.25 course ke numbers nahi dega (pehla step hi 2.0 → 1.0 ho jaata hai). Course numbers chahiye to lr = α(1 − β) aur dampening = 0 rakho.
  • MCQ me formula dekh ke pehchano: "(1 − β)" dikhe to EWMA form; sirf "+ g" ho to PyTorch form; "+ η g" ho to classic form.

16.7 Momentum kyun kaam karta hai — aur kahan fail hota hai

Fayda 1: Consistent direction me speed badhti hai (acceleration)

Unroll karo: vt = (1−β)[gt + βgt−1 + β2gt−2 + ...]. Teacher ke slide (Prince) ki line: "gradient step is an infinite weighted sum of all the previous gradients... The effective learning rate increases if all these gradients are aligned over multiple iterations but decreases if the gradient direction repeatedly changes as the terms in the sum cancel out." Jab saare terms same sign ke hon, wo jud-te hain — ravine ke flat floor pe yahi hota hai.

Fayda 2: Oscillations cancel hoti hain

Ravine ki steep direction me gradient ka sign har step palatta hai: +3, −3, +3, −3. Inka average ≈ 0 — to velocity me ye direction lagbhag gayab. Lab 7 ke shabdon me: "Gradients that oscillate back and forth (along w1) have alternating signs and cancel out in the velocity accumulator. Gradients pointing in the same continuous direction (along w0) accumulate and accelerate progress." 16.1 wali figure me yahi dikha.

Fayda 3: Chhote gaddhe / shallow local minimum se nikal sakta hai

Teacher ka Worksheet 07 Part 4: do ghaati wala loss f(w) = 0.25(w2 − 1)2 + 0.2w, f′(w) = w3 − w + 0.2. Flat points: w = −1.0880 (global minimum, f = −0.2092), w = +0.2091 (ridge/deewar, f = 0.2704), w = +0.8789 (local minimum, f = 0.1887). Local minimum se ridge tak chadhai = 0.2704 − 0.1887 = 0.0817. Start w0 = 1.4, α = 0.5, 500 steps (EWMA-form momentum):

β500 steps baad kahan (w₀ = 1.4, α = 0.5)
0 (plain GD)+0.8789 — shallow ghaati me atka
0.5+0.8789 — atka
0.8+0.8789 — atka
0.9−1.0880 — global minimum
0.95−1.0880 — global minimum
0.98−1.0880 — global minimum

β = 0.9 run ko dhyaan se dekho (teacher ki table J): step 5 pe w = 0.7547, gradient lagbhag zero (0.0168), par velocity 0.2732 badi hai. Step 6 se 17 tak, 12 lagataar steps, gradient ulta (peeche) bolta raha aur momentum phir bhi aage chalta raha — velocity dheere-dheere khatam hoti rahi (step 9: 0.1229, step 14: 0.0385) aur step 17 pe w = 0.2022 pe ridge paar. Energy kahan se aayi? Outer wall pe ludhakte waqt jama hue gradients se, jo v me store the.

Imaandaar caveat (teacher ka): Ye isliye chala kyunki flat jagah aane se pehle v badi thi. Agar start hi w0 = 0.95 ho (shallow ghaati ke bilkul andar), to har β atak jaata hai. Momentum search strategy nahi hai, memory hai — aur memory tabhi kaam aati hai jab yaad rakhne layak kuch ho.

Nuksaan

  • Overshoot: minimum ke paas pahunch ke bhi velocity bachi rehti hai, to wo paar nikal jaata hai aur oscillate karta hai (16.5: lowest 0.5208, minimum se 0.4792 paar, settle step 42 pe). Ilaaj → NAG (16.9).
  • Ek extra hyperparameter β (typical 0.9; kabhi 0.5 se shuru karke 0.99 tak).
  • Ek extra memory: har parameter ke liye ek velocity number (parameters jitni ek copy).
  • Momentum direction theek karta hai, distance nahi: har parameter ka learning rate abhi bhi same α. Teacher ka Worksheet 08: α = 0.08 pe flat direction ko 574 steps chahiye the, momentum ne 539 kiye — sirf 6% sudhar. "It is not the fix." Asli fix → Chapter 17.

Exam Radar

  • Momentum = EWMA of gradients; stores velocity (a gradient average), not labels / Hessian.
  • Typical β (momentum) = 0.9. Effective memory ~10 steps.
  • Same-direction gradients → accumulate → acceleration; alternating gradients → cancel → less zig-zag.
  • Ek ulta gradient velocity ko turant reverse nahi karta (weight sirf 1 − β).
  • PyTorch form me constant gradient pe velocity → g/(1 − β) = 10g (β = 0.9).
  • Main drawback: overshoot near the minimum. History: heavy-ball method, Polyak 1964; backprop me Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986).

16.8 PyTorch me momentum: optim.SGD(..., momentum=0.9)

PyTorch me momentum alag class nahi hai — optim.SGD ka ek argument hai:

API

optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, momentum=0.9)
# poora signature (important args):
# optim.SGD(params, lr=1e-3, momentum=0, dampening=0, weight_decay=0, nesterov=False)
  • params — kaunse tensors update karne hain (aksar model.parameters()).
  • lr — learning rate η. (Purane PyTorch versions me lr dena compulsory tha; naye versions me default 1e-3 hai — exam me hamesha khud likho.)
  • momentum — β. Default 0 = plain SGD. 0.9 sabse common.
  • dampening — velocity me naye gradient pe (1 − dampening) factor. Default 0.
  • weight_decay — L2 penalty, gradient me λw jodta hai (Chapter 19).
  • nesterov — True karne pe NAG (16.10).
PyTorch: bt = μ·bt−1 + (1 − τ)·gt  (pehle step pe b1 = g1)    w ← w − lr·bt
  • b = "momentum buffer" (velocity), har parameter ke liye optimizer ki state me store hota hai.
  • μ = momentum, τ = dampening. τ = 0 pe ye exactly form (b) hai.

PyTorch · course ke worksheet numbers PyTorch se reproduce karo

import torch
import torch.optim as optim

# ek sample x=2, y=2  ->  L = 0.5*(w*x - y)^2  ->  grad = 4(w - 1)
x, y = 2.0, 2.0
w = torch.tensor([2.0], requires_grad=True)

alpha, beta = 0.25, 0.8                       # course (EWMA form) ke numbers
optimizer = optim.SGD([w], lr=alpha * (1 - beta), momentum=beta)   # lr = 0.05

for step in range(1, 5):
    optimizer.zero_grad()                     # purane .grad saaf
    loss = 0.5 * (w * x - y) ** 2             # forward
    loss.backward()                           # w.grad = 4(w - 1)
    optimizer.step()                          # buffer update + weight update
    print(f"step {step}: w = {w.item():.4f}")

Output (asli PyTorch run)

step 1: w = 1.8000
step 2: w = 1.4800
step 3: w = 1.1280
step 4: w = 0.8208

Bilkul worksheet wale numbers! Kyunki form (c) with α = 0.25 ≡ PyTorch with lr = 0.25 × (1 − 0.8) = 0.05.

Python · manual momentum (course ka EWMA form), bina PyTorch

def grad(w):
    return 4 * (w - 1)            # dL/dw for x=2, y=2

w, v = 2.0, 0.0                   # v0 = 0
alpha, beta = 0.25, 0.8
for t in range(1, 7):
    g = grad(w)                               # 1) gradient abhi wale w pe
    v = beta * v + (1 - beta) * g             # 2) velocity = EWMA of gradients
    w = w - alpha * v                         # 3) velocity ki direction me kadam
    print(f"t={t}  g={g:.4f}  v={v:.4f}  w={w:.4f}")

Output

t=1  g=4.0000  v=0.8000  w=1.8000
t=2  g=3.2000  v=1.2800  w=1.4800
t=3  g=1.9200  v=1.4080  w=1.1280
t=4  g=0.5120  v=1.2288  w=0.8208
t=5  g=-0.7168  v=0.8397  w=0.6109
t=6  g=-1.5565  v=0.3604  w=0.5208

Training loop me kuch nahi badalta — sirf optimizer wali line: optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, momentum=0.9), baaki zero_grad → forward → loss → backward → step wahi (Chapter 13).

Galti mat karna

  • optim.Momentum naam ki koi class nahi hai. Momentum = optim.SGD(..., momentum=0.9).
  • Momentum buffer optimizer ke andar rehta hai. Har epoch naya optimizer banaoge to velocity reset ho jaayegi — optimizer loop ke bahar ek baar banao.
  • optimizer.zero_grad() bhoole to .grad jud-te jaayenge (ye momentum nahi, bug hai).

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

Momentum = ludhakti gend. β = kitni speed bachi rehti hai, α = kitna lamba kadam. Seedhi dhalaan pe tez, uchhal-kood cancel, par minimum ke paas brake nahi.

16.9 NAG (Nesterov Accelerated Gradient) — look before you leap

Kahani

Raju auto-rickshaw wala tez chala raha hai. Aage speed-breaker hai. Naya driver tab brake marta hai jab pahiya speed-breaker pe chadh chuka hota hai — dhadaam! Raju experienced hai: wo dekhta hai ki is speed se main 2 second baad kahan hounga, wahan speed-breaker dikhta hai, to pehle se brake laga deta hai. Worksheet 06 me yahi cyclist ki kahani hai jo sharp mod (bend) aane se pehle aage dekh ke dheema ho jaata hai.

Momentum naya driver hai: gradient wahin naapta hai jahan abhi khada hai. NAG Raju hai: gradient wahan naapta hai jahan velocity use le ja rahi hai.

Look-ahead point aaya kahan se? (teacher ka derivation)

Momentum ki dono lines ko jodo (velocity ko weight wali line me substitute karo):

wt = wt−1 − α( βvt−1 + (1 − β)gt )
= wt−1 − αβvt−1 − α(1 − β)gt
       ↑ pehle se tay (committed)     ↑ naya gradient ka contribution

Pehle term me gt hai hi nahi! Naya gradient kuch bhi ho, step ka ye hissa to hona hi hai. To gradient naapne ki imaandaar jagah us committed hisse ke end pe hai: wlook = wt−1 − αβvt−1. Gradient wahan naapo.

1 predict: wlook = wt−1 − αβ·vt−1
2 measure: g = ∇L(wlook)
3 correct: vt = β·vt−1 + (1 − β)·g
4 move: wt = wt−1 − α·vt
  • wlook = look-ahead point: jahan step ka already-committed hissa tumhe le jaayega.
  • αβvt−1 = wahi committed hissa. Factor αβ hai, sirf α nahi, kyunki velocity ka sirf βvt−1 hissa naya gradient aane se pehle fix hai.
  • g = gradient, wlook pe naapa gaya, wt−1 pe nahi. Poora farak bas yahi hai.
  • vt, wt, α, β — sab momentum jaise. Actual update hamesha asli wt−1 se hota hai, look-ahead point se nahi.

Teacher ki line: "The order is the method. Swap actions 1 and 2 and you are back to plain momentum." Aur Worksheet 06: "Momentum asks: what is the slope here? NAG asks: what is the slope where momentum is taking me?"

Pehla step hamesha same: v0 = 0 hai, to wlook = w0. NAG aur momentum ka step 1 identical hota hai; farak step 2 se shuru hota hai jab velocity ho.

Doosra common form (Sutskever / cs231n)

vt = β·vt−1 + η·∇L(θt−1 − βvt−1)     θt = θt−1 − vt
  • Ye momentum ka form (a) hai, bas gradient look-ahead point θ − βv pe. Yahan look-ahead "−βv" hai (−αβv nahi) kyunki is form me v ke andar η pehle se ghusa hua hai.
  • 16.6 jaisa hi: course form (α, β) ≡ is form ke saath η = α(1 − β). Lab 7 isko "gradient computed at wt − ηβvt" likhta hai (PyTorch-form velocity ke saath).

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 06 ladder (ek step)

Sawaal: θt = 2.000, vt = 0.500, α = 0.1, β = 0.9, aur look-ahead pe gradient ∇L(θlook) = 3.000. (Worksheet index t → t+1 use karti hai; matlab same.)

  1. Predict: θlook = 2.000 − 0.1(0.9)(0.500) = 2.000 − 0.045 = 1.955
  2. Correct ke do terms: βvt = 0.9(0.500) = 0.450, (1 − β)∇L(θlook) = 0.1(3.000) = 0.300
  3. Jodo: vt+1 = 0.450 + 0.300 = 0.750
  4. Move (asli parameter se): θt+1 = 2.000 − 0.1(0.750) = 1.925

θ: 2.000 → 1.925. Velocity ne look-ahead point ko downhill bheja; wahan ka gradient next velocity ko correct karta hai.

Practice: θt = 1.500, vt = 0.200, α = 0.1, β = 0.8, ∇L(θlook) = −1.000 → θlook = 1.500 − 0.1(0.8)(0.200) = 1.484, vt+1 = 0.8(0.200) + 0.2(−1) = 0.160 − 0.200 = −0.040, θt+1 = 1.500 − 0.1(−0.040) = 1.504.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — momentum vs NAG, same problem (Worksheet 07 solved)

Wahi 16.5 wala: g(w) = 4(w − 1), minimum w = 1, w0 = 2.0000, v0 = 0, α = 0.25, β = 0.8. Shortcut: αβ = 0.25 × 0.8 = 0.2, to wlook = w − 0.2v.

  1. Step 1 — predict wlook = 2.0000 − 0.2(0) = 2.0000; measure g = 4(2.0000 − 1) = 4.0000; correct v1 = 0.8(0) + 0.2(4.0000) = 0.8000; move w1 = 2.0000 − 0.25(0.8000) = 1.8000. Momentum ne bhi 1.8000 diya — expected.
  2. Step 2 — wlook = 1.8000 − 0.2(0.8000) = 1.6400; g = 4(1.6400 − 1) = 2.5600 (momentum ne 3.2000 use kiya tha); v2 = 0.6400 + 0.5120 = 1.1520; w2 = 1.8000 − 0.2880 = 1.5120. Momentum 1.4800 pe tha — NAG thoda peeche hai: aage chhota gradient dikha, to kam velocity banayi.
  3. Step 3 — wlook = 1.5120 − 0.2(1.1520) = 1.2816; g = 4(0.2816) = 1.1264; v3 = 0.9216 + 0.2253 = 1.1469; w3 = 1.5120 − 0.25(1.1469) = 1.2253
  4. Step 4 (payoff) — wlook = 1.2253 − 0.2(1.1469) = 0.9959 ← minimum ke paar ja chuka! g = 4(0.9959 − 1) = −0.0164 ← negative, peeche bolta hai; v4 = 0.8(1.1469) + 0.2(−0.0164) = 0.9175 − 0.0033 = 0.9142; w4 = 1.2253 − 0.25(0.9142) = 1.2253 − 0.2286 = 0.9967
  5. Yahi brake hai: w = 1.2253 pe asli gradient 4(0.2253) = +0.9012 tha ("aur neeche jao"), par look-ahead minimum cross kar chuka tha, to wahan ka gradient negative aaya aur velocity badhne ke bajaye ghati. Momentum ne apne step 4 pe current point (1.1280) pe gradient +0.512 naapa, velocity 1.2288 rakhi, aur 0.8208 pe gira.

NAG: 1.8000 → 1.5120 → 1.2253 → 0.9967 (minimum se sirf 0.0033 paar). Momentum: → 0.8208 (0.1792 paar).

Exam Radar

  • NAG gradient look-ahead point pe naapta hai: wlook = w − αβv (course form) ya θ − βv (classic form).
  • 4 ordered actions: predict → measure → correct → move. Pehle do swap kiye = plain momentum.
  • Pehla step momentum ke barabar (v0 = 0). NAG early me thoda peeche, par overshoot kam, settle jaldi.
  • NAG fixes momentum's overshoot ("brakes"); still one global learning rate for all parameters.
  • Yuri Nesterov, 1983 (convex optimization); deep learning me Sutskever et al. 2013 ne popular kiya.

16.10 NAG in PyTorch: nesterov=True + manual implementation

API

optimizer = optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, momentum=0.9, nesterov=True)
  • nesterov=True ke liye momentum > 0 aur dampening = 0 zaroori. Warna PyTorch error deta hai: ValueError: Nesterov momentum requires a momentum and zero dampening (real run se check kiya).
  • PyTorch ka NAG formula: bt = μbt−1 + gt, phir w ← w − lr·(gt + μbt). Yahan gt current w pe hi naapa jaata hai — look-ahead pe alag se forward/backward nahi karna padta.
  • Ye classic NAG ka hi rearranged (equivalent) form hai: PyTorch jo weights store karta hai wo classic NAG ke look-ahead points hote hain. Isliye printed numbers hand-calculation se alag dikhenge, par dono same minimum pe pahunchte hain.

PyTorch · nesterov=True, worksheet wala problem

import torch
import torch.optim as optim

x, y = 2.0, 2.0                                   # grad = 4(w - 1)
w = torch.tensor([2.0], requires_grad=True)
optimizer = optim.SGD([w], lr=0.25 * (1 - 0.8), momentum=0.8, nesterov=True)

for step in range(1, 6):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    loss = 0.5 * (w * x - y) ** 2
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    print(f"step {step}: w = {w.item():.4f}")

Output (asli PyTorch run)

step 1: w = 1.6400
step 2: w = 1.2816
step 3: w = 0.9959
step 4: w = 0.8139
step 5: w = 0.7346

Dhyaan se dekho: 1.6400, 1.2816, 0.9959 — ye bilkul upar wale hand-calculation ke wlook values hain (step 2, 3, 4 ke)! PyTorch ka parameter "ek kadam aage jhaanka hua" point hai. Same algorithm, alag bookkeeping.

Python · manual NAG (course form) — hand numbers verify

def grad(w):
    return 4 * (w - 1)

w, v = 2.0, 0.0
alpha, beta = 0.25, 0.8
for t in range(1, 5):
    w_look = w - alpha * beta * v          # 1) predict: committed hissa aage
    g = grad(w_look)                       # 2) measure: gradient WAHAN
    v = beta * v + (1 - beta) * g          # 3) correct: velocity update
    w = w - alpha * v                      # 4) move: asli w se kadam
    print(f"t={t}  w_look={w_look:.4f}  g={g:.4f}  v={v:.4f}  w={w:.4f}")

Output

t=2  w_look=1.6400  g=2.5600  v=1.1520  w=1.5120
t=3  w_look=1.2816  g=1.1264  v=1.1469  w=1.2253
t=4  w_look=0.9959  g=-0.0164  v=0.9142  w=0.9967

f(θ) = θ2, gradient 2θ, θ0 = 1, lr η = 0.1, momentum 0.9 (PyTorch form b). Plain GD: θ ← θ − 0.1(2θ) = 0.8θ.

  1. Momentum step 1: g = 2, v = 2, θ = 1 − 0.1(2) = 0.8
  2. Step 2: g = 1.6, v = 0.9(2) + 1.6 = 3.4, θ = 0.8 − 0.34 = 0.46

Galti mat karna

  • nesterov=True akela kaafi nahi — momentum bhi dena padega (default 0 hai, to error).
  • NAG ka actual update hamesha current w se hota hai; look-ahead point sirf gradient naapne ke liye hai.
  • Look-ahead factor course form me αβv hai; αv (poora step) nahi.

Exam Radar

  • Increasing EWMA β gives a smoother (and longer) memory. (Worksheet 06 MCQ.)
  • Momentum stores a gradient average. NAG measures its gradient at the look-ahead point.
  • Course formulas: vt = βvt−1 + (1 − β)gt, wt = wt−1 − αvt; NAG wlook = wt−1 − αβvt−1.
  • PyTorch: optim.SGD(params, lr=0.01, momentum=0.9); nesterov=True needs momentum > 0, dampening = 0. SGD defaults: momentum 0, dampening 0, weight_decay 0, nesterov False.
  • Course form (α, β) ≡ PyTorch form with lr = α(1 − β).
  • Diagnosis map (Worksheet 06): noisy direction → Momentum; overshoot risk → NAG.

Dimaag me aise baitha lo

SGD reacts, EWMA remembers, Momentum rolls, NAG peeks. "Momentum: slope yahan kya hai? NAG: slope wahan kya hai jahan main ja raha hoon?"

Chapter 17

Adaptive Learning Rates: AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam (+AdamW)

Har parameter ka apna step size · g² ki memory · bias correction · decoupled weight decay · Optimizer Zoo

Momentum ne direction theek ki — kidhar chalna hai. Par kitna chalna hai, wo abhi bhi har parameter ke liye same α se tay hota hai. Teacher ke Worksheet 08 ka title hi yahi kehta hai: "One Learning Rate Is Not Enough — every parameter gets its own step size, measured from its own gradients." Is chapter ka safar: SGD → AdaGrad (g² ka total) → RMSProp (g² ka EWMA) → Adam (EWMA of g + EWMA of g² + bias correction) → AdamW (weight decay alag).

17.1 Ek learning rate sabke liye kyun nahi chalta

Kahani

Board exam aa rahe hain. Golu ki mummy uski padhai sambhal rahi hain. Physics ke sawaal roz aate hain, har din bade-bade galtiyan dikhti hain (bade gradients) — mummy kehti hain "Physics me ab chhote-chhote sudhaar karo, bahut ho gaya". Sanskrit hafte me ek baar padha jaata hai, galtiyan chhoti aur kabhi-kabhi dikhti hain (chhote, rare gradients) — mummy kehti hain "jab bhi Sanskrit ka mauka mile, zor laga ke padho". Har subject ka apna "kitna zor" — uske apne record ke hisaab se.

Ek aur example: WhatsApp group ki chat se language model seekh raha hai. "hai", "the", "ok" jaise words har message me aate hain (frequent features, unke weights ko roz update milta hai). "Kanyakumari" ya "Dhoni" kabhi-kabhi aate hain (rare / sparse features). Rare word ko jab bhi update mile, wo bada hona chahiye, warna wo kabhi seekh hi nahi paayega.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 08 Part 1

Ek network ke do parameters: w1 steep direction pe, w2 flat direction pe. Dono 1.0000 se shuru. Measured gradients: w1 ke 3 phir 4; w2 ke 0.3 phir 0.4 (har step 10 guna chhote). Plain SGD, α = 0.1:

  1. w1: 1.0000 − 0.1(3) = 0.7000, phir 0.7000 − 0.1(4) = 0.3000
  2. w2: 1.0000 − 0.1(0.3) = 0.9700, phir 0.9700 − 0.1(0.4) = 0.9300

w1 0.7000 chala, w2 sirf 0.0700 — das guna farak, kyunki step = α × gradient, aur kuch nahi.

α ghatao to w1 sudhar jaata hai par w2 ruk jaata hai; badhao to w2 chalta hai par w1 overshoot/diverge. Teacher ki animation ka measurement (steep aur flat direction ko finish hone me kitne steps):

αsteep direction ke stepsflat direction ke stepsflat, momentum β = 0.9 ke saath
0.022123012268
0.083574539
0.1944241200
0.22diverges165—

α = 0.08 pe steep direction 3 steps me khatam, flat ko 574 chahiye. Momentum 574 → 539 (sirf 6% sudhaar). Koi bhi ek α dono ke liye sahi nahi. Jawab (Worksheet 08): har parameter ka step uske apne gradients ke "running size" se divide karo. Jis parameter ke gradients lagataar bade rahe (steep), wo chhote kadam le; jiske chhote rahe (flat), wo bade kadam le. Ab poora chapter ek sawaal hai: wo running measure kya ho?

Definition

Adaptive learning rate method: optimizer jo har parameter ke liye alag effective learning rate rakhta hai, jo us parameter ke pichhle gradients ke size (aksar squared gradients) se automatically set hota hai. Examples: AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW.

17.2 AdaGrad — apni history se divide karo

AdaGrad (Adaptive Gradient) — Duchi, Hazan & Singer, 2011 (JMLR). Gradient ka size naapne ka sabse simple tareeka: har parameter ke saare squared gradients jodte jao. Square isliye ki sign cancel na ho (−10 bhi +10 jitna bada gradient hai).

Gt = Gt−1 + gt2     wt = wt−1 − α√Gt + ε·gt
  • gt = is parameter ka current gradient; gt2 = uska square (element-wise: har parameter apna-apna, ⊙).
  • Gt = accumulator: ab tak ke saare squared gradients ka sum, G0 = 0. Har parameter ka apna G (worksheet 06 ise rt, classroom notebook st likhta hai).
  • α/(√Gt + ε) = us parameter ka effective (adaptive) learning rate.
  • ε (epsilon) ≈ 10−8 (PyTorch Adagrad me default 10−10): bas zero se divide hone se bachane ke liye; hand calculation me ignore karte hain. Kuch books √(G + ε) likhti hain — idea same.

√ kyun, G se seedha divide kyun nahi? Units! G gradient² ki units me hai; √G wapas gradient ki units me. To g/√G ek pure number ban jaata hai (size-free), aur step ka size α tay karta hai. Worksheet 08 ki line: "The gradient now sets the direction of the step. It no longer sets the distance."

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 08 Part 2 (do parameters)

Sawaal: w1 = w2 = 1.0000, α = 0.1, G0 = 0. Gradients w1: 3, 4; w2: 0.3, 0.4. ε ignore.

  1. Step 1, w1: G1 = 0 + 32 = 9.0000, √9 = 3.0000, step = 0.1(3)/3.0000 = 0.1000
  2. Step 1, w2: G1 = 0 + 0.32 = 0.0900, √0.09 = 0.3000, step = 0.1(0.3)/0.3000 = 0.1000. Gradients 10 guna alag, steps bilkul barabar!
  3. Step 2, w1: G2 = 9.0000 + 42 = 25.0000, √25 = 5.0000, step = 0.1(4)/5.0000 = 0.0800; w1 = 0.9000 − 0.0800 = 0.8200
  4. Step 2, w2: G2 = 0.0900 + 0.42 = 0.2500, √0.25 = 0.5000, step = 0.1(0.4)/0.5000 = 0.0800; w2 = 0.8200
G₁step 1G₂step 2w after
w₁9.00000.100025.00000.08000.8200
w₂0.09000.10000.25000.08000.8200

Plain SGD ne inhe 0.3000 aur 0.9300 pe chhoda; AdaGrad ne dono ko 0.8200 aur 0.8200 pe. Parameter ke saare gradients ko 10 se multiply karo to √G bhi 10 guna, ratio g/√G wahi.

Pehla step hamesha exactly α: t = 1 pe G1 = g12, to step = αg1/|g1| = ±α, gradient chahe kuch bhi ho.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 06 (vector, ek saath)

Sawaal: rt−1 = (0, 0), gt = (4, 1), ε ignore.

  1. Square each coordinate: g2 = (42, 12) = (16, 1)
  2. Accumulator: rt = (0, 0) + (16, 1) = (16, 1)
  3. Square root: √rt = (√16, √1) = (4, 1)
  4. Normalise: g/√r = (4/4, 1/1) = (1, 1) — raw gradient 4 wala coordinate bhi effective 1, aur 1 wala bhi 1.
  5. Agla identical gradient (4, 1): r = (32, 2), g/√r = (4/5.657, 1/1.414) = (0.707, 0.707) — step chhota ho gaya.

AdaGrad baar-baar bade gradient wale coordinate ko "cautious" banata hai. Drawback: cumulative denominator kabhi bhoolta nahi.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — step kaise sikudta hai (classroom notebook, 4 steps)

Sawaal: w0 = 5, s0 = 0, α = 0.1, har step gradient g = 2.

  1. s1 = 0 + 22 = 4, step = 0.1 × 2/√4 = 0.1000, w1 = 4.9000
  2. s2 = 4 + 4 = 8, step = 0.1 × 2/√8 = 0.2/2.8284 = 0.0707, w2 = 4.8293
  3. s3 = 12, step = 0.2/3.4641 = 0.0577, w3 = 4.7716
  4. s4 = 16, step = 0.2/4 = 0.0500, w4 = 4.7216

Gradient same (2) raha, phir bhi step 0.1 → 0.0707 → 0.0577 → 0.05. Constant gradient pe step = α/√t.

AdaGrad kya tod deta hai: learning rate mar jaata hai

g2 kabhi negative nahi, to G sirf badhta hai. Steady gradient g ke liye Gt = tg2, to effective step = α/√(tg2) = (α/g)·(1/√t):

t steps baadGteffective step α/√Gt
1g²1.0000 α/g
44g²0.5000 α/g
2525g²0.2000 α/g
100100g²0.1000 α/g
400400g²0.0500 α/g
25002500g²0.0200 α/g
1000010000g²0.0100 α/g

Teacher ne Part 1 wale loss pe naapa (α = 0.1): flat direction ka effective step 1 step baad 0.1000, 10 baad 0.0325, 100 baad 0.0113, 1000 baad 0.0049 (α ka sirf 4.9%). AdaGrad ko flat direction 1% tak laane me 10590 steps lage, jabki plain SGD (α = 0.19) ne 241 me kar diya. "Equalising the two parameters cost us the ability to finish." Wajah: measure ke paas bhoolne ka koi tareeka nahi — step 5 ka gradient aur step 5000 ka gradient G me barabar gina jaata hai, jabki parameter tab tak bahut aage nikal chuka.

Fayde: per-parameter learning rate khud set hota hai (manual tuning kam); sparse features ke liye bahut accha (NLP word embeddings, recommendation — rare features ka G chhota rehta hai, to unhe bade updates milte hain); gradient scale se fark nahi padta. Nuksaan: G sirf badhta hai → effective LR → 0 → learning ruk jaati hai (deep nets ki lambi training me pehle hi); har parameter ke liye ek extra accumulator (memory). Lab 7 ke chikne quadratic bowl pe yahi "weakness" faayda ban gayi (decaying step ne bina overshoot ke minimum pe utaar diya — 17.8 dekho).

PyTorch · optim.Adagrad — Worksheet 08 numbers reproduce

import torch
import torch.optim as optim

w = torch.tensor([1.0, 1.0], requires_grad=True)     # [w1 (steep), w2 (flat)]
optimizer = optim.Adagrad([w], lr=0.1)               # defaults: lr_decay=0, initial_accumulator_value=0, eps=1e-10

for g in [[3.0, 0.3], [4.0, 0.4]]:                   # worksheet ke measured gradients
    w.grad = torch.tensor(g)          # gradient seedha daal diya (optimizer sirf .grad padhta hai)
    optimizer.step()
    print(w.tolist())

Output (asli PyTorch run)

[0.8999999761581421, 0.8999999761581421]
[0.8199999928474426, 0.8199999928474426]

Float32 ki wajah se 0.8999999... dikhta hai — matlab 0.9000 aur 0.8200. Trick note karo: optimizer.step() sirf p.grad padhta hai, to hum w.grad me koi bhi gradient daal ke hand-calculation check kar sakte hain. Normal training me ye loss.backward() bharta hai.

  • optim.Adagrad(params, lr=0.01, lr_decay=0, weight_decay=0, initial_accumulator_value=0, eps=1e-10) — default lr = 0.01.
  • initial_accumulator_value = G0 (default 0). lr_decay = lr ko aur ghatane ka option (default 0).

numpy · manual AdaGrad (element-wise, vector parameters)

import numpy as np

w = np.array([1.0, 1.0])
G = np.zeros_like(w)              # har parameter ka apna accumulator, G0 = 0
lr, eps = 0.1, 1e-8
for g in [np.array([3.0, 0.3]), np.array([4.0, 0.4])]:
    G = G + g ** 2                            # squared gradients ka running SUM
    step = lr * g / (np.sqrt(G) + eps)        # har coordinate ka apna effective lr
    w = w - step
    print("G =", G, " step =", step.round(4), " w =", w.round(4))

Output

G = [9.   0.09]  step = [0.1 0.1]  w = [0.9 0.9]
G = [25.    0.25]  step = [0.08 0.08]  w = [0.82 0.82]

Exam Radar

  • AdaGrad: accumulates sum of squared gradients forever (cumulative g²), per parameter.
  • Effective LR = α/(√G + ε): frequent/large-gradient parameters → small steps; rare/small → relatively large steps → sparse data (NLP) ke liye best.
  • Main drawback: learning rate monotonically decays to ~0 → training premature stop. Constant gradient pe step ∝ 1/√t.
  • First step = exactly α (sign of g). PyTorch defaults: lr 0.01, eps 1e-10.

17.3 RMSProp — aisa average jo bhoolna jaanta hai

Kahani

Chhata (umbrella) le ke jaayein ya nahi? AdaGrad wala aadmi pichhle 10 saal ki har weather report jod ke faisla karta hai — 2016 ka toofan aaj bhi uske faisle me utna hi bhaari hai. RMSProp wala aadmi haal-filhaal ka mausam yaad rakhta hai; mahino purana toofan dheere-dheere fade ho jaata hai (Worksheet 06 ki analogy). Pahadi trekker bhi aisa hi: dheeli patthar wali jagah chhote kadam, pakki zameen aayi to phir normal kadam — purani dheeli zameen ki yaad hamesha ke liye nahi.

RMSProp (Root Mean Square Propagation) — Geoffrey Hinton ne apne Coursera course "Neural Networks for Machine Learning" ke Lecture 6e (2012) me propose kiya (Tieleman & Hinton). Ye kabhi formal paper me publish nahi hua — famous "unpublished" optimizer. Idea: Chapter 16 ka EWMA gradients pe chala ke direction smooth ki thi; wahi EWMA squared gradients pe chalao to size track ho jaayega.

E[g2]t = β·E[g2]t−1 + (1 − β)·gt2     wt = wt−1 − α√E[g2]t + ε·gt
  • E[g2]t = squared gradients ka EWMA (running mean of g²). Worksheet 08 ise vt (decay β2), Worksheet 06 st (decay ρ), Lab 7 aur PyTorch decay ko alpha, Keras rho kehte hain. Sab ek hi cheez.
  • √E[g2] = "Root of Mean of Squares" = RMS of recent gradients → naam RMSProp.
  • β = decay rate, typical 0.9 (Hinton), PyTorch default alpha=0.99. ~1/(1 − β) recent gradients "recent" maane jaate hain.
  • α = learning rate (Hinton ne 0.001 suggest kiya; PyTorch default lr = 0.01). ε ≈ 10−8.

Teacher: "Only the accumulator changed. The update line is AdaGrad's." AdaGrad har squared gradient jodta hai; RMSProp recent waalon ka average leta hai. Classroom notebook: "That one change is the core evolution from Adagrad to RMSProp."

AdaGrad

Gt = Gt−1 + gt2
saare purane g² hamesha ke liye
late training: aur darpok (step → 0)

RMSProp

vt = βvt−1 + (1 − β)gt2
purana scale baar-baar discount
late training: step wapas aa sakta hai

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 08 Part 4 (β₂ = 0.9)

Sawaal: w1 = 1.0000, v0 = 0, α = 0.1, β2 = 0.9, gradients 3 phir 4 (squared 9, 16). (w2 ke 0.3, 0.4 bilkul same steps denge.)

  1. Step 1: v1 = 0.9(0) + 0.1(9.0000) = 0.9000; √0.9000 = 0.9487; step = 0.1(3)/0.9487 = 0.3162; w1 = 1.0000 − 0.3162 = 0.6838
  2. Dhyaan: α = 0.1 tha, step 0.3162 hua — 3.16 guna! (Wajah neeche.)
  3. Step 2: v2 = 0.9(0.9000) + 0.1(16.0000) = 0.8100 + 1.6000 = 2.4100; √2.4100 = 1.5524; step = 0.1(4)/1.5524 = 0.2577; w1 = 0.6838 − 0.2577 = 0.4261
v₁step 1v₂step 2w after
w₁0.90000.31622.41000.25770.4261
w₂0.00900.31620.02410.25770.4261

Sum ki jagah exponentially weighted average aaya, aur step decay hona band hua (AdaGrad: 0.1, 0.08; RMSProp: 0.3162, 0.2577).

RMSProp ki apni problem: pehla step bahut bada

v0 = 0, to v1 = (1 − β2)g12 — ye g12 ka estimate nahi, uska sirf das-va hissa hai (β₂ = 0.9 pe). Square root 3.16 guna chhota, to step 3.16 guna bada:

first step = αg1√(1 − β2)g12 = α√1 − β2
  • Gradient cancel ho gaya — error ka size sirf β2 pe depend karta hai. Ye wahi 16.4 wala start-up bias hai, ab denominator me.
β₂1 − β₂RMSProp ka pehla step (α ki units me)
0.50.5001.41 ×
0.90.1003.16 ×
0.99 (PyTorch default)0.01010.00 ×
0.9990.00131.62 ×

Mazedaar check: f(θ) = θ2, θ0 = 1, optim.RMSprop(lr=0.1) (alpha 0.99): pehla step = 10 × 0.1 = 1.0, to θ seedha 0 pe (asli PyTorch run: 5.96e-08, yaani float32 me lagbhag 0). PyTorch ka RMSprop bias correction nahi karta.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 06 (purana scale fade hota hai)

Sawaal: st−1 = (16, 1), gt = (4, 1), ρ = 0.9, ε ignore.

  1. Square: g2 = (16, 1)
  2. Purane scale ka 90%: ρst−1 = 0.9(16, 1) = (14.4, 0.9)
  3. Naye squared gradient ka 10%: (1 − ρ)g2 = 0.1(16, 1) = (1.6, 0.1) → st = (14.4 + 1.6, 0.9 + 0.1) = (16, 1)
  4. Normalise: g/√s = (4/√16, 1/√1) = (1, 1)
  5. Practice: st−1 = (4, 9), g = (2, 3), ρ = 0.5 → s = 0.5(4, 9) + 0.5(4, 9) = (4, 9), g/√s = (2/2, 3/3) = (1, 1)

Is step me s AdaGrad jaisa (16, 1) hi aaya, to kya dono same hain? Nahi! RMSProp me bahut purana squared gradient har step 0.9 se multiply ho ke ghatta jaata hai; AdaGrad me wo hamesha poora gina jaata hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — recovery: gradient achanak chhota ho jaaye

Pehle 20 steps gradient 10 (bade-bade), phir step 21 se hamesha 1. α = 0.1, RMSProp β = 0.9. Gradient 1 wale steps ka size dekho (Python se compute):

AdaGrad purane toofan (g = 10) ko kabhi nahi bhoolta: step hamesha ~0.0022 (α ka 2%). RMSProp ka v purane bade gradients ko bhool jaata hai aur step wapas ~α (0.1) ki taraf aata hai.

PyTorch · optim.RMSprop — Worksheet 08 numbers

w = torch.tensor([1.0, 1.0], requires_grad=True)
optimizer = optim.RMSprop([w], lr=0.1, alpha=0.9)     # alpha = DECAY rate (beta2), learning rate nahi!

    w.grad = torch.tensor(g)
    optimizer.step()

Output (asli PyTorch run)

[0.6838, 0.6838]

  • optim.RMSprop(params, lr=0.01, alpha=0.99, eps=1e-08, weight_decay=0, momentum=0, centered=False) — defaults yaad karo: lr 0.01, alpha 0.99.
  • alpha = smoothing/decay constant of the squared-gradient EWMA (course ka β / ρ). Keras me isi ka naam rho (classroom notebook: tf.keras.optimizers.RMSprop(learning_rate=0.01, rho=0.9)).
  • momentum > 0 diya to: b = μb + g/(√v + ε), w −= lr·b (RMSProp + momentum). centered=True → gradient ka variance estimate (mean² ghata ke) se normalize.

numpy · manual RMSProp + AdaGrad vs RMSProp accumulator (classroom notebook)

import numpy as np

w = np.array([1.0, 1.0])
v = np.zeros_like(w)
lr, beta, eps = 0.1, 0.9, 1e-8
for g in [np.array([3.0, 0.3]), np.array([4.0, 0.4])]:
    v = beta * v + (1 - beta) * g ** 2        # g^2 ka EWMA (bhoolne wala average)
    step = lr * g / (np.sqrt(v) + eps)
    w = w - step
    print("v =", v.round(4), " step =", step.round(4), " w =", w.round(4))

g = 2.0                                       # constant gradient: dono accumulators compare
s_ada, s_rms = 0.0, 0.0
print("step | Adagrad s | RMSProp s")
for t in range(1, 11):
    s_ada = s_ada + g**2                      # sirf badhta hai
    s_rms = beta*s_rms + (1-beta)*g**2        # g^2 = 4 ki taraf jaata hai, usse upar nahi
    print(f"{t:>4} | {s_ada:>9.3f} | {s_rms:>9.3f}")

AdaGrad ka s 4, 8, 12 ... seedha badhta gaya; RMSProp ka s 4 (= g2) ki taraf jaata hai aur wahin rukta hai — bounded. (Classroom notebook ka hi example: w0 = 5, α = 0.01, β = 0.9, g = 2, 2 → s1 = 0.4, w1 = 5 − 0.01 × 2/√0.4 ≈ 4.9684, s2 = 0.9(0.4) + 0.1(4) = 0.76, w2 ≈ 4.9684 − 0.0229 = 4.9455.)

Exam Radar

  • RMSProp = AdaGrad with EWMA of g² instead of sum → fixes AdaGrad's dying learning rate; old scale fades, step can recover.
  • Proposed by Geoffrey Hinton, Coursera lecture 6e (2012), unpublished. Typical decay 0.9; PyTorch alpha default 0.99, lr default 0.01.
  • No first-moment (direction) memory by itself; no bias correction → first step = α/√(1 − β) (too large).
  • Match: AdaGrad → "squared gradients accumulated forever"; RMSProp → "fading squared-gradient scale".

Galti mat karna

  • PyTorch RMSprop ka alpha learning rate nahi hai (learning rate lr hai). Lab 7 me {'lr': 0.15, 'alpha': 0.9}.
  • RMSProp me numerator abhi bhi raw gradient gt hai (koi momentum average nahi) — wo Adam me aayega.

17.4 Adam — Momentum + RMSProp + bias correction

Kahani

Yaad hai Pappu bhaiya coach (16.2)? Ab unhone ek assistant rakh liya. Coach do register rakhte hain: (1) form register — batsman haal me kis direction me ja raha hai (runs badh rahe ya ghat rahe) = momentum; (2) "kitna uthal-puthal" register — is batsman ke scores aam taur pe kitne bade-chhote hote hain = RMSProp. Aur naye season ki shuruaat me dono registers me imaginary zeros hote hain, to wo unhe bias correct karke padhte hain. Faisla: "is player ko kitna push karna hai" = direction ÷ usual size.

Adam = Adaptive Moment estimation — Diederik Kingma & Jimmy Ba, 2014 (arXiv; ICLR 2015 me publish). Classroom notebook ki line: "Adam ≈ Momentum in the numerator + RMSProp in the denominator", plus bias correction.

RMSProp me kya kami thi? (Worksheet 08 Part 5)

  • Average zero se shuru hota hai → first step α/√(1 − β2) (β₂ = 0.999 pe 31.6 guna bada).
  • Numerator ek raw gradient hai → Chapter 16 ne dikhaya ek gradient noisy direction hai. RMSProp size theek karta hai, phir bhi raw gradient se point karta hai.

Dono halves humare paas pehle se hain: momentum ne gradient ka average liya (direction), RMSProp ne squared gradient ka (size). Ek square kyun karta hai, doosra kyun nahi? Gradients lo +3, −3, +3, −3: g ka total 0 ("koi bharosemand direction nahi" — sahi!), g2 ka total 36 ("gradients bade the" — ye bhi sahi!). m ko sign rakhna hai (palat-ti direction pe bharosa nahi karna), v ko sign phenkna hai (−10 bhi +10 jitna bada).

Teacher ka tareeka — RMSProp ki update line me ek-ek cheez badlo:

start:    wt = wt−1 − α gt / (√vt + ε)   (RMSProp)
change 1: wt = wt−1 − α mt / (√vt + ε)   (raw gradient ki jagah averaged direction)
change 2: wt = wt−1 − α m̂t / (√v̂t + ε)   (dono averages corrected) = Adam
1 direction: mt = β1·mt−1 + (1 − β1)·gt
2 size: vt = β2·vt−1 + (1 − β2)·gt2
3 correct: m̂t = mt1 − β1t    v̂t = vt1 − β2t
4 step: wt = wt−1 − α·m̂t√v̂t + ε
  • mt = first moment estimate (gradient ka mean, EWMA of g) — momentum wala, sign rakhta hai. PyTorch state me naam exp_avg.
  • vt = second (raw) moment estimate (EWMA of g2, "uncentered variance") — RMSProp wala, hamesha ≥ 0. PyTorch me exp_avg_sq. (Dhyaan: Adam ka v squared gradients hai, momentum wala velocity nahi!)
  • m̂, v̂ = bias-corrected versions (16.4 wala hi formula); t = step number (PyTorch state step).
  • β1 = 0.9 (direction ki memory ~10 steps), β2 = 0.999 (size ki memory ~1000 steps), α (lr) = 0.001, ε = 10−8 — paper aur PyTorch dono ke defaults.
  • m̂/(√v̂ + ε) = "direction ÷ usual size" — ek pure number, aksar ±1 ke aas-paas.
linekya haikahan mile the
1gradients ka averageMomentum (Chapter 16)
2squared gradients ka averageRMSProp (17.3)
3har average ko uske applied weight se dividebias correction (16.4)
4m̂ ki direction me, √v̂ se scaled stepAdaGrad ki update line (17.2)

Teacher: "There is no new idea on this page. Adam is the three previous parts, assembled." β₂ > β₁ kyun? Direction ko mod pe badal paana chahiye (chhoti memory, 0.9); size estimate denominator me baitha hai, use steady hona chahiye (lambi memory, 0.999) — jumpy denominator har step jumpy bana deta hai.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 06 ladder (defaults wale betas)

Sawaal: m0 = 0, v0 = 0, g1 = 4, β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.999, α = 0.01. ε ignore.

  1. First moment (direction memory): m1 = 0.9(0) + 0.1(4) = 0.4
  2. Second moment (scale memory): v1 = 0.999(0) + 0.001(42) = 0.016
  3. Bias-correct m: m̂1 = 0.4/(1 − 0.9) = 0.4/0.1 = 4 (correction ne estimate bada kiya — wahi chahiye tha, kyunki 0.4 zero ki taraf biased tha)
  4. Bias-correct v: v̂1 = 0.016/(1 − 0.999) = 0.016/0.001 = 16
  5. Normalised direction: m̂1/√v̂1 = 4/√16 = 4/4 = 1
  6. Movement: Δθ1 = 0.01(1) = 0.01, θ1 = θ0 − 0.01
  7. Continuation, g2 = 2: m2 = 0.9(0.4) + 0.1(2) = 0.36 + 0.2 = 0.56, v2 = 0.999(0.016) + 0.001(22) = 0.015984 + 0.004 = 0.019984
  8. Poora step 2: 1 − 0.92 = 0.19 → m̂2 = 0.56/0.19 = 2.9474; 1 − 0.9992 = 0.001999 → v̂2 = 0.019984/0.001999 = 9.9970; √9.9970 = 3.1618; ratio = 2.9474/3.1618 = 0.9322; Δθ2 = 0.01 × 0.9322 = 0.0093

Adam ka m remembered direction deta hai, v adaptive scale. θ0 = 0 se: 0 → −0.0100 → −0.0193 (asli PyTorch run bhi yahi deta hai).

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 08 "Adam by hand" (β₁ = β₂ = 0.9)

Sawaal: w1 = 1.0000, m0 = v0 = 0, α = 0.1, β1 = β2 = 0.9 (sheet ne 0.9 isliye liya taaki do steps me correction ka kaam dikhe), gradients 3 phir 4.

  1. Step 1, dono averages: m1 = 0.9(0) + 0.1(3) = 0.3000 (direction, bahut chhota), v1 = 0.9(0) + 0.1(9.0000) = 0.9000 (size, ye bhi chhota)
  2. Correct: 1 − 0.91 = 0.1000 → m̂1 = 0.3000/0.1000 = 3.0000 (= g1), v̂1 = 0.9000/0.1000 = 9.0000 (= g12)
  3. Step: √9.0000 = 3.0000, Δw = 0.1 × 3.0000/3.0000 = 0.1000, w1 = 0.9000
  4. Step 2: m2 = 0.9(0.3000) + 0.1(4) = 0.2700 + 0.4000 = 0.6700, v2 = 0.9(0.9000) + 0.1(16.0000) = 0.8100 + 1.6000 = 2.4100
  5. Correction factor ab: 1 − 0.92 = 0.1900 → m̂2 = 0.6700/0.1900 = 3.5263, v̂2 = 2.4100/0.1900 = 12.6842
  6. √12.6842 = 3.5615, Δw = 0.1(3.5263)/3.5615 = 0.0990, w2 = 0.9000 − 0.0990 = 0.8010
  7. Bina correction (line 3 hata do): step 1 = 0.1(0.3000)/√0.9000 = 0.03/0.9487 = 0.0316, step 2 = 0.1(0.6700)/√2.4100 = 0.067/1.5524 = 0.0432 → w = 0.9252.
step 1step 2w after
w₁ (Adam)0.10000.09900.8010
w₂ (Adam, gradients 0.3, 0.4)0.10000.09900.8010
w₁, correction off0.03160.04320.9252

Adam: 1.0000 → 0.9000 → 0.8010. Plain SGD gradient 4 pe 0.4000 chalta; Adam sirf 0.0990 — kyunki 4 "is parameter ke liye usual" hai, aur v ye jaanta hai. Correction off wala run 2 steps me sirf 0.0748 chala.

Sabse important insight: pehla step = α × sign(g)

t = 1:   m̂1 = (1 − β1)g11 − β1 = g1,   v̂1 = (1 − β2)g121 − β2 = g12  ⇒  m̂1√v̂1 = g1|g1| = ±1
  • Dono betas cancel, gradient ka size bhi cancel. Pehla step exactly α · sign(g1), gradient 0.001 ho ya 1000 (ε ignore karke).
  • Compare: RMSProp ka pehla step α/√(1 − β2) tha (β₂ pe depend). AdaGrad ka bhi pehla step α tha.
  • Aage bhi m̂/√v̂ aksar ±1 ke aas-paas → Adam ka har step lagbhag α size ka. Isi liye lr = 0.001 ka matlab hai "har weight ek step me ~0.001 hilega".

Teacher ka one-liner: "A step is not big because the gradient is big. It is big when the gradient is bigger than usual for this parameter." Parameter A ke gradients aam taur pe ~100, B ke ~0.01; dono apne usual size ka gradient report karein to dono ~α chalenge. Lab 7 saddle point pe Adam isi wajah se nikal bhaagta hai: w1 ka gradient sirf −0.01 tha, par Adam ne use normalize karke poora ~α (0.2) ka kadam diya, jabki SGD ne 0.1 × 0.01 = 0.001 ka.

Bias correction kyun zaroori hai — bina uske numbers

Uncorrected Adam ka step, steady gradient pe, sahi step ka (1 − β1t)/√(1 − β2t) guna hota hai (gradient cancel, sirf betas ki property). Default betas pe pehla step: 0.1/√0.001 = 0.1/0.0316 = 3.16 × α.

β₂ (β₁ = 0.9)uncorrected step 1sabse zyada galat5% ke andar kab se
0.90.32 ×0.32 × (step 1)step 23
0.991.00 ×2.13 × (step 13)step 237
0.999 (default)3.16 ×6.57 × (step 12)step 2375

Default β₂ = 0.999 pe uncorrected Adam 6.6 guna tak bade steps leta, aur step 2374 tak 5% se zyada galat rehta. Do divisions sab theek kar dete hain. Agar sirf m correct karo aur v nahi: t = 1 pe √v1 = √0.001·|g| = 0.0316|g| → step = α/0.0316 ≈ 31.6α — dhamaka! Dono correct karna zaroori.

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Adam on f(θ) = θ² (defaults, lr = 0.1)

θ0 = 1, gradient 2θ, β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.999.

  1. t = 1: g = 2, m = 0.2, v = 0.004, m̂ = 0.2/0.1 = 2, v̂ = 0.004/0.001 = 4, step = 0.1 × 2/2 = 0.1 → θ = 0.9
  2. t = 2: g = 1.8, m = 0.18 + 0.18 = 0.36, v = 0.003996 + 0.00324 = 0.007236; m̂ = 0.36/0.19 = 1.8947, v̂ = 0.007236/0.001999 = 3.6198, √v̂ = 1.9026; step = 0.1 × 0.9959 = 0.0996 → θ = 0.8004
  3. t = 3: g = 1.6008, m = 0.4841, v = 0.009791; m̂ = 0.4841/0.271 = 1.7863, v̂ = 0.009791/0.002997 = 3.2671, √ = 1.8075; step = 0.1 × 0.9883 = 0.0988 → θ = 0.7016

θ: 1 → 0.9000 → 0.8004 → 0.7016 → 0.6039 (4th). Har step ~0.1 = lr, gradient chahe 2 se 1.4 tak gira.

PyTorch · optim.Adam — Worksheet 06 aur 08 dono

import torch
import torch.optim as optim

# Worksheet 08: betas = (0.9, 0.9), lr = 0.1
w = torch.tensor([1.0, 1.0], requires_grad=True)
optimizer = optim.Adam([w], lr=0.1, betas=(0.9, 0.9))
for g in [[3.0, 0.3], [4.0, 0.4]]:
    w.grad = torch.tensor(g)
    optimizer.step()
    print([round(v, 4) for v in w.tolist()])

# Worksheet 06: default betas (0.9, 0.999), lr = 0.01
theta = torch.tensor([0.0], requires_grad=True)
optimizer = optim.Adam([theta], lr=0.01)
for g in [4.0, 2.0]:
    theta.grad = torch.tensor([g])
    optimizer.step()
    print(round(theta.item(), 4))
print(optimizer.state[theta])        # andar kya store hai?

Output (asli PyTorch run)

[0.9, 0.9]
[0.801, 0.801]
-0.01
-0.0193
{'step': tensor(2.), 'exp_avg': tensor([0.5600]), 'exp_avg_sq': tensor([0.0200])}

State me exp_avg = m2 = 0.56 aur exp_avg_sq = v2 = 0.019984 (display me 0.0200) — bilkul worksheet ke numbers. Har parameter ke liye do extra numbers → Adam ko SGD se do extra copies of the parameters jitni memory chahiye (momentum ko ek).

  • optim.Adam(params, lr=0.001, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-08, weight_decay=0, amsgrad=False)
  • betas ek tuple hai: (β₁, β₂). weight_decay Adam me gradient me λw jodta hai (L2 style — 17.5 me iski problem). amsgrad=True → AMSGrad variant (v yaani exp_avg_sq ka running max use karta hai, taaki denominator kabhi chhota na ho).

Fayde: tez, robust, kam tuning (lr = 1e-3 aksar chal jaata hai), noisy/sparse gradients aur saddle points pe accha, har parameter ka apna scale. Isi liye "default first choice". Nuksaan: 2× extra memory; kabhi-kabhi well-tuned SGD+momentum se worse generalization (Lab 7 cheat-sheet); simple convex problems pe zaroori nahi ki jeete (17.8); L2 weight decay ke saath gadbad → AdamW.

Exam Radar

  • Adam = Adaptive Moment Estimation, Kingma & Ba 2014 (ICLR 2015) = Momentum (1st moment) + RMSProp (2nd moment) + bias correction.
  • Defaults: lr 0.001, β₁ 0.9, β₂ 0.999, ε 1e-8. β₂ > β₁.
  • Signed direction state = mt; scale state vt ≥ 0.
  • Bias correction: m̂ = m/(1 − β₁t), v̂ = v/(1 − β₂t); needed because m0 = v0 = 0; matters early, vanishes later.
  • First Adam step = α · sign(g) (magnitude exactly α). Memory: 2 states per parameter.

Galti mat karna

  • Adam ka vt = squared gradients ka average; Chapter 16 ka vt = velocity. Same letter, alag cheez!
  • Bias correction me exponent t = step count (1, 2, 3 ...), epoch nahi.
  • ε denominator me √v̂ ke baad judta hai (PyTorch: √v̂ + ε).
  • betas=0.9 galat; betas=(0.9, 0.999) sahi (tuple).

17.5 AdamW — weight decay ko alag rakho (decoupled)

Kahani

Cycle chalate waqt do alag controls hain: handle (manzil ki taraf steering) aur lane ke beech me rehna (drift na karna). Agar dono ek hi lever se ho, to tez mod pe lane-control bhi utna hi ghoom jaayega. AdamW dono ko alag rakhta hai — adaptive steering (Adam) alag, weights ko zero ki taraf kheenchna (decay) alag. (Worksheet 06 ki analogy.)

Weight decay / L2 regularization (Chapter 19) ka kaam: weights ko chhota rakhna (overfitting kam). Plain SGD me "loss me λw2/2 jodo" aur "har step weight ko (1 − αλ) se shrink karo" — ek hi cheez hain. Adam me nahi!

  • Adam + L2 (optim.Adam(..., weight_decay=λ)): gradient ban jaata hai g + λw, aur ye poora m, v me jaata hai → decay wala hissa bhi √v̂ se divide ho jaata hai. Jis weight ke gradients bade the (bada √v̂), uska decay bahut kam; jiske chhote the, uska zyada. Regularisation worksheet (L8 Part 2) ka jawab: "Adam rescales the penalty along with the gradient, so equal weights shrink unequally."
  • AdamW (Loshchilov & Hutter, "Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization", 2017; ICLR 2019): Adam step sirf data gradient se, aur decay seedha weight pe, alag se.
θt+1 = (1 − αλ)·θt − α·m̂t√v̂t + ε  =  θt − α( m̂t√v̂t + ε + λθt )
  • (1 − αλ)θt = decay term: parameter ko khud shrink karta hai, adaptive scale se bilkul independent.
  • αm̂/(√v̂ + ε) = adaptive term: normal Adam move; m̂, v̂ sirf loss ke gradient se bane (λθ unme nahi gaya).
  • λ = weight decay coefficient (PyTorch AdamW default 0.01).

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Worksheet 06 AdamW ladder

Sawaal: θt = 1.00, α = 0.01, λ = 0.1, normalised Adam direction m̂/√v̂ = 0.50. Decay pehle, adaptive move baad me.

  1. Decay-only: (1 − αλ)θt = (1 − 0.01 × 0.1)(1) = (1 − 0.001)(1) = 0.999
  2. Adaptive move: α(0.50) = 0.01 × 0.50 = 0.005
  3. Combine: θt+1 = 0.999 − 0.005 = 0.994
  4. Direction check: agar normalised direction negative hoti, to −α(negative) θ ko upar le jaata; phir bhi decay term θ ko zero ki taraf hi kheenchta.

θ: 1.00 → 0.994 (0.001 decay se, 0.005 Adam move se).

Chalo numbers se samjhein — Adam + L2 me decay "gayab" (asli PyTorch, ek step)

θ = 1.0, gradient 4, lr 0.01, λ = 0.1, pehla step.

  1. AdamW(lr=0.01, weight_decay=0.1): decay 1.0 × (1 − 0.001) = 0.999, phir Adam ka pehla step exactly lr: 0.999 − 0.01 = 0.989
  2. Adam(lr=0.01, weight_decay=0.1): gradient 4 + 0.1 × 1.0 = 4.1 → pehla Adam step = lr × sign = 0.01 → 1.0 − 0.01 = 0.990. Decay ka koi asar hi nahi dikha — normalization ne use nigal liya!
  3. Lambi training me (rough estimate): Adam+L2 me decay hissa ≈ αλθ/√v̂. √v̂ = 10 wale weight ka decay ≈ 0.01 × 0.1/10 = 0.0001; √v̂ = 0.1 wale ka ≈ 0.01 — 100 guna farak. AdamW me dono ka exactly αλθ = 0.001.

AdamW: 0.989, Adam+L2: 0.990 (asli PyTorch outputs). AdamW ka regularization har weight pe barabar aur predictable.

PyTorch · L2 vs true weight decay (Regularisation worksheet ki do lines)

# L2 penalty gradient ke andar (Adam ise bhi rescale kar deta hai)
optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

# true (decoupled) weight decay
optimizer = optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-2)
# AdamW signature: optim.AdamW(params, lr=0.001, betas=(0.9, 0.999), eps=1e-08, weight_decay=0.01)
# Naye PyTorch me optim.Adam(..., weight_decay=λ, decoupled_weight_decay=True) bhi AdamW jaisa hi hai

AdamW better kyun? (1) Regularization strength sab weights pe barabar, gradient history pe depend nahi; (2) λ aur lr ka tuning zyada independent ho jaata hai; (3) practice me better generalization — isi liye BERT/GPT jaise transformers ka standard optimizer AdamW hai.

Exam Radar

  • AdamW decouples weight decay from the adaptive (gradient-based) update. Loshchilov & Hutter (2017/2019).
  • Adam's weight_decay = L2 inside gradient (rescaled by √v̂); AdamW's = true weight decay.
  • Defaults: Adam weight_decay = 0; AdamW weight_decay = 0.01.
  • Rule: θ ← (1 − αλ)θ − αm̂/(√v̂ + ε).
